3.14.1.6.7 (01-01-2026)

Erroneous Refunds

  1. An Erroneous Refund (ERRF) is defined as "any receipt of money from the IRS to which the recipient is not entitled" . IRM 21.4.5 , Erroneous Refunds, if the foremost authority on Erroneous Refund processing.

  2. Erroneous refunds can be a full refund or only part of a refund.

  3. In the Notice Review Function, erroneous refunds can result from:

    • Errors found on cases where the taxpayer has received a refund as a Split Refund, Form 8888, Allocation of Refund. These refunds do not apply the systemic refund hold (55555 in the blocking series),

    • Errors found on cases reviewed after the deadline for preventing a refund from generating for the cycle, or

    • Errors on notices not subject to the systemic refund hold (55555 in the blocking series) such as CP 16 and CP 51B.

  4. If a duplicate refund is present, i.e., TC 840 (manual refund) and TC 846 (systemic refund) treat the TC 840 as the erroneous refund.

  5. When an erroneous refund is identified, determine the correct erroneous refund category to correctly process the case. There are four categories of IMF erroneous refunds. See the table below for more information.

    Erroneous Refund Category Description
    "A1"

    • A category A1 erroneous refund occurs when the tax liability has been reduced below the correct amount, due to an error on either a tax assessment, or on an adjustment to the tax liability, and the error results in a refund.

    • This category applies when the IRS lowered the tax during processing of the original return or an incorrect tax assessment/adjustment (ADJ47 or ADJ54).
    "A2"

    • A category A2 erroneous refund involves errors on refundable or non-refundable credits that are subject to deficiency procedures.

    • This category applies when the taxpayer or the IRS has erroneously increased refundable or non-refundable credits, and the refund is issued before the error is identified.

    Caution:

    Withholding and estimated tax payment erroneous refunds are not included in this category.
    "B"

    • A category B erroneous refund involves Federal Income Tax Withheld (withholding) overstated by the taxpayer on a return or claim for refund, and as a result, a refund, offset, or credit elect generated.

    • The withholding must be reversed (adjusted).

    • If the IRS caused the overstatement of withholding or estimated tax payments, the erroneous refund becomes a Category D erroneous refund and can only be recovered through the Category D process, see below.

    Note:

    This ERRF category does not apply to Excess Social Security Tax Withheld [Excess Federal Insurance Contributions Act (FICA)]

    .
    "D"

    • A category D erroneous refund includes any erroneous refund not included in any other ERRF category.

    • Misapplied payments.

    • IRS caused overstatement of withholding or estimated tax payments.

    • Entity errors that caused a refund to be paid to wrong taxpayer.

    • Duplicate refunds issued (i.e., TC 840 and TC 846) for same overpayment.

    • Refunds issued after the refund statute expiration date (RSED).

  6. For detailed procedures on classifying and processing erroneous refunds, see IRM 21.4.5, Erroneous Refunds. It is mandatory to use the IAT Erroneous Refund Tool for all ERRF.

  7. Erroneous refund procedures are not necessary in the following situations:

    1. An erroneous refund in Category A1 or A2 that is ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡

    2. Missing signature(s).

      Note:

      It is still necessary to attempt to obtain the missing signature(s). Adhere to the 45-day correspondence timeline. See IRM 3.14.1.7.4, Notice Review Sent Taxpayer Correspondence-Reply and No Reply Procedures, for more information.

    3. A Credit Elect request to the next year was not processed, and instead the credit refunded.

    4. No Computer Condition Code (CCC)"L" or "W" present on a decedent account.

    5. No Form 1310, Statement of Person Claiming Refund Due a Deceased Taxpayer, or court appointment documentation is present for a decedent tax return.

    6. An error found in Notice Review (including errors made during initial processing) results in a tax increase with a prior tax increase from the taxpayer's figures.

    7. An error found in Notice Review (including errors made during initial processing) results in a refundable credit (except withholding) decrease with a prior refundable credit decrease from the taxpayer's figures.

    8. Scenario (f) and (g) are identified as "turnaround" cases and should be adjusted by REQ54 / ADJ54 using Blocking Series "77” or “78" as appropriate, Source Code "6" , and Hold Code "0" . Apply Label 1 in OLNR in the current cycle. Input of the REQ54/ADJ54 adjustment with blocking series 77 or 78 will provide appeal rights to the taxpayer. See IRM 3.14.1.7.6, Tax Adjustments for more information.

  8. If a return with an erroneous refund also requires reprocessing, Accounts Management will input all IDRS actions. Follow the steps below for Notice Review actions and routing:

    1. Order the paper return, if the return is not in Notice Review, using Form 2275, Records Request, Charge and Recharge.

    2. Recharge the paper return using CC ESTABDT (see IRM 2.3.17-1, Input Format, CC ESTAB—Document Request, for more information) to Accounts Management.

    3. For a MeF return, print TXMODA and the first page of ENMOD or INOLES.

    4. Route the ERRF reprocessing case paper return or MeF account prints to Accounts Management for corrective action. See IRM 3.14.1.6.7 (9) below for completion of the Form 3465, Adjustment Request, fields.

    5. Void the notice in OLNR; leave a void history item using CC ACTON in IDRS.

  9. Complete Form 3465, Adjustment Request, fields as stated below and staple to the front of a paper return below the entity or to the front of the IDRS prints for a MeF return.

    1. Classification: choose Non-TPI.

    2. Original DLN: enter the DLN of the tax return.

    3. Taxpayer’s Name or Name Control: enter the full name of the correct primary taxpayer.

    4. Renumbered Refile DLN: leave blank.

    5. Routing: choose Accounts Management.

    6. EIN or SSN: enter the correct TIN for the primary taxpayer.

    7. MFT Code: always MFT 30 for IMF tax returns.

    8. Period ending: enter the correct tax period in YYYYMM format (e.g., 202512).

    9. Form No.: enter 1040.

    10. Cycle No: enter Notice Review cycle number (e.g., 202614).

    11. Document attached: leave blank.

    12. Action requested: do not select any boxes instead, go to Other adjustment and enter "ERRF Reprocess" .

    13. Remarks: enter "Routing due to Erroneous Refund - Reprocess also Needed" . Explain specifically why the refund is erroneous and what category of ERRF applies. State specifically why the tax return needs to be reprocessed including where it originally posted (year, tax period, etc) and to where it needs to be reprocessed.

    14. Signature of Requestor: enter signature not SEID.

    15. Unit: enter Notice Review and 10-digit IDRS number.

    16. Phone ext.: enter email address; unless a desk phone is present, then enter the desk phone number.

    17. Date: Enter current date.

    Note:

    Once the Form 3465 is complete and the package ready, give to the lead for routing to Accounts Management.

3.14.1.6.7.1 (01-01-2026)
Category A1 ERRF Resolution

  1. A Category A1 Erroneous Refund (CAT A1 ERRF) occurs when the tax liability has been reduced below the correct amount, due to an IRS error on either a tax assessment, or on an adjustment to the tax liability, and the error results in a refund that is issued before the error is identified.

  2. Research the case and ensure that the refund cannot be intercepted or any offsets brought back.

  3. Once the determination is made the account has a CAT A1 ERRF :

    1. Navigate to CC TXMODA in IDRS.

    2. Open the mandated IAT Erroneous Refund Tool.

    3. Ensure the TIN, MFT, and Tax Period are populated for the notice taxpayer and click the icon of an IDRS screen (research) to activate the tool.

    4. Choose the radio button next to CAT A1.

      Note:

      Do not refer a Category A1 erroneous refund case to Exam when the erroneous refund amount is under ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡. However, always input the appropriate TC 971 AC 663 for all Erroneous Refunds, regardless of amount.

    5. Complete Form 5101, Examination Referral Slip, only if routing to Exam per the note above. See below for detailed Form 5101 completion instructions.

    6. Input TC 971 AC 663 using CC REQ77, response screen FRM77. See IRM 21.4.5-1, TC 971 AC 663 - Identifying Erroneous Refunds, for input fields.

  4. Form 5101, Examination Referral Slip, is required to route CAT A1 ERRF to Exam. Complete only the fields listed below.

    1. TIN: notice primary taxpayer with CAT A1 ERRF,

    2. Other: state "CAT A1 ERRF" include a detailed explanation of why it is an erroneous refund, the necessary adjustment including Transaction Codes.

    3. Attach the following behind Form 5101, ENMOD (first page), TXMODA, and MeF and/or IDRS screen shots of the processing error (or line) that caused the ERRF condition. If the documentation is not included the case will be rejected by Exam.

      Caution:

      Notice Review does not input adjustments for CAT A1 ERRF. Exam inputs any necessary adjustments.

  5. Give the Form 5101 package to the lead for routing to Exam.

  6. Apply Label 15 ( IRM 3.14.1.7.8.5.17) or 16 ( IRM 3.14.1.7.8.5.18) in OLNR as appropriate.

3.14.1.6.7.2 (01-01-2026)
Category A2 ERRF Resolution

  1. A Category A2 Erroneous Refund (CAT A2 ERRF) occurs when refundable or non-refundable credits are increased in error, and the error results in a refund that is issued before the error is identified.

    • This category applies when the taxpayer or the IRS has erroneously increased refundable or non-refundable credits.

    Caution:

    Withholding and Estimated Tax Payment Erroneous Refunds are not included in this category.

  2. Research the case and ensure that the refund cannot be intercepted or any offsets brought back.

  3. Once the determination is made the account has a CAT A2 ERRF:

    1. Navigate to CC TXMODA in IDRS.

    2. Open the mandated IAT Erroneous Refund Tool.

    3. Ensure the TIN, MFT, and Tax Period are populated for the notice taxpayer and click the icon of an IDRS screen (research) to activate the tool.

    4. Choose the radio button next to Cat A2.

      Note:

      Do not refer a Category A2 erroneous refund case to Exam when the erroneous refund amount is under ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡. However, always input the appropriate TC 971 AC 663 for all Erroneous Refunds, regardless of amount.

    5. Complete Form 5101, Examination Referral Slip, only if routing to Exam per the note above. See below for detailed Form 5101 completion instructions.

    6. Input TC 971 AC 663 using CC REQ77, response screen FRM77. See IRM 21.4.5-1, TC 971 AC 663 - Identifying Erroneous Refunds, for input fields.

  4. Form 5101, Examination Referral Slip is required to route CAT A2 ERRF to Exam. Complete only the fields listed below:

    1. TIN: notice primary taxpayer with CAT A2 ERRF,

    2. Other: state "CAT A2 ERRF" include a detailed explanation of why it is an erroneous refund, the adjustment needed including Transaction Codes, Credit Reference Numbers, Item Reference Numbers, and

    3. Attach the following behind Form 5101, ENMOD (first page), TXMODA, and MeF and/or IDRS screen shots of the processing error(s) (or line) that caused the ERRF condition. If the documentation is not included the case will be rejected by Exam.

      Caution:

      Notice Review does not input adjustments for CAT A2 ERRF. Exam inputs any necessary adjustments.

  5. Give the Form 5101 package to the lead for routing to Exam.

  6. Apply Label 15 ( IRM 3.14.1.7.8.5.17) or 16 ( IRM 3.14.1.7.8.5.18) in OLNR as appropriate.

3.14.1.6.7.3 (01-01-2026)
Category B ERRF Resolution

  1. Category B Erroneous Refunds (CAT B ERRF) occur when taxpayers overstate their Federal income tax withholding credits or Estimated Tax Payments on a return or a claim for refund.

    Caution:

    If the IRS caused the overstatement of withholding or estimated tax payments, the erroneous refund becomes a Category D ERRF and can only be recovered through the Category D procedures (IRM 3.14.1.6.7.4).

  2. Per the Office of Chief Counsel, input an assessment to reverse Federal withholding overstated on a return or a claim for refund by the taxpayer.

    Reminder:

    These instructions do not apply to overstatements of Excess Social Security Tax Withheld (Excess FICA), which should be resolved using Category D procedures (IRM 3.14.1.6.7.4).

  3. Standard TC 807 withholding reversals on CC REQ54 do not post to the Summary Record of Assessment. To correct any taxpayer overstated withholding (whether the refund is erroneous or can be intercepted), an IRC 6201(a)(3) assessment must be input to "reverse" the withholding in a way that is becomes part of the Summary Record of Assessment. A Summary Record Assessment is done utilizing a charge with a TC 290 increase as opposed to decreasing a credit with a TC 807.

  4. An IRC 6201(a)(3) assessment protects the IRS' ability to collect, satisfies the requirement of denying a refund claim, and places burden of proof upon the taxpayer, should a case develop in Tax Court.

  5. ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡≡ ≡

  6. Input a TC 971 AC 663 only if the Category B Erroneous Refund is a true erroneous refund and cannot be intercepted. See IRM 21.4.5-1, TC 971 AC 663 - Identifying Erroneous Refunds, for input information.

  7. Use CC REQ54, response screen ADJ54, to input an IRC 6201(a)(3) assessment to recover the overstated portion of Federal income tax withheld. The bullets below are for an Erroneous Refund adjustment input. If the refund can be intercepted but still meets IRC 6201 (a)(3) criteria, see the Caution below the bullets.

    Note:

    Do not include any other adjustment items in the IRC 6201(a)(3) adjustment. The IAT Erroneous Refund Tool seems to indicate a need for a Credit Reference Number, this is not accurate. If other items need to be adjusted in the tax account, input a separate REQ54 / ADJ54 adjustment per normal procedures outlined in IRM 3.14.1.7.6, Tax Adjustments.

    • Blocking Series 00, if paper return is in Notice Review or Blocking Series 05, if no return / MeF return.

    • Use Category Code ERRF not OURV (see Caution below).

    • In the Activity field of CC ADJ54, input: "W/H–6201A3."

    • Input TC 290 for the amount of overstated withholding being recovered (e.g., TC 290 5,000.00).

    • Source Code 2.

    • Reason Code 051 (Withholding).

    • Hold Code 0 (See Caution below).

      Caution:

      Counsel has advised if a refund claim is pending (the taxpayer has included the overstated amount in their claimed refund), an assessment using a TC 290 must be used to recover the overstated credit. This is true even if the IRS (Notice Review) can prevent the refund from generating, (i.e., the error is identified and the refund is prevented from being issued). In this situation, follow the above procedures; however, use Category Code RFDL, Hold Code "3" , retype the withholding on the notice to the allowed amount, and include TPNC 582. Do not use a Label 15 or 16.

    • In the Remarks field of CC ADJ54, input: "IRC 6201A3 assessment to reverse overstated withholding" .

    • Source Document N (no), unless Blocking Series above was 00, then use Y for yes.

    • Apply Label 15 ( IRM 3.14.1.7.8.5.17) or 16 ( IRM 3.14.1.7.8.5.18) in OLNR as appropriate.

    • Do not use Item Reference Code 807.

3.14.1.6.7.4 (01-01-2026)
Category D ERRF Resolution

  1. Category D Erroneous Refunds (CAT D ERRF) include any erroneous refund that is not included in any other erroneous refund category. See IRM 21.4.5.5.5, Overview of Category D Erroneous Refunds, for more information. Some examples of CAT D ERRF are:

    Note:

    This is not an all-inclusive list.

    • Misapplied Payments.

    • A taxpayer receives a manual refund (TC 840) and a systemic refund (TC 846).

    • Overstatements of Excess Social Security Tax Withheld (Excess FICA).

    • IRS caused overstatement of withholding or estimated tax payments.

  2. Once research is performed and a CAT D ERRF is verified, take all steps to correct the account. The taxpayer must be put into balance due before the erroneous refund can be processed and routed to the Accounting Function.

    • Input all applicable credit transfers, adjustments, and entity changes prior to routing the case.

    • Use TC 570 on the debit side of any credit transfers.

    • If removing a timely credit will create FTF or ES Tax penalty assessments, input a TC 290 .00 with Hold Code 3, to suppress an adjustment notice.

  3. Below are erroneous refund actions required on nearly every CAT D ERRF case. See the exceptions below and IRM 21.4.5.6.1, Account Actions For Category D Erroneous Refunds, for more information. Use of the IAT tool is required to process the CAT D ERRF.

    • A TC 470 Closing Code (CC) 93 is required on all CAT D ERRF cases. This can be input with the IAT Erroneous Refund Tool per the instructions below. This will stop all collection notices and processes. To input manually: use REQ77 / FRM 77, input 470 in the TC field, posting delay code 1, closing code 93, and remarks, NSD CAT D ERRF. See IRM 2.4.19-2, Command Code REQ77 Response, for more information.

    • If a TC 844 is required (most CAT D ERRF cases) it must be input manually in IDRS stating the correct date of demand. The TC 844 generates a - U freeze on the account which is an erroneous refund freeze across the entire account not just one module For TC 844 input format see IRM 3.14.1.6.7.4 (4) below.

      Exception:

      If the erroneous refund date is a future date, request on the Form 12356, Erroneous Refund worksheet, that a TC 844 be input by the Accounting Function upon receipt of the case.

    • TC 971 AC 663 is required on all erroneous refund cases and the IAT Erroneous Refund Tool will input the transaction on Cat D ERRF only. See IRM 21.4.5-1, TC 971 AC 663 - Identifying Erroneous Refunds, for input information.

    • Send the taxpayer a Letter 510C, Refund In Error; Return Check, Refund in Error; Return Check, using the IAT Erroneous Refund Tool or IAT Letters Tool. This is the method used by the IRS to "demand " the erroneous refund be repaid. The input date of the letter (current date) is considered the date of demand. See IRM 21.4.5.14, Interest and Penalty Consideration for Category D Erroneous Refunds, for correct balance information for the 510C (generally if the ERRF amount is under $50,000.00 the interest is calculated from the refund date (date of TC 840/ TC 846) to the notice date). Send the best paragraphs that apply to the situation for the erroneous refund (Example paragraphs: G, P, Z, c, g). For all paragraphs see Correspondex Index.

      Exception:

      If the erroneous refund module contains a bankruptcy indicator (-V freeze), the erroneous refund issue must be addressed by Field Insolvency or Centralized Insolvency Operation (CIO). Refer to IRM 21.5.6.4.44, -V Freeze. Do not request repayment or issue a Letter 510C, Refund in Error; Return Check. Refer the case to CIO in Philadelphia. The lead will fax a completed Form 4442, Inquiry Referral, including case data and reason for routing to ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡. CIO will determine the appropriate action.

  4. TC 844 input for CAT D ERRF using REQ77 / FRM 77:

    1. If the CAT D ERRF is an IRS error or less than $50,000.00, input 844 in the TC field, input Date of Demand (current date) in the EXTENSION-DT field (MMDDYYYY), input the date of the TC 840 or TC 846 that is erroneous in the TRANS-DT field (MMDDYYYY), input the erroneous refund amount in the FREEZE-RELEASE-AMT field (8,000.00), and input NSD CAT D ERRF in the remarks field. See IRM 21.4.5.6.1(7), Account Actions For Category D Erroneous Refunds, and IRM 2.4.19-6, Examples of Command Code FRM77, for more REQ77 / FRM 77 input instructions.

    2. If the CAT D ERRF is a taxpayer error or more than $50,000.00, only input three fields; input 844 in the TC field, input the date of the erroneous refund (TC 840 or TC 846) in the "TRANS-DT" field, and NSD CAT D ERRF. See 2.4.19-6, Examples of Command Code FRM77.

  5. When the taxpayer is in balance due and the necessary ERRF actions have been identified (and manual items input), proceed to the mandated IAT Erroneous Refund Tool.

    1. Start in IDRS at CC TXMODA.

    2. Open the mandated IAT Erroneous Refund Tool. See the IAT Erroneous Refund Tool Job Aid for more information.

    3. Ensure the TIN, MFT, and Tax Period are populated for the notice taxpayer and click the icon of an IDRS screen (research) to activate the tool.

    4. Choose the radio button next to Cat D.

    5. A box will display within the tool showing all TC 840 and 846, posted refunds. Select the TC 840 or 846 that is the CAT D ERRF and select submit.

    6. The tool will research CC TXMOD, auto-populate the demand date and the TC 846 field. These fields can be changed manually if necessary. A box is provided for input of IRS received date (enter *).

    7. The tool will display account actions that it will perform or assist in performing (TC 570, TC 470, TC 290, 510C Letter, complete Form 12356).

    8. TC 971 AC 663 is required on all erroneous refund cases and the Erroneous Refund Tool will input the transaction on Cat D ERRF only. Choose the appropriate drop-down information on the display.

    9. If the CAT D ERRF was caused by a misapplied payment, include the information at the bottom of the tool for TIN, MFT and Tax Period for where the misapplied payment should have posted.

    10. Select Process Cat D ERRF.

      Caution:

      Do not choose Auto Transmit. This will go quickly through the process and not allow a choice of Letter 510C, Refund In Error; Return Check paragraphs or correction of any questionable fields. For 510C paragraphs see the Correspondex Index.

    11. Make sure to choose print anytime possible to aid in building the required ERRF package to send to the Accounting function. Print as pdf is the best option as all packages must be sent electronically.

  6. Once all actions are completed with the IAT tool, ensure you have a completed Form 12356, Erroneous Refund worksheet. See the field descriptions below and IRM 21.4.5.6.2, Preparing Form 12356, Erroneous Refund Worksheet, for more information.

    • Discovering Function: Specific Team - example: TS SP KC Dept. 2 Team 202.

    • Date Discovered: Current Date - all ERRF should be processed the day its identified.

    • Function who created the erroneous refund: The area that caused the erroneous refund. Example: Lockbox for misapplied payment.

    • Campus responsible for collecting erroneous refund: See 7 and 8 below to determine the correct SPC. Input will be Austin, Kansas City or Ogden.

    • ERRF Category: D.

    • Erroneous Refund is: Check the corresponding box for the CAT D erroneous refund type manual (TC 840) or systemic (TC 846).

    • Dated: The IDRS date of the TC 840 or TC 846.

    • ERRF Refund DLN: The IDRS DLN of the TC 840 or TC 846

    • RSN: The Refund Schedule Number found in IDRS posted with the TC 846 or TC 840.

    • ERSED: Check the 2-year box for either TP error or IRS error for erroneous refund statute expiration date (ERSED). Notice Review must route suspected fraud cases per IRM 21.4.5.15.1.1, Statutes of Limitations Category D Erroneous Refunds IRC 6532(b) ERSED.

    • 510 C Date: Current Date - Date of the 510C letter - all ERRF should be processed the day its identified.

    • Date of Demand: Date of the 510C letter.

    • ERRF Amount $: The amount of the TC 840 or TC 846 that is erroneous.

    • TC 470 Date: Date of the TC 470.

    • TC 844 Date: Date of the TC 844.

    • TC 971/663 Date: Date of the TC 971/ AC 663.

    • Identify taxpayer(s) and account(s) involved: Erroneous Refund TP is the location of the ERRF. Enter the TIN, MFT, tax Period, name, and address of the account the erroneous refund was issued from.

    • Identify taxpayer(s) and account(s) involved: X-REF TP, if a misapplied payment, enter the TIN, MFT, tax Period, name, and address of the cross-reference account where the payment belongs.

    • Provide a detailed explanation for the causes of, and the function responsible for, the erroneous refund: Click the appropriate box for the type of CAT D erroneous refund identified.

    • Provide a detailed explanation for the causes of, and the function responsible for, the erroneous refund: Details - Be very specific. Example: The X-REF taxpayer made a payment which clearly stated the posting location including, TIN, MFT, and Tax Period on the check and voucher (can be seen in included RTR screen shot). However, the Lockbox function applied the payment to the wrong taxpayer account; Erroneous Refund TP, shown above. Include all research steps and actions taken.

    • Discovering Employee Information: Include IDRS number, telephone number if applicable, and mail stop number.

    • Date: Current Date

      Note:

      Do not email or take a printed form to the manager for signature. The lead will obtain a signature after review.

  7. Before completing the ERRF package per the instructions below, review IDRS to ensure manual input and IAT Erroneous Refund Tool input of all transactions are correct.

    1. Confirm that all Notice Review IDRS control bases are closed.

    2. Instead, open a control base to the correct Accounting Unit to which the case will be routed: Austin - 0611300000, Kansas City - 0911800000, Ogden - 0411700000. The control base should be input with ACTON as C#,ERROREF,M,ERRF. The second line of ACTON is the appropriate Accounting IDRS number,*. See below for identifying the correct SPC.

  8. Employees who identify a Category D erroneous refund are responsible for creating an erroneous refund package and completing the necessary actions before referring the case to the appropriate Accounting ERRF Unit; the Erroneous Refund IAT tool will determine this data automatically based on the Refund Schedule Number (RSN) of the TC 846. For more information on the RSN see IRM 3.17.79-4 , Refund Schedule Number Format. For example, an erroneous TC 846 refund has an RSN showing 2010046281Z, the 8th and 9th position is 28, so match to the table in IRM 21.4.5.6.3 , Routing Category D Erroneous Refund Packages, to identify the SPC which to route the package. In this case, Ogden.

  9. The ERRF package must include the below information and be merged into one pdf document. The Form 12356 needs to be the first page of the document.

    • Completed and signed Form 12356, including all actions and information.

    • Copy of the 510C letter sent to the taxpayer.

    Note:

    Lead will route the completed and signed Form 12356 ERRF package to the appropriate Accounting Unit, but the identifying tax examiner is responsible for creating the package. Lead, review the package and route via email according to IRM 21.4.5.6.3, Routing Category D Erroneous Refund Packages.

  10. Don’t forget notice disposition; apply Label 15 or 16 in OLNR as appropriate.

    Exception:

    When the erroneous refund is issued on an Adjustment notice, void the notice.

3.14.1.6.8 (03-10-2025)

Excess Collections (XSF) and Unidentified Remittance (URF) Files

  1. When there is not enough information to properly apply credits to a taxpayer’s account (e.g., when a taxpayer does not claim a payment and the correct taxpayer cannot be located), funds may be transferred to the Unidentified Remittance File (URF) or the Excess Collections File (XSF).

    Note:

    TC 820 may indicate that a payment has been moved from the taxpayer’s account to URF or XSF. If the cross-reference TIN and tax period (next to the transfer DLN) are all zeros or nines, the credit was transferred to either the URF or the XSF. If a taxpayer files a return claiming credits that were applied to the URF or XSF, it may be necessary to transfer the credit from the URF or the XSF to the Master File. Use Form 8765, IDRS Control File Credit Application. Figure 3.14.1-3a.

    Caution:

    If the DLN of the payment is for another Submission Processing Campus, send the request to that campus.

    1. Credits less than 12 months old are applied to the Unidentified Remittance File. Credits over 12 months old are applied to Excess Collections. An application to move credits to Unidentified Remittances can be made in the 11th month.

      Exception:

      Credits with Document Codes 48, 58, or 65 may be added to the XSF regardless of age.

    2. Earned Income Credit (TC 764 or TC 768) and Generated Refundable Credit (TC 766) will be accepted by Excess Collections.

  2. For assistance in matters related to XSF and URF, contact lists for Excess Collections and Unidentified Remittance Files are provided in the Who/Where tab of SERP.

3.14.1.6.8.1 (01-01-2026)
Excess Collections File (XSF) — 6800 Account

  1. The XSF consists of two accounts:

    • 6800 Account — Credits over one year old that cannot be applied to a taxpayer's account are transferred to the 6800 Account.

    • 9999 Account — Credits in the 6800 Account are automatically transferred to the 9999 Account after one year.

  2. Before requesting a payment from the XSF determine whether the statute of limitations for refunds has expired. The general rule is that a claim for refund must be filed within three years from the date the original return was filed, even if the return was delinquent, or two years from the date the tax was paid, whichever is later. See the table below for limitations.

    If the claim was filed Then the amount paid within
    Within the three-year period The prior three years, plus any return filing extension period, may be refunded
    Within the two-year period The prior two years may be refunded

    Note:

    Prepaid credits are treated as being paid on the Return Due Date (RDD). These include withholding (TC 806), Estimated Tax payments (TC 660, TC 716, and TC 710), Earned Income Credit (TC 764 and TC 768), and Generated Refundable Credit Allowances (TC 766).

    1. Check the Quarterly Statute Alert Bulletin. More information can be found in IRM 25.6.1.4.2, The Statute Awareness Program.

    2. The remarks section of the CC XSINQ record should indicate "STATUTE" or "FROZ" if the credit is barred from refunding.

    3. If the refund statute (RSED) has expired (found on TXMOD), the application to move credits from XSF must not exceed the tax liability, interest, and penalties. There can be no refund or credit elect.

3.14.1.6.8.1.1 (01-01-2026)
Requesting Payments from the XSF

  1. Use CC XSINQ to verify that the credit is available.

    Note:

    Do not request a transfer of the credit if the remarks section of the CC XSINQ record indicates "CLOS" . These credits are not available for transfer.

  2. Prepare Form 8765, IDRS Control File Credit Application, per instructions. Figure 3.14.1-3a

  3. Attach a current print (less than seven days old) of CC TXMOD or CC IMFOL and CC XSINQ to Part 1 of Form 8765, IDRS Control File Credit Application.

  4. Enter CC STAUPS for eight cycles on balance due accounts to prevent erroneous or unnecessary notices. See IRM 3.14.1.6.24, Command Code STAUPS, for more information.

  5. Determine which campus transferred the original credit to the XSF.

  6. If the original transfer to XSF was local, the lead will route Part 1 of Form 8765, IDRS Control File Credit Application, with research, to the local Statutes function. After Statutes completes their clearing process, they will forward the case to Accounting, per the Statute of Limitations, refer to IRM 25.6.1.7.3.3, Transferring Credits from the XSF.

  7. If the original transfer was done in another campus, route the case to the other campus' Accounting function, per the Statute of Limitations, refer to IRM 25.6.1.7.3.3, Transferring Credits from the XSF.

  8. Attach Part 2 of Form 8765 to the case.

  9. Include a complete explanation for the request.

    Note:

    An IRM reference alone is not a sufficient explanation.

  10. Give the completed form and all necessary attachments to the lead to hand-carry to the Statute Classifier, who will stamp "STATUTE CLEARED" on the form before routing it to the Excess Collections Unit.

3.14.1.6.8.1.2 (01-01-2026)
Transferring Payments to the XSF

  1. Correspond for the missing payment information using Letter 1687C- Unidentified Payment/ Credit. See IRM 3.14.1.7.4, Notice Review Sent Taxpayer Correspondence-Reply and No Reply Procedures, for more information.

  2. If the taxpayer does not reply, or replies with insufficient information, use Form 8758, Excess Collection Files Addition, to apply a credit to the XSF. Form 8758, Excess Collection Files Addition, is a two-part form. Attach the research to part one (the original) Figure 3.14.1-4a .

  3. Use the received date of the credit. Do not use the available date of the credit or the return due date.

  4. Use the original DLN of the credit, not a transfer DLN.

  5. Issue a manual refund when money is transferred out of an account using a Form 8758, Excess Collection Files Addition, paper document and there is still an overpayment to be refunded. Refer to IRM 3.14.1.6.6, Manual Refunds.

  6. Move each payment individually. Do not transfer a lump sum.

  7. The date on Form 8758, Excess Collection Files Addition, and the date of the CC IMFOLT or CC TXMOD print must be no more than seven days prior to receipt of the case in the Excess Collections Function.

  8. Both copies of Form 8758, Excess Collection Files Addition, must be complete and identical. Route both copies to the Excess Collections Function.

  9. Attach the following to the original copy: a current CC IMFOLT or CC TXMOD print, a copy of any taxpayer correspondence, tax returns, vouchers, or other research relevant to the transfer to the XSF, and a research history sheet showing the research performed on the case.

    Note:

    Send only copies of original (DLN) documents. Do not send original "live" documents.

  10. Use activity code "CLTO6800" to close the IDRS control base.

  11. A TC 971 AC 296 must be input using CC REQ77 to indicate taxpayer contact has been attempted. Input "971" in Field TC>, input "296" in Field TC 971/151-CD>, and input "Credit to Excess Collections" for remarks. Refer to IRM 3.17.220, Excess Collections File.

3.14.1.6.8.2 (01-01-2015)
Unidentified Remittance File (URF) — the 4620 Account

  1. Follow procedures in the subsections that follow when transferring credits to, or from, the 4620 URF account.

3.14.1.6.8.2.1 (01-01-2026)
Requesting Payments from the URF

  1. Use CC URINQ to verify that the credit is available. See SERP Command Code Job Aid for URINQ (Input) and URINQ (Response) for more information.

  2. Follow the instructions on Form 8765, IDRS Control File Credit Application, see Figure 3.14.1-3a for more information.

  3. Attach Form 8765, IDRS Control File Credit Application, to a print of CC URINQ.

  4. Include research as required.

  5. Enter CC STAUPS for eight cycles on balance due accounts to prevent erroneous or unnecessary notices. See IRM 3.14.1.6.24, Command Code STAUPS, for more information.

  6. Lead will route Form 8765, IDRS Control File Credit Application, with research, to the Unidentified Remittance Function.

3.14.1.6.8.2.2 (01-01-2026)
Transferring Payments to the URF

  1. Correspond for the missing payment information using Letter 1687C- Unidentified Payment/Credit.

  2. Issue a manual refund for the substantiated payment(s) when there is still an overpayment amount to be refunded. Refer to IRM 3.14.1.6.6, Manual Refunds.

  3. If the taxpayer does not reply, or replies with insufficient information, use Form 2424, Account Adjustment Voucher to apply a payment to the URF. Form 2424 is a two-part form: the "pink" copy is the original, and the "blue" copy is the duplicate. While this form is no longer printed on paper of color, the electronic Form 2424 , Account Adjustment Voucher, is notated with pink and blue to identify the duplicate. Attach the research to the pink copy. See Figure 3.14.1-5.

  4. Use the received date of the credit. Do not use the available date of the credit or the Return Due Date.

  5. Use the original DLN of the credit, not a transfer DLN.

  6. Include the payment DLN, the tracer ID, and the reason for the transfer to the URF in the “Remarks” section.

    Note:

    An IRM reference alone is not a sufficient explanation.

  7. The date on Form 2424 , Account Adjustment Voucher, and the date of the CC IMFOLT or TXMOD print must be no more than seven days prior to receipt of the case in the Unidentified Remittance Function.

  8. Both the pink and blue copies of the Form 2424, Account Adjustment Voucher, must be completed and sent to the Unidentified Remittance Unit. The blue copy must be legible and match the original pink copy.

  9. Attach the following to the original (pink) copy: a current CC IMFOLT or TXMOD print, a copy of any taxpayer correspondence, tax returns, vouchers, or other research relevant to the transfer to the URF, a research history sheet (except on Statute credits) showing the research performed on the case and the results, and a copy of the check.

    Note:

    Send only copies of original (DLN) documents. Do not send original ("live" ) documents.

3.14.1.6.9 (01-01-2026)

Special Notice Review Issues

  1. This subsection contains instructions related to miscellaneous issues. These issues include:

    • Taxpayer Correspondence

    • Taxpayers Meeting Taxpayer Advocate Service (TAS) Criteria

    • $10,000,000 (Ten Million Dollar) Refunds

    • Frivolous Claims

    • RIVO (Return Integrity and Verification Operation)

    • Initial Allegation or Suspicion of Tax-Related Identity Theft Indicators

    • Slipped Blocks and Mixed Data Blocks

    • Community Property Allocation

    • Injured Spouse Allocation

    • Natural Disaster Procedures

    • Combat Zone or -C Freeze Returns

    • Large Dollar Review

    • Premium Tax Credit (PTC)

    • 8962 PTC Calculator Tool

    • ACA Shared Responsibility Payment (SRP)

    • Tax Reform Act of 2017

    • IRC Section 965 - Transition Tax on Untaxed Foreign Earnings

    • Qualified Business Income Deduction (QBID)

    • Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) of 2022 (including EPE)

    • Prisoner Returns

3.14.1.6.9.1 (01-01-2026)
Taxpayer Correspondence

  1. If taxpayer correspondence is discovered attached to the return, review, analyze, and determine disposition as necessary. Follow Policy Statement -21-3 requirements (noted below (2) to initiate a response. Follow the table below for actions regarding correspondence attached to the return.

    If the taxpayer And there is Then
    Requests installment payments or indicates an inability to pay No indication that Code and Edit has forwarded the letter to the Collection Function

    1. Verify that the taxpayer’s SSN and address are on the letter

    2. Send the letter to the Collection Function

    3. Input CC STAUPS for eight cycles on balance due notices. See IRM 3.14.1.6.24, Command Code STAUPS, for more information.

    4. Input CC REQ77 with TC 971 AC 043

      Note:

      For Electronic Filed Returns

      MeF sends all Form 9465, Installment Agreement Request, data to Compliance in a separate file. Form 9465, Installment Agreement Request, attached to electronic returns are routed through MeF. Do not print and send to Collections.
    Inquires about an account An open control base Route the original letter to the tax examiner who has the case controlled on IDRS
    Inquires about an account No open control base Route the original letter to Accounts Management.

    Reminder:

    Input CC STAUPS for eight cycles on a balance due module.

    See IRM 3.14.1.6.24, Command Code STAUPS, for more information.
    Requests abatement of a penalty due to Reasonable Cause The request was denied (identifiable by CCC "7" ) Route the request to Accounts Management for correspondence with the taxpayer.

    Note:

    Code and Edit tax examiners assign CCC "7" and send the Appeals letters
    Requests abatement of a penalty due to Reasonable Cause NRPS data does not show CCC "7" or CCC "M" Route the request to Accounts Management for correspondence with the taxpayer.
    Requests acknowledgment of payments and/or documents attached to the return NRPS data does not show CCC 7 or CCC M Route the request to the Receipt and Control Function
    Attached original or certified documents (such as, birth certificates, SSN card, marriage license etc.) NRPS data does not show CCC 7 or CCC M Return them to the taxpayer upon completion of the case, unless the taxpayer indicates that returning them is unnecessary. If the document is needed as a source document, attach a copy to the return. Do not detach death certificates on decedent returns even if original document.
    Attached documents labeled as copy or the taxpayer has indicated returning them is unnecessary NRPS data does not show CCC 7 or CCC M Staple documents to the back of the return or attach completed Form 9856, Attachment Alert, and return to files.
    Has replied to IRS initiated Processing correspondence (Letter 12C - Individual Return Incomplete for Processing: Forms 1040 & 1040-SR,, Form 3531, Request for Signature or Missing Information to Complete Return, Form 6001, Letter 0012C Correspondence Action Sheet (CAS), etc.) No evidence of a Return Processable Date (RPD) on the account

    1. Prevent the refund from generating if it reflects interest

    2. Input RPD with TC 290 with appropriate Hold Code

    3. Issue Manual Refund if necessary to avoid paying interest
    Has not replied to IRS Processing correspondence (no reply stamp on Form 3531, Request for Signature or Missing Information to Complete Return, Form 6001, Letter 0012C Correspondence Action Sheet (CAS), etc.) No I– freeze on account (freeze is set by Computer Condition Code U)

    1. Prevent the refund from generating if it reflects erroneous interest

    2. Verify correct no-reply procedures were followed by ERS/Rejects

    3. Issue manual refund for overpayment without interest
    Was not required to reply (Correspondence was issued in error) An I – freeze on the account Issue manual refund for the appropriate amount of credit interest (TC 770), calculating interest on the initial systemic refund of overpayment principal (TC 846), less the back-off period of IRC 6611 (b)(2). See IRM 20.2.4.8.1, Systemic Refunds, calculating interest on that interest amount to one business day past the CC RFUNDR date (two days for swing shift)
    Attaches Form W-7, or Form W-7A An I – freeze on the account

    1. Make a copy of the return, front and back pages only, and indicate across the copied return that it is a “COPY ONLY”. Line thru the DLN of the copied return. Do not send original returns. If taxpayers attach passports or other original non-tax documents include those with the Form W-7.

    2. Detach the Form W-7 from the original return, make a copy of it and staple the copy to the back of the original return. Notate on the Form W-7 copy that the original was sent to Austin SPC Stop 6090, ITIN and the date it was sent. Staple the original Form W-7 to the front of the copied return.

    3. Route the original Form W-7 and the copied return to: Internal Revenue Service ITIN Operation Mail Stop 6090 - AUSC 3651 S Interstate 35 Austin, TX 78741. Use Document 13011 to determine the correct envelope. Include a Form 3210 , Document Transmittal, and follow correct mail procedures in IRM 1.22.3.8, Requirements for Shipping Personally Identifiable Information (PII). Do not allow exemptions or credits as the Form W-7, Application for IRS Individual Taxpayer Identification Number, has not been processed.

  2. Policy Statement P-21-3 Guidelines are the result of a task force initiated to provide timely, quality responses to taxpayer correspondence. A Quality Response is an accurate and professional communication which based on the information provided:

    • Resolves the taxpayer issues, or

    • Requests additional information from the taxpayer, or

    • Notifies the taxpayer that we have requested information from outside the IRS.

  3. A Quality Response is timely when initiated within 30 days (calendar days) of the IRS Received Date.

  4. When a Quality Response cannot be issued timely, contact headquarters for guidance.

  5. Exceptions to Policy Statement -21-3 Requirements:

    • Substitute returns

    • Amended returns

    • Tentative Carry backs

    • CAF/POA

    • Address Changes

    • Responses to IRS solicitation for information necessary to secure or complete processing of the tax return.

3.14.1.6.9.2 (01-01-2025)
Taxpayer Advocate Service (TAS)

  1. The Taxpayer Advocate Service (TAS) is an independent organization within the IRS, led by the National Taxpayer Advocate, who helps taxpayers and protects taxpayer rights. TAS offers free help to taxpayers when a tax problem is causing a financial difficulty, when they’ve tried and been unable to resolve their issue with the IRS, or when they believe an IRS system, process, or procedure just isn't working as it should. TAS strives to ensure that every taxpayer is treated fairly and knows and understands their rights under the Taxpayer Bill of Rights. TAS has at least one taxpayer advocate office located in every state, the District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico. See IRM 13.1.7, Taxpayer Advocate Service (TAS) Case Criteria if additional information is required.

  2. While the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) is continually working to serve customers in a quality manner, some taxpayers still have difficulty getting solutions to their problems or getting timely and appropriate responses to their inquiries. Per IRC 7803(c), Congress established the office of the National Taxpayer Advocate (NTA) and its functions within the IRS to assist these taxpayers. TAS has identified criteria that qualify taxpayers for TAS assistance. The Case Advocate will conduct an independent review of actions that have been taken or need to be taken to resolve the problems taxpayers are experiencing.

  3. Employees should not view TAS case criteria as a means of excluding taxpayers from TAS, but rather, as a guide to TAS case acceptance. The criteria under which TAS accepts a case should not govern whether a taxpayer is entitled to relief.

3.14.1.6.9.3 (01-01-2026)
$10,000,000 (Ten Million Dollar) Refunds

  1. An account with an overpayment of $10,000,000 or more requires that a manual refund be issued since a TC 846 will not generate. These cases should also have an X- Accounting Manual Refund Freeze. see IRM 3.14.1.6.11.29 for more information.

  2. These cases need to be worked by the lead the same day they are received in the Notice Review Function. See IRM 3.14.1.6.14.2, $10 Million Dollar or more AMS Refund Transcripts.

  3. Use the following procedures for resolving the case before doing a manual refund:

    1. Verify all unclaimed credits.

    2. Offset the overpayment as needed to cover any debit balances.

    3. Abate any interest caused by an overpayment not due the taxpayer.

    4. Monitor the case until all actions post to the Master File.

  4. The account must have a zero balance or be in debit status before closing the control. If another area has an open control on the case, contact that area, route all available documents to that area, and close the Notice Review control base.

    Exception:

    The control base may be closed without a control base or further actions if there is an -L freeze on the module and a Revenue Agent has advised that the credit not be refunded due to legal implications.

  5. If, after any adjustments, the account has a credit balance of less than $10,000,000:

    1. Offset credit to any debit balance modules.

    2. Prepare a manual refund for the excess credit.

    3. Monitor the case until the TC 840 posts.

  6. If, after any adjustments, the account has a credit balance of $10,000,000 or more, and no other areas have an open control base, Notice Review must issue the manual refund. See IRM 3.14.1.6.6, Manual Refunds, for more information.

  7. Close the control base after all account transactions post.

3.14.1.6.9.4 (01-01-2024)
Frivolous Claims

  1. A frivolous argument is used for expressing dissatisfaction with the substance, form, or administration of the tax laws by attempting to illegally avoid or reduce tax liabilities.

  2. A TC 971 AC 089 indicates that a frivolous return has been received, and the entire account is frozen. An F- freeze is generated on all tax periods. Adjustments should not be made to accounts showing an F- freeze.

  3. Currently, one of the most common frivolous claims is the Reparations Tax (also known as the Black Investment Tax). The claim is based on the premise that African-Americans should receive repayment for historical slavery. There is no existing law that allows payment of reparations. Any claim(s) for reparations should be disallowed.

  4. Another example of a frivolous claim is when taxpayers attempt to eliminate their tax liability by removing their income by citing "Less Native American Indian Treaty" or simply "Native American Indian Treaty" . Usually, these filings include Form 1099–MISC, Miscellaneous Information, income and tax withheld (generally higher than 18 percent of earnings) that results in a refund.

  5. Use the following procedures IRM 21.5.3.4.16.7, Identifying Frivolous Returns/Correspondence and Responding to Frivolous Arguments when referring frivolous claims and/or correspondence to the Ogden Campus Frivolous Return Program:
    Ogden Compliance
    1973 N Rulon White Blvd., Mail Stop 4450 OSC
    Ogden, UT 84404
    Attention: Frivolous Return Program.

  6. For additional information and examples, see the table in IRM 3.11.3-13, Frivolous Filer/Non-Filer Review Box Criteria and Definitions, and IRM 4.19.15, Discretionary Programs.

3.14.1.6.9.5 (01-01-2026)
RIVO (Return Integrity and Verification Operation)

  1. Return Integrity & Verification Operations (RIVO) performs revenue protection program review utilizing the Electronic Fraud Detection System (EFDS) to screen and verify the accuracy of wages and withholding reported on paper and electronically filed tax returns. RIVO cases can be identified in IDRS on CC TXMOD by one or more items from the list below. See IRM 21.2.4.3.18, Return Integrity & Verification Operations (RIVO) and Criminal Investigation (CI), Transcript Issues, for more information.

    • A RIVO open control base starting with 148XX for the IDRS unit number,

    • A RIVO P- freeze (See IRM 21.5.6.4.31.2, P- Freezes with Return Integrity Verification Operations (RIVO) Involvement, for more information.),

    • A TC 971 with any of the following Action Codes (AC) 121/122/124/129/134/199/617, or

    • A TC 971 AC 123 with MISC field showing one of the following letters, 4464C, 4883C, 5071C, 5216C, 5447C, 5747C, 6330C, 6331C , has been issued to the taxpayer.

      Caution:

      ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡

  2. If the account contains a math error that needs to be corrected, adjust the account using hold code 4 to prevent a notice from generating and the overpayment from being released in error, before RIVO is done reviewing the case.

  3. RIVO cases may or may not also be identity theft cases. See IRM 3.14.1.6.9.6, Initial Allegation or Suspicion of Tax-Related Identity Theft Indicators, for more information on identifying identity theft cases.

  4. If a questionable refund based on the criteria below IRM 3.14.1.6.9.5 (5), RIVO criteria or IRM 3.14.1.6.9.5 (6)suspected identity theft, is identified, the case should not be referred to RIVO again.

  5. Refer cases that meet potential RIVO Criteria below to the lead, before taking any action. If the case is not returned to the tax examiner timely (by Thursday 10:00 P.M.), prevent the refund from generating.

    • Refund Schemes, Form W-2 is altered, handwritten or a substitute/similar statement

    • Form(s) 4852 attached and no other withholding documentation is present

    • Similarities between Form(s) W-2 on different returns such as: Typing or printing, Wage amounts, Withholding amounts, Employer, Earned Income Credit (EIC) is being claimed and only the attached Form W-2 is altered, handwritten or a substitute/similar statement.

    • IDT/Operation Mass Mailing (OMM) – refund scheme involving bulk filings. Returns are often identical or vary only slightly. Multiple returns with matching characteristics such as: duplicate filing addresses, same writing instruments (matching ink, pencil, color), same/similar handwriting, matching attached envelopes, same paper stock, same amounts entered on similar Form 1040, U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, line entries (including Schedules/Forms), multiple entries ending in zeros, same occupations, large number of returns submitted in a single envelope/box and duplicate bank routing number and account numbers. See IRM 25.25.2.11, Identity theft Scheme Criteria, for more information.

    Reminder:

    Do not send RIVO returns that already have been stamped by (RIVO/AMTAP/QRDT) or returns that have a zero balance or a balance due.

  6. If identity theft is suspected on a notice or refund transcript case, use the following criteria to determine whether the case should be sent to RIVO for consideration. Refer the below cases to the lead, before taking any action. If the case is not returned to the tax examiner timely (by Thursday 10:00 P.M.), prevent the refund from generating.

    Caution:

    This list is not inclusive of all possible criteria. Not all cases will meet all criteria, but a case should have at least 3 of the indictors below to be considered suspect (See Exceptions.).

    1. A drastic change of address from prior year (e.g., a different state)

    2. Children claimed that are not claimed in prior years

    3. The employer changes from prior years (use CC IRPTR)

    4. The filing status changed from prior years

    5. If direct deposit was elected, research the routing/account number using CC TRDBV to determine if the number has changed from prior years. Refund Anticipation Loan (RAL) commonly displays the taxpayer’s SSN as the last nine digits or displays the SSN in reverse order. Refer to IRM 21.4.1.5.7.1, Direct Deposit of Refunds.

    6. Occupation/type of work changed from prior year (e.g., wage earner (W-2) vs. Schedule C filer, etc.)

    7. A drastic change in the refund amount claimed from previous years.

    8. Methods of tax payments changed, or information on the tax module doesn’t match the payment history. Examples of this might include: The taxpayer has made substantial ES payments but claims refundable credits or reports low AGI. The taxpayer has made a payment with extension (TC 670/460) that posts after the return or is inconsistent with the posted TC 150. The taxpayer is requesting a refund and there are estimated tax payments on the module that are not claimed on the return.

      Exception:

      Per RIVO, cases may be routed on this criteria alone.

    9. Income type changed (e.g., Investment to employment). Returns that have employment income but the account history indicates the taxpayer has not been employed and only filed investment returns (i.e. retired status)

      Exception:

      Per RIVO, cases may be routed on this criteria alone.

    10. Method of preparing the return has changed (paid preparer versus self-prepared, or MeF versus paper, etc.).

  7. Leads (managers or backups) must review possible RIVO cases received from tax examiners, and either return the cases to the tax examiners with instruction to work as normal or email the cases to RIVO. ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ Make sure to encrypt the email. Include local P&A analysts, HQ analysts, and any necessary local personnel in the email. These cases must be in an Excel spreadsheet and include: TIN, MFT, Tax Period, and reason(s) for sending to RIVO. All cases must also have and maintain an open Notice Review IDRS control base until RIVO accepts the case or the TC 846 has posted.

3.14.1.6.9.6 (01-01-2026)
Initial Allegation or Suspicion of Tax-Related Identity Theft Indicators

  1. Taxpayers can notify the IRS of identity theft utilizing Form 14039 Identity Theft Affidavit, or another similar statement included with their tax return. The IRS also has tools that can identify possible identity theft on behalf of a taxpayer. See paragraphs (4) and (5) below for IDRS IDT information.

    Note:

    Prisoners are often victims of IDT while they are incarcerated. For more information on reviewing prisoner returns for release date and earned income see IRM 3.14.1.6.9.19, Prisoner Returns, for more information.

  2. If the Form 14039 is attached to a tax return, paper or electronic, or identity theft statement made without a form, review the account carefully.

  3. Ensure that the tax return filed with the Form 14039 matches the posted tax return on IDRS and the filing patterns of the taxpayer. Verify the taxpayer filing pattern by reviewing IDRS CC IRPTRL, IMFOLT, and TRDBV data for three years prior to the notice module being reviewed, looking for IDT indicators on the previous modules as well. If the posted account information matches the true taxpayer tax return, process the case following normal IRM 3.14.1.6.1, General Review Procedures.

    Caution:

    Identity theft can occur for multiple years so be very careful the pattern of tax returns reviewed belong to the true taxpayer.

    1. If the posted return appears to be identity theft, and there are no indicators that RIVO or another area is already working the case see IRM 3.14.1.6.9.5, RIVO (Return Integrity and Verification Operation). If the case meets the criteria in IRM 3.14.1.6.9.5 (6)(if identity theft is suspected), continue with the steps below. If the case does not meet the criteria but there is still concern about IDT (for specific reasons) see the lead.

    2. If the tax return and notice (or transcript) account meet RIVO criteria, stop the refund. If the case is an AMS refund transcript leave notes in AMS about referring the case to RIVO. Give the case to the lead for routing to RIVO. See IRM 3.14.1.6.9.5, RIVO (Return Integrity and Verification Operation), for complete information.

      Reminder:

      If the refund was stopped with a TC 570, open a control base, see IRM 3.14.1.7.2, Controlling Cases, for more information. If the refund was stopped with a NOREFP maintain an open control base until RIVO accepts the case or returns it to Notice Review.

    3. If the address on the notice can be verified as the true taxpayer (IDRS CC IRPTRL, FINDS, RTVUE for prior years), then print intercept the notice, or retype intercept if an adjustment was needed (made with a hold code 4) in OLNR. If the address on the notice cannot be verified as that of the true taxpayer, then void intercept the notice in OLNR. Leave a history item in IDRS for void or retype.

  4. Use CC ENMOD to detect identity theft indicators marked by TC 971 with the Action Codes identified below. The codes will display in ENMOD on two lines.

    Example:

    971 10262025--------------20124705 08277-204-00000-5 for the TC 971 entry and below the 971 entry the IDT indicator will post as 971-CD>501.

    CC ENMOD Identity Theft Indicators

    Action Code Description
    501 Tax administration related identity theft - taxpayer provided the required ID theft documentation and case resolution is complete.
    504 Taxpayer-Identified Identity Theft not Affecting Tax Administration. Note: In FY 2014, the TC 971 AC 504 was expanded for use on both tax and non-tax-related identity theft allegations.
    505 IRS loss of PII-IRS identified, taxpayer not required to provide required ID theft documentation.
    506 IRS identified identity theft - IRS identified, taxpayer not required to provide required ID theft documentation, unless requested and Identity Theft issue is resolved.
    522 Identity theft claim has been made. Reminder: TC 971 AC 522 does not provide taxpayer protections or prevent future occurrences of identity theft. This code is used to identify potential identity theft cases.
    523 IRS identifies a potential repeat identity theft
    524 Locking SSNs with No Filing Requirements.
     

  5. Other indicators of identity theft can be seen on TXMOD (or IMFOLT). Be careful not to release any refunds on cases that are under review for identity theft.

    CC TXMOD Identity Theft Indicators

    Action Code Description
    111 Indicates the return with the matching DLN has been identified as ID Theft and moved to MFT 32.
    121 Potential ID Theft Case selected by Taxpayer Protection Program (TPP) for review prior to posting.
    129 Potential ID Theft Case selected by Taxpayer Protection Program (TPP) for review after the return posted.
     

3.14.1.6.9.7 (01-01-2026)
Slipped Blocks and Mixed Data Blocks

  1. Slipped blocks and mixed data blocks occur when data from a document or payment posts to a module related to a different document or payment in the same block of DLNs.

  2. Slipped Blocks have the following characteristics:

    1. A block (or part of a block) of documents or payments posted to the Master File incorrectly.

    2. The incorrect transactions have DLNs from other documents or payments in the same block.

    3. The DLN is usually from the document or payment immediately before or after the notice document or payment in the block sequence.

    4. A slipped block may result in erroneous refunds, incorrect notices, and/or lost or missing documents, returns, or payments.

      Note:

      Per Chief Counsel: If money is found in the wrong account(s) due to a Slipped Block and the money has refunded, Erroneous Refund Procedures (CAT- D) must be used to recover the money even if the money is not in the originally assigned case.

  3. Mixed Data Blocks have the following characteristics:

    1. A block (or part of a block) of documents or payments posted to the Master File incorrectly.

    2. The data is incorrect due to a transcription error.

    3. A mixed-data block may result in erroneous refunds and/or incorrect notices.

  4. Suspect a slipped block or a mixed data block if any of the following conditions are present:

    1. The data on the notice module does not match the data on the document.

    2. A posted payment amount does not match the amount listed on the payment voucher.

    3. A payment is missing or is misapplied.

  5. Using RTR DLN numbers (if able) and IDRS research the five payments and their accounts which posted immediately prior to the payment found in error, and the five payments and their accounts immediately after to the error payment from the notice document.

  6. To resolve the accounts found in error from the research above:

    1. Prevent the refund from generating when present and if possible. See IRM 3.14.1.7.1.1, Refund Intercepts, if needed to resolve the credit discrepancy.

      Note:

      If the refund cannot be prevented from generating and is needed to resolve the credit discrepancy, work any math error adjustment and the credit discrepancy as a Category D erroneous refund. See IRM 3.14.1.6.7.4 , Category D ERRF Resolution.

    2. Transfer all payments not belonging to the notice taxpayer to the appropriate account(s). Input a TC 570 on the credit side if needed to freeze the credit.

    3. If any payments belonging to the notice taxpayer are found, transfer them into the notice taxpayer's account.

    4. Reverse any current cycle offsets if needed to make the necessary credit transfers to correct the payment posting location.

      Note:

      Use a TC 570 on the credit side of any offset reversal.

    5. Review all math errors following IRM 3.14.1.6.12, Reviewing Math Error Notices – CP 10, CP 11, CP 12, CP 13, CP 16, CP 23, CP 24, and CP 25.

    6. Determine the notice disposition using IRM 3.14.1.7.8, Notice Disposition.

      Note:

      Make every effort to resolve these situations in cycle.

3.14.1.6.9.8 (01-01-2026)
Community Property Allocation

  1. Generally, community property is all property acquired during a marriage while the spouses are domiciled in a community property state. Examples of community property are:

    • Income, rents, dividends, and/or interest derived from community property.

    • Salaries, wages, or pay for the services of either spouse during the marriage.

    • Economic benefits attributable to the efforts of the spouse (for example, income reported on Schedules C, E, or F).

  2. However, taxpayers (filing FS-1, FS-3, or FS-4) who reside in a community property state may be able to allocate their income, deductions, and other items on their tax return in specific methods. The community property states are:

    • Arizona

    • California

    • Idaho

    • Louisiana

    • Nevada

    • New Mexico

    • Texas

    • Washington

    • Wisconsin

  3. Taxpayers use Form 8958, Allocation of Tax Amounts Between Certain Individuals in Community Property States, to determine the allocation of tax amounts between married filing separate spouses, California same-sex spouses, or registered domestic partners (RDP) with community property rights.

    1. RDP residing in California, Nevada, or Washington, must follow state community property laws and report half the combined community income of the individual and their partner.

    2. RDP can use only FS-1, or if they qualify, FS-4 for federal tax purposes.

  4. If information on the tax return, such as income, withholding, ES credits, etc., differs from the Form W-2, Wage and Tax Statement, and tax module information, suspect a community property allocation if the taxpayer is filing in one of the above states.

    Caution:

    Review both spouse’s tax modules for possible erroneous refunds.

    1. Determine if there is a Form 8958, Allocation of Tax Amounts Between Certain Individuals in Community Property States or a similar attachment to the return which indicates allocation of income and credits between the two taxpayers. If necessary, adjust to taxpayer intent. See IRM 3.14.1.7.6, Tax Adjustments, for more information.

    2. Request the tax return, if paper, to identify the exact split; use Form 2275, Records Request, Charge and Recharge.

  5. After reviewing the account and making any necessary changes in IDRS, disposition the notice in OLNR. See IRM 3.14.1.7.8 ,Notice Disposition for more information.

3.14.1.6.9.9 (01-01-2026)
Injured Spouse Allocation

  1. An Injured Spouse Allocation request can be filed by one spouse to protect their share of a joint overpayment. The spouse, whose portion of a joint income tax overpayment that was or will be offset to a Federal tax debt or TOP offset for which they are not liable, is known as the injured spouse.

  2. Injured Spouse Allocation requests are indicated by the following:

    1. DLN Blocking Series should be 920–929. See Document 6209, Section 4, Document Locator Number, Chapter 2 DLN Composition, Block Series for more information.

    2. Form 8379, Injured Spouse Allocation.

    3. "Injured Spouse" written or notated on the tax return or MeF file.

  3. Injured Spouse Allocations must be issued by manual refund (TC 840) to bypass the offset process.

    Caution:

    Notice Review does not process manual refunds for Injured Spouse Allocations.

  4. Review the notice following general review procedures.

  5. If the return is a true Injured Spouse Allocation and the blocking series is 920–929 follow the table below:

    If And Then
    No adjustment is required There is no TC 840 on the tax module

    1. Mark the notice disposition in OLNR.

    2. Open a Control Base to Accounts Management assigned to IDRS number 0547484769 in A status. See IRM 3.14.1.7.2, Controlling Cases for more information.

    3. Route the case to Accounts Management, using Form 3465, Adjustment Request. State in the remarks field of the Form 3465: Injured Spouse Allocation, R- frozen refund, no TC 840. If another freeze code is present notate on the Form 3465.

    4. See IRM 3.14.1.6.9.9 (7) below for package routing instructions.
    No adjustment is required TC 840 is present on the module Mark the notice disposition in OLNR. No other action is required.
    An adjustment must be made to the account TC 840 is present on the module

    1. Use CC REQ54 to input the adjustment using Blocking Series 05 with a Hold Code 4.

    2. Open a Control Base to Accounts Management assigned to IDRS number 0547484769 in A status. See IRM 3.14.1.7.2, Controlling Cases for more information.

    3. Ensure all Notice Review Control Bases are closed.

    4. Mark the notice disposition in OLNR.

    5. Route the case to Accounts Management, using Form 3465, Adjustment Request. State in the remarks field of the Form 3465: Injured Spouse Allocation, posted TC 840, pending adjustment with HC 4, K- freeze.

    6. See IRM 3.14.1.6.9.9 (7) below for package routing instructions.

  6. If the return has an Injured Spouse Allocation and the DLN blocking series is not 920–929, follow the table below:

    If And Then
    No adjustment is required There is no TC 840 (manual refund) on the tax module

    1. Prevent any refund from generating if possible, per IRM 3.14.1.7.1.1, Refund Intercept.

    2. Open a Control Base to Accounts Management assigned to IDRS number 0547484769 in A status. See IRM 3.14.1.7.2, Controlling Cases for more information. This control must be opened even if a NOREFP is not required (case is worked during the TC 570 timeline).

    3. Ensure all Notice Review Control Bases are closed and the AM base is in A status.

    4. Mark the notice disposition in OLNR.

    5. Route the case to Accounts Management, using Form 3465, Adjustment Request. State in the remarks field of the Form 3465: DLN blocking is incorrect for an Injured Spouse Allocation, the refund is held with a P- freeze (or R- freeze as applicable) and there is no TC 840.

    6. See IRM 3.14.1.6.9.9 (7) below for package routing instructions.
    No adjustment is required TC 840 is present on the module Mark the notice disposition in OLNR. Routing is not required.
    An adjustment must be made to the account Adjustment is a net increase (decreases the overpayment)

    1. Prevent any refund from generating if possible, per IRM 3.14.1.7.1.1, Refund Intercept.

    2. Open a Control Base to Accounts Management assigned to IDRS number 0547484769 in A status. See IRM 3.14.1.7.2, Controlling Cases for more information. This control must be opened even if a NOREFP is not required (the case is worked during the TC 570 timeline).

    3. Input the necessary adjustment using CC REQ54 using Blocking Series 05 with Hold Code 4. Be sure to input the adjustment using C for closed, to close the Control Base.

    4. Use CC REQ77/FRM77 to input a TC 470 with no Closing Code. This will prevent notices and identify a pending claim. See the SERP Command Code Job Aid for FRM77 for more information.

    5. Ensure all Notice Review Control Bases are closed and the AM base is in A status.

    6. Mark the notice disposition in OLNR.

    7. Route the case to Accounts Management, using Form 3465, Adjustment Request. State in the remarks field of the Form 3465: DLN blocking is incorrect for Injured Spouse Allocation, no TC 840, pending adjustment with HC 4, K- freeze. TC 470 input no closing code.

      Caution:

      See the note below if the offsets need to be brought back to the module. Be sure to freeze all credit transfers and notate the same on the Form 3465.

    8. See IRM 3.14.1.6.9.9 (7) below for package routing instructions.

    Note:

    If the prevented refund will not satisfy the debit created by the adjustment, check for offsets. If offsets of any type are present, See IRM 3.14.1.6.4.2, Lump Sum Credit Offsets — TC 826/706, TC 820/700 and IRM 3.14.1.6.4.3, Treasury Offset Program (TOP) Offsets — TC 898/899 for reversal instructions. See IRM 21.4.6.4, Refund Offset Research, if there are multiple TC 898 or TC 826.
    An adjustment must be made to the account Adjustment is a net decrease (increases the overpayment)

    1. Input the necessary adjustment using CC REQ54 and Blocking Series 05 with Hold Code 4. Be sure to input the adjustment using C for closed, to close the Control Base.

    2. Open a Control Base to Accounts Management assigned to IDRS number 0547484769 in A status. See IRM 3.14.1.7.2, Controlling Cases for more information.

    3. Ensure all Notice Review Control Bases are closed and the AM base is in A status.

    4. Route the case to Accounts Management, using Form 3465, Adjustment Request. State in the remarks field of the Form 3465: DLN blocking is incorrect for an Injured Spouse Allocation, the refund is held with a P- freeze (or R- freeze as applicable), there is no TC 840, and there is a pending adjustment with HC 4, K- freeze.

    5. See IRM 3.14.1.6.9.9 (7) below for package routing instructions.

  7. When routing an Injured Spouse Allocation to Accounts Management take the following steps:

    1. If a paper return, and the return is in Notice Review, use CC ESTABDT to recharge the return to Accounts Management. See the SERP Command Code Job Aid for ESTABD for more information.

    2. If the return is unavailable or is electronically filed, print TXMOD and INOLES for the case.

    3. Prepare Form 3465, Adjustment Request, according to the directions in the table above. Staple the completed Form 3465 to the front of the return or INOLES screen print (below the entity) and give to the lead for routing to Accounts Management in the current cycle.

3.14.1.6.9.10 (01-01-2025)
Natural Disaster Procedures

  1. Accounts impacted by a designated disaster should have a "–O" freeze present. A TC 971/AC 086 appearing on the taxpayer's CC ENMOD screen indicates disaster processing is in place. A list of regions (such as counties, parishes, or other political subdivisions) impacted by a designated disaster is compiled and provided by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA). The IRS then identifies the corresponding ZIP codes for disaster processing purposes.

  2. For processing years after 12/31/2006, a "–S" freeze may be present on the account. A TC 971/AC 688 would appear on CC ENMOD to indicate disaster processing.

  3. The Local Control File (input on designated ZIP codes) can be used to select notices for the area(s) designated on the Disaster Relief Memorandum, if penalty adjustments are required.

  4. If the "–O" (or "–S" if processed after 12/31/2006) freeze is not present on an account with an address that is either in the FEMA Zip Code list, or is outside the FEMA Zip Code list and the taxpayer has "self-identified" as being impacted by the disaster, take the following action:

    1. Access CC ENMOD for the taxpayer.

    2. While in the CC ENMOD screen, execute CC REQ77.

    3. Input TC 971 as the transaction code, using the disaster end date in the "TRANS-DT>" field. Input Action Code 086 (or 688 if processed after 12/31/2006) in the "TC 971-CD>" field.

      Example:

      For Hurricane Katrina, use a "TRANS-DT>" of 08292005, and an "EXTENSION-DT>" of 02282006 for all states except Florida. For Florida, use a "TRANS-DT>" of 08242005.

    4. In the "FEMA-NUM>" field, enter the four digit code of the disaster identified on the return, as shown in the FEMA lists. The lists can be found on the Technical Reference Information System (TRIS) web site at IRS Disaster Memos & Declarations.

    5. If there are multiple FEMA codes for the same disaster and the taxpayer identifies a particular state or region, use the FEMA code for that state or region. If it cannot be determined which FEMA code should be used, enter whichever FEMA code for that disaster will provide the longest period of extension relief/penalty suspension for the taxpayer.

    6. On the Remarks line of the FRM77 response screen, enter "Disaster relief per self-identification" or "Disaster relief per FEMA Zip Code" as appropriate.

    7. Label the notice using Custom Label 98, since a label has not yet been added to OLNR programming, with the following language:
      "We are giving your return penalty relief consideration, because your return indicates that you were affected by certain disasters. If any penalties or interest on your account will be reduced by this consideration, you will receive another notice in 2–3 weeks."

      Exception:

      Do not apply this Label, if after inputting TC 971 AC 086 or AC 688, no penalties or interest will abate. The TC 971 itself, however, should still be input as described above.

      Note:

      Master File has special processing in place that will allow an adjustment notice to generate for recomputation of interest (TC 196) and Failure to Pay Penalty (TC 276) when a TC 971 AC 086 or AC 688 is input. This is an exception to normal adjustment notice generation.

  5. If the taxpayer notates on the front of the return the designated disaster phrase, and the return has not been edited with the appropriate Computer Condition Codes (CCC), input the TC 971 and label the notice as described in Item (4) above.

  6. If correspondence, either attached to the return or subsequently received from the taxpayer, requests relief from any penalty due to disaster damage or disruption, take the following actions:

    1. Determine whether the taxpayer qualifies for relief based on disaster criteria as noted in item (1) above. If the taxpayer qualifies, input the TC 971 as described in Item (4) above.

    2. If the taxpayer does not qualify for relief based on disaster criteria, but may qualify based on "Reasonable Cause" , route the case to Accounts Management Function.

  7. If the estimated tax penalty has been imposed, determine if the taxpayer was required to make an estimated tax payment during the disaster period and if so, whether the payment was received by the date required by the Disaster Relief Memorandum. If the payment was received within this period, input the TC 971 as described in Item (4) above, which will systemically abate the portion of the estimated tax penalty assessed for the underpayment.

  8. If the payment was not received within the allowable period, and it concerns the estimated tax payment obligation of an individual, estate, or trust (not a corporation's obligation), then evaluate the taxpayer's statement to determine if it meets IRC 6654(e)(3)(A) relating to waivers due to casualty, disaster, or other unusual circumstances. See IRM 20.1, Penalty Handbook.
