3.14.1.6.12 (01-01-2026)

Reviewing Math Error Notices – CP 10, CP 11, CP 12, CP 13, CP 16, CP 23, CP 24, and CP 25

  1. Tax returns with math errors must receive the appropriate notice and math error explanations (TPNCs), even if the refund or balance due is what the taxpayer expected.

  2. Notices that contain Math Error information are:

    • CP 10 —Math error on an overpaid module, which causes a reduction of credit elect.

    • CP 11 — Math error on a module with a balance due of $5 or more.

    • CP 12 — Math error on a module with an overpayment of $1 or more.

    • CP 13 — Math error on a module with an even balance, a balance due of less than $5 or an overpayment of less than $1.

    • CP 16 — Math error on an overpaid module, and part or all the overpayment is offsetting to satisfy another tax module liability.

  3. Estimated Tax (ES) Discrepancy notices are not considered true Math Error notices, but they may also contain math errors.

    • CP 23 — ES discrepancy with a possible math error on a balance due module of $5 or more.

    • CP 24 — ES discrepancy with a possible math error on an overpaid module of $1 or more.

    • CP 25 — ES discrepancy with a possible math error on a module with an even balance, a balance due of less than $5, or an overpayment of less than $1.

  4. Review each TPNC assigned by ERS starting with the point of error through the remainder of the return. Although a complete review of the entire return is not required, a review of all lines, forms, and schedules affected by the error is necessary.

  5. Ensure that each TPNC matches the math error involved. The TPNC must clearly state the taxpayer’s error.

    • When assigning TPNCs, only one TPNC should be assigned to cover the point of error. Assigning two TPNCs that cover the same situation is incorrect.

  6. If the ERS (computer) figures are incorrect, adjust the module using CC REQ54.

    Note:

    ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡

  7. Prevent the refund from generating when increasing the tax (including Self-Employment (SE) Tax) or when decreasing refundable credits.

    Note:

    Do not prevent the refund from generating unless decreasing the overpayment.

  8. Only math error notices CP 12 and CP 24 have a systemic refund hold applied (TC 570 with blocking series "55555" ).There will not be a TC 846 on the account due to the temporary refund hold. These notices must be worked in cycle and the refund intercepted by Thursday 10 P.M. Eastern time to prevent an erroneous refund from going out to the taxpayer. When a refund needs to be prevented from generating, follow guidelines in IRM 3.14.1.7.1.1, Refund Intercepts.

  9. See the following for additional guidance on Math Errors:

    • Key 060 - Tax Period More Than Two Years Prior To Current Tax Year. See IRM 3.14.1.6.17.7.

    • Key 061 - Multiple Math Error Explanations. See IRM 3.14.1.6.17.8.

    • Key 100 - Non-Standard TPNC Explanations Not Computer Generated. See IRM 3.14.1.6.17.12.

  10. Correct all associated notices in the NRPS package if their accuracy is affected by a change to the primary notice or to the notice module.

3.14.1.6.12.1 (01-01-2026)
Items to Review on All Math Error Notices

  1. The following items need to be reviewed on every math error notice when impacted by the point of error:

    • TIN Type and Validity

    • Adjusted Gross Income (AGI)

    • Taxable Income (TXI)

    • Tax

    • Self-Employment (SE) Tax, if present

    • Accuracy of TPNCs assigned to the notice

    Note:

    TPNC verbiage shown on OLNR will always be that of the default (general) TPNC. The literal TPNC has line specifics which vary by tax form and tax year. These will appear on the actual notice and in the ERS IRM 3.12.3-1, Taxpayer Notice Codes.

  2. Also review the tax period, entity, and signature(s) on math error notices. These items are covered in IRM 3.14.1.6.1.1, Verifying Return Information.

3.14.1.6.12.1.1 (01-01-2026)
Verifying TIN Type, Validity, and Assignment Date

  1. The Protecting Americans from Tax Hikes Act (Path Act) was enacted December 18, 2015. The Path Act prohibits taxpayers from retroactively claiming certain TIN related credits for any tax year in which the taxpayer, spouse or qualifying child did not have a valid SSN, ATIN, or ITN active and assigned by the return due date as extended. The PATH Act applies to:

    Note:

    The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBA) enacted in 2025 allows the credits below only with a Social Security Number (SSN) for all applicable dependents. See each section for specific taxpayer SSN requirements. EIC has always been allowed with SSNs only for taxpayers (primary and secondary as applicable) and dependents.

    • Child Tax Credit (CTC), IRM 3.14.1.6.12.5.2

    • Additional Child Tax Credit (ACTC), IRM 3.14.1.6.12.5.6

    • American Opportunity Credit (AOTC) both refundable and non-refundable, IRM 3.14.1.6.12.5.7

    • Earned Income Credit (EIC),IRM 3.14.1.6.12.3

    Note:

    For more information about dependent TIN errors see IRM 3.14.1.6.12.4, Dependent TIN-Related Errors.

  2. The PATH Act prohibits current year refunds of EIC or ACTC before February 15, (including amended returns). If ERS previously disallowed credits, and Notice Review is adjusting the account to allow them before February 15 on current year returns, input the adjustment with the appropriate hold codes so the refund will not be released before February 15.

  3. The PATH Act does not allow the removal of PATH Act impacted credits previously allowed due to a filing status change to Married Filing Joint unless initiated by the taxpayer.

  4. Research is required on all TINs on the return (primary, secondary, and dependent, as applicable) to determine whether the PATH Act credits are allowable on an original tax return filing use CC-INOLES-TIN ASGMT to research:

    1. SSN - if the field is populated with all zeros, the assignment date is prior to January 1, 2012. If the credit(s) is associated to an SSN, the SSN must have been assigned earlier than the due date or approved due date as extended of the return being processed.

    2. ITIN - if the field is populated with all zeros, the ITIN assignment date is prior to January 1, 2012. If the credit(s) is associated to an ITIN, the ITIN assignment date must have been assigned earlier than the due date or approved due date as extended of the return being processed.

      Note:

      For prior year returns, if the ITIN assignment date is 90 days or less after the return due date, the Real Time System (RTS) in EUP can be used to verify the received date of the application. If received prior to the due date, allow the credit.

    3. ATIN - if the credit(s) is associated to an ATIN, the ATIN application must have been received earlier than the due date or approved due date as extended of the return processed.

  5. On CC RTVUE, each dependent TIN is listed with the name control and a NAP EIF Response Indicator (NRI):

    An Indicator of Indicates the TIN
    NRI = S is valid
    NRI = L is invalid

  6. On CC INOLES each dependent ITIN will have a Status Value”

    A Status Value of Indicates the ITIN is
    Status Value “I” Inactive (expired)
    Status Value “A” Active (not expired)
    Status Value “U” Unvalidated

  7. Use the table below to research dependent TIN validity and appropriate account and notice actions based on the research performed.

    If And Then
    TPNC 705 was assigned, and CC RTVUE shows that not all dependents listed on the return were transcribed The additional dependent TIN is valid

    1. Adjust the account to allow the dependent.

    2. Void, retype, or label the notice as appropriate.
    TPNC 705 was assigned, and CC RTVUE shows that not all dependents listed on the return were transcribed The additional dependent TIN is invalid

    1. Print the notice.

    2. Prevent the refund from generating if applicable, using guidelines outlined in IRM 3.14.1.7.1.1, Refund Intercepts.
    TPNC 710 was assigned, check CC INOLES to see if ITIN is active or inactive If ITIN is inactive

    1. Print the notice.

    2. Disallow any credits incorrectly allowed for the invalid dependent.

    3. Prevent the refund from generating if applicable using guidelines outlined in IRM 3.14.1.7.1.1, Refund Intercepts.

3.14.1.6.12.1.1.1 (01-01-2026)
Expired ITIN Math Errors

  1. When reviewing a math error notice with an expired ITIN TPNC:

    1. The expired ITIN may be present as a primary taxpayer, secondary taxpayer, dependent, education credit student, and/or child and dependent care credit qualifying individual, and Credit for other Dependents. All these positions will need to be researched per the TPNC assigned to determine the disallowed claim on the math error. CAUTION: Other math errors not involving an expired ITIN may also be present.

    2. Exemptions, Child Tax/Additional Child Tax Credit, Credit for other Dependents, and Education Credit will not be allowed on a return when claimed for an expired ITIN.

      Note:

      Child and Dependent Care expenses will be allowed if the qualifying child has a valid and active ITIN. (Exception: this is the only credit that will be allowed and does not need to be assigned by the due date of the return).

    3. Expired ITIN indications: Research Command Code INOLES and/or IMFOLE.

    • INOLES ITIN Status- Value “I” means Inactive (expired)

    • INOLES ITIN Status-Value “A” means Active (not expired)

    • INOLES ITIN Status-Value “U” means un-validated

    • INOLES ITIN Status-Value “Blank” means the TIN input is NOT an ITIN (it is an SSN, IRSN, or ATIN)

    • IMFOLE: Posted TC 971 AC 193 the ITIN has expired

    • IMFOLE: Posted TC 972 AC 193 means the ITIN has renewed and is now active.

    • Review the ITINs on the return applicable to the TPNC to verify the ITIN Status is still Inactive (INOLES field ITIN Status with the value of “I”; IMFOLE un-reversed TC 971 AC 193). If the ITIN status for the ITIN credit was disallowed and has changed to Active (INOLES), or there is a posted TC 972 AC 193 (IMFOLE) on the module.

    • Adjust the account to allow the exemption(s) credit(s) and retype the notice.

      Note:

      Care must be taken to only adjust the exemption(s) and credit(s) to allow the claims ONLY for ITINs that have become Active between ERS assignment of the TPNC and review of the notice.

    For example, if two dependent exemptions and child tax/additional child tax credit were disallowed, but only one has since renewed, only adjust the account to allow the claim for ONE of the ITINs.

3.14.1.6.12.1.2 (01-01-2026)
Verifying Adjusted Gross Income (AGI), Taxable Income (TXI), and Tax Changes

  1. Compare Adjusted Gross Income (AGI), Taxable Income (TXI), and tax including Self-Employment (SE) Tax to the notice as described below:

    1. Verify any change made by ERS to the AGI, TXI, and tax amounts on IDRS to the tax return filed by the taxpayer.

    2. If filing status is the point of error, compare the filing status on the return to the tax account. If ERS changed the filing status, verify that the filing status was changed correctly.

    3. Perfect the AGI and TXI if adjusting the tax on the tax module. However, do not adjust AGI and TXI if no changes to the tax are needed.

      Reminder:

      AGI can be adjusted below zero, but TXI and tax cannot. The adjustment will unpost.

    4. If the claimed Qualified dividends are more than the claimed Ordinary dividends, research IRP data to verify dividend amounts. . If the amounts cannot be verified with IRP data, add the amount for both Ordinary and Qualified dividends from the tax return and use the total as Ordinary dividends while still using the originally reported Qualified dividends to figure tax.

      Note:

      See Miscellaneous Quick Reference Chart in Job Aid 2534-002.

    5. If Lump Sum Election (LSE) is notated on the return, use the taxpayer figures for taxable Social Security.

    6. Compare IDRS overpayment, balance due, and credit elect amounts to the notice.

    7. If the ERS (computer) figures are incorrect, adjust the module using CC REQ54.

      Note:

      ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡

    8. Prevent the refund from generating when increasing the tax (including SE Tax) or when decreasing refundable credits.

      Note:

      Do not prevent the refund from generating unless decreasing the overpayment.

  2. Take appropriate action to correct the taxpayer’s account and incorrect or incomplete TPNCs to adequately explain math errors.

3.14.1.6.12.1.3 (01-01-2026)
Verifying Self-Employment Income and Self-Employment Tax Changes

  1. The Social Security Administration (SSA) determines Social Security Benefits based, in part, on the Social Security Tax Withheld from earnings. For self-employed individuals this includes taxes reported on Schedule SE , Self-Employment Tax.

  2. Usually taxpayers must pay self-employment (SE) tax on all net earnings of $400 or more. Generally, the amount subject to self-employment tax is 92.35% of net earnings from self-employment ($434.00 X .9235), regardless of age, even if receiving Social Security or Medicare benefits (See Publication 17, Your Federal Income Tax, for exceptions). SE Tax is entered on the appropriate line of Form 1040 , U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, or Form 1040-SR, U.S. Income Tax Return for Seniors, Schedule 2 , Additional Taxes.

    1. Common items included in computing SE Tax are Schedule C, Profit or Loss from Business (Sole Proprietorship), Schedule E, Supplemental Income and Loss, and Schedule F, Profit or Loss from Farming, and "other income" .

    2. Taxpayers earning W-2 wages and self-employment income must include all required data on Sch SE to correctly figure SE Tax.

    3. Use Tax Worksheets, Schedule SE, for the applicable tax year, to correctly figure/verify SE Tax.

  3. If a math error is related to self-employment income, then verify:

    • Income,

    • Schedule SE,

    • Deductible portion of Self-Employment Tax (adjustment to income, which could also impact AGI, TXI, Tax, and application of non-refundable credits), and

    • Self-Employment Tax.

  4. Use the following table as a guide for determining how to review various SE Tax scenarios.

    If Then
    The Schedule C, Schedule F, or Schedule E Self-Employed income amount has changed Verify that the tax on Schedule SE was also changed.
    The taxpayer has Social Security wages greater than the current year limitation (can be found in IMF National Job Aids 2533-002, FICA, Medicare, and SE Tax Chart) The entire self-employment amount may not be subject to Social Security tax since self-employment (SE) tax is now divided between Social Security and Medicare taxes.

    Reminder:

    There is no longer a maximum Medicare income limit for 199412 and later returns.
    The taxpayer has self-employment income of less than $434 (Exception: For church employee income, less than $108.28) Do not assess SE Tax.

    Exception:

    If the taxpayer enters SE income of $433.00 to $433.99, round up the entry to $434 and assess the tax.
    The taxpayer used either of the optional SE Tax methods Verify that the SE Tax method was not changed by ERS to the normal method. Adjust the SE Tax if necessary.
    The taxpayer computed SE Tax, but did not include Schedule SE with the return Check for Schedules C, E, or F. Follow the taxpayer’s intent to assess SE Tax.
    Self-Employment income is shown on the line marked Other Income on the front of the Form 1040, but no SE Tax is computed The return should have been coded with an RPC N. If the account was not coded with an RPC N, recharge the return (if paper) and route the case to the Examination Function using Form 3465, Adjustment Request.
    No SE Tax is self-assessed, and Schedules C, E, or F is attached Do not assess the SE Tax unless EIC is claimed.

    Exception:

    If the taxpayer qualifies for EIC, additional instructions may apply. Refer to , IRM 3.14.1.6.12.1.4, SE Tax Computation — TPNC 580.

  5. Self-Employment Tax is calculated per individual taxpayer including limitations for Social Security Withholding, or the portion of wages and/or self-employed income paid to the Social Security Administration. If the tax return is married filing jointly status (FS-2) and there is no indication which taxpayer is liable for SE Tax, refer to the table below.

    If the primary taxpayer’s Social Security wages (Form W-2) are Then assign the SE Tax to
    At least the current year limitation (can be found in IMF National Job Aids 2533-002, FICA, Medicare, and SE Tax Chart) The secondary taxpayer
    Less than the current year limitation (can be found in IMF National Job Aids 2533-002, FICA, Medicare, and SE Tax Chart) The primary taxpayer

  6. When adjusting the SE Tax, ensure that all Item Reference Numbers (IRNs) have been addressed, in addition to a TC 290 tax increase or a TC 291 tax decrease. This is a general list but may not be all inclusive. Refer to Document 6209, Section 8A, Part 2, for all transaction codes.

    • 888 - AGI, if changing the SE Tax deduction amount

    • 886 - TXI, if changing the SE Tax deduction amount and TXI needs to be changed

    • 889 - Self-Employment Tax amount, this represents the total amount of SE Tax (combining if FS2 and both taxpayers are self-employed)

    • 878 - Primary Self-Employment Income, the net SE income for the primary taxpayer only

    • 879 - Secondary Self-Employment Income, the net SE income for the secondary taxpayer only

    • 895 - Primary Medicare Income, the net Medicare income for the primary taxpayer only

    • 896 - Secondary Medicare Income, the net Medicare income for the secondary taxpayer only

    Note:

    The Medicare portion of the SE Tax (2.9%) applies to all earnings from self-employment, even if the maximum amount to which social security tax applies is reached (current year limitation for SE Tax can be found in IMF National Job Aids 2533-002, FICA, Medicare, and SE Tax Chart).

  7. SE Tax does not apply to amounts earned by:

    • Nonresident aliens, unless an international Social Security agreement applies.

    • Public officials, except for public officials compensated solely on a fee basis whose services are not covered by a Section 218 agreement.

    • Members of certain religious sects who filed and had approved a Form 4029, Application for Exemption From Social Security and Medicare Taxes and Waiver of Benefits.

    • Members of the clergy who filed and had approved Form 4361, Application for Exemption From Self-Employment Tax for Use by Ministers, Members of Religious Orders and Christian Science Practitioners.

    1. Review CC ENMOD MIN-SE-TX-EXMPT> field or CC IMFOLE MINISTER SE CD: field to determine if Form 4029 or Form 4361 was filed. If the value is: 0 - Neither form is on file, 1 - Form 4361 approved, 2 - Form 4361 denied, 4 - Form 4029 approved, 8 - Form 4029 denied.

3.14.1.6.12.1.4 (01-01-2026)
Self- Employment (SE) Tax Computation – Possible TPNC 580

  1. TPNC 580 states: We computed self-employment tax on your tax return for the self-employment income you reported. Since you included self-employment income in computing your Earned Income Credit (EIC), you must pay self-employment tax to receive EIC.

  2. ERS assigns a TPNC 580 if the taxpayer has requested EIC, has income subject to self-employment (SE) tax, but does not include the SE Tax on their tax return. ERS computes the SE Tax and assesses the SE Tax (up to, but not exceeding, the amount of EIC).

  3. If the SE Tax exceeds EIC, ERS instructions are to assign Return Processing Code (RPC) N, instead of assigning TPNC 580 and assessing the SE Tax.

  4. Notice Review tax examiners should review the case the same as ERS. If ERS has incorrectly adjusted the SE Tax, follow the table below, regardless of an assignment of TPNC 580.

    If the Correct SE Tax Then
    Exceeds the EIC amount Assess the SE Tax up to the amount of EIC. Follow the steps in IRM 3.14.1.6.12.1.4 (5) below.

    Exception:

    Refer the case to the Examination Function, if the SE income is greater than $10,000. Route using Form 3465, Adjustment Request.
    Does not exceed the EIC amount for which the taxpayer is eligible Correct the SE Tax with REQ54/ADJ54. See IRM 3.14.1.6.12.1.3, Verifying Self-Employment Income and Self-Employment Tax Changes, for more information.

  5. If routing is not appropriate or if the Examination Function does not accept the case, assess the SE Tax up to, but not exceeding, the EIC amount. Follow the list below and refer to the example if necessary.

    1. Do not factor in the SE Tax deduction from income.

    2. Do not change the AGI or TXI.

    3. Address the Item Reference Codes 878/895 or (879/896), by backing into them from the EIC/SE Tax amount (see example below)

    4. On the CC ADJ54 screen, use "SE-TAX/EIC" in the Activity field to identify the adjustment as an EIC-limited SE Tax assessment.

    5. In the Remarks field, include the statement, "Assess EIC-limited SE Tax, equivalent to $x,xxx in wages, -SE-Tax-Deduction not applied."

    Example:

    If the EIC received by the taxpayer is $1,500, the TC 889 for SE Tax will also be $1,500. By dividing that amount by .153, it will establish an amount of $ 9,804.00 as the wages for Item Reference Codes 878/879 (Social Security earnings) and 895/896 (Medicare earnings), upon which the SE Tax is being assessed.

3.14.1.6.12.1.5 (01-01-2026)
Verifying Accuracy of Assigned Taxpayer Notice Codes

  1. When reviewing notices containing TPNCs, it is important to allow only TPNCs that reflect actual errors made by the taxpayer. A ripple is a TPNC assigned in error by ERS to a computer calculation resulting from a previous math error. Each TPNC must be reviewed on its own and not be the result of a previous error to be considered a valid TPNC.

    Example:

    ERS assigns a TPNC 121 for a Schedule C error made by the taxpayer. The Schedule C error causes a change to SE Tax, but the taxpayer correctly calculated SE Tax on the incorrect Schedule C figures. The ERS tax examiner assigns a TPNC 268 for the change in SE Tax. This is a ripple error. In this example, if all the math calculations are now correct, the notice disposition in OLNR is retype and remove TPNC 268.

  2. If another taxpayer error is found after the point of error, add the correct TPNC.

  3. Remove incorrect TPNCs.

  4. Custom TPNC 100s are no longer valid in OLNR. Review TPNC 100s assigned by ERS and choose the five most important TPNCs in OLNR.

3.14.1.6.12.1.6 (01-01-2026)
Verifying Information from Form W-2, Form W-2G, and Form 1099

  1. Verify Form W-2, Wage and Tax Statement, Form W-2G, Certain Gambling Winnings, Form 1099-MISC, Miscellaneous Information, and other types of income using IRP data and attached documents when the point of error is one of the following:

    • Additional Child Tax Credit (Schedule 8812)

    • Adjusted Gross Income (AGI)

    • Child and Dependent Care (Schedule 2 or Form 2441)

    • Credit for Elderly or Disabled (Schedule 3 or Schedule R)

    • Earned Income Credit (EIC)

    • Estimated Tax Payment Discrepancy (CP 23, CP 24, or CP 25)

    • Excess Federal Insurance Contribution Act (FICA)

    • Gambling Winnings

    • Individual Retirement Account (IRA)

    • Lump Sum Distribution

    • Non-Compute Returns (CP 51A, CP 51B, or 51C)

    • Pensions

    • Self-Employment Income (Schedule C, Schedule E, or Schedule F)

    • Self-Employment Tax (Schedule SE)

    • Social Security Benefits

    • Total Income

    • TPNC 297 or 299

    • Wages

    • Withholding

  2. Tax Period: The individual income tax period usually runs from January 1 through December 31 of a given year. Compare the year of Form W-2, Wage and Tax Statement, with the tax form year. Wages may only be claimed for the tax period in which the wages were paid. If Form W-2, Wage and Tax Statement, indicates the tax return was processed to the incorrect year, reprocess the return as appropriate. See IRM 3.14.1.6.21 Reprocessing Returns. If the module is overpaid, and the refund transaction has not generated, prevent the refund from generating using procedures in IRM 3.14.1.7.1.1, Refund Intercepts, and void any notices associated reprocess to a different tax period. If the refund transaction has already generated, follow Erroneous Refund procedures, IRM 3.14.1.6.7.

  3. Name Mismatch: If the name shown on Form W-2, Wage and Tax Statement, does not match the return follow the table below.

    If the taxpayer Then
    Did not use the money amount on W-2 for computing Wages or Withholding Remove and process as loose Form W-2, Wage and Tax Statement.
    Did use the W-2 wages or withholding Accept all attached W-2 wages and withholding per taxpayer intent.
    Claimed children's income without Form 8814, Parents' Election To Report Child's Interest and Dividends Remove child/children's income and send TPNC 134.
    Claimed child/children's income withForm 8814, Parents' Election To Report Child's Interest and Dividends Allow child/children's income from interest and/or dividends only.

    Note:

    A parent can only claim interest and/or dividend income from a child when there is no federal income tax withheld from the child's income until the age of 19 or age 24 if the child is a full-time student.

  4. Wages, Allocated Tips, and Other Compensation: The sum of all entries for wages and other compensation shown on Form W-2, Wage and Tax Statement, box 1, should equal the amount claimed on Form 1040, U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, or Form 1040SR, U.S. Income Tax Return for Seniors. Follow the verification table below.

    If the amount on the return And the taxpayer Then
    Includes compensation from other than Form W-2 , Wage and Tax Statement, wages Included this compensation to compute EIC Accept the income as earned unless it can be identified as unearned income (unemployment compensation or pension income, for example).

    Caution:

    If unearned income is from Temporary Assistance for Needy Family (TANF), FS4 or FS5 may need to be changed to FS1.
    Is greater than the total wages on W-2 Included this compensation to compute EIC Do not decrease the entry. Accept the larger wage amount unless the taxpayer made a double entry, a transposition error, or used Social Security wages from Form W-2, Wage and Tax Statement. Exception: Form W-2, Wage and Tax Statement, box 12 or 14 includes deferred compensation such as Thrift Savings Plan (TSP) or 401(k) contributions.
    Is less than the total wages on W-2 Included this compensation to compute EIC Change the amount entered as wages on the return to match the total Form W-2, Wage and Tax Statement, wages.
    Is less than the total wages on W-2 Included a statement indicating that the Form(s) W-2 are incorrect Do not process as a math error.
    Is less than the total wages on W-2 Has Schedule C income Review the Schedule C to determine if the taxpayer included Form W-2, Wage and Tax Statement, income on Schedule C. If so, do not increase wages for (Statutory Employees) on Form 1040 , U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, or Form 1040-SR, U.S. Income Tax Return for Seniors.
    Is less than the total wages on W-2 Reported a gross income amount on line 7, Form 1040, U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, and also, on Form 1040-SR ,U.S. Income Tax Return for Seniors, Schedule C Deduct the amount reported from Form 1040, U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, Line 7 if it is determined to be a duplicate of Schedule C income reported elsewhere on the return.

  5. Federal Income Tax Withheld: Federal Income Tax withheld by the employer is reported on Form W-2, Wage and Tax Statement, box 2. It is a refundable credit that is applied against the total tax due on the tax return. Federal income tax withheld may also be reported on Form W-2G, Certain Gambling Winnings, Form 8959, and Form 1099-MISC, Miscellaneous Information, . Combine all the federal income tax withheld from all sources. Compare amount to the taxpayer’s entry on the line marked "Federal income tax withheld from Form(s) W-2 and 1099" on Form 1040, U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, and Form 1040-SR, U.S. Income Tax Return for Seniors. Follow the verification table below.

    1. If Then
      The withholding amount claimed is more than the total from all attached documents.

      1. Determine if any attached Form 1099 includes withholding.

      2. Allow any withholding shown on Form 1099.

      3. If no withholding is shown, follow guidelines in ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡

      Note:

      The taxpayer is required to attach Form 1099-R, Distributions From Pensions, Annuities, Retirement or Profit-Sharing Plans, IRAs, Insurance Contracts, etc., if any federal income tax was withheld from a distribution from pensions, annuities, retirement or profit-sharing plans, IRAs, insurance contracts, etc.

      Caution:

      If withholding is overstated and the tax module is refunding, follow Category B Erroneous Refund Procedures, even if the refund can be prevented from generating. Refer to IRM 3.14.1.6.7.3, Category B ERRF Resolution.
      The taxpayer claims more withholding than is substantiated by W-2 and has no earned income on Form 1040, wages line

      3. Assign 582 e.

      The taxpayer used Social Security Tax withheld (W-2, box 4) instead of Federal Income Tax withheld (W-2, box 2)

      2. Assign TPNC 283

        If withholding is overstated and the tax module is refunding, follow Category B Erroneous Refund Procedures, even if the refund can be prevented from generating. Refer to IRM 3.14.1.6.7.3, Category B ERRF Resolution.
      Withholding is claimed on a secured return (identified by a TC 599 in the left hand margin of page 1 of the tax return) and Form W-2(s) is not attached

      2. If no attachments, check CC TDINQ or CC IRPTR

      3. Attach the printout to the return

      4. Adjust withholding accordingly
      Form W-2, Wage and Tax Statement, is missing and withholding is claimed

      The withholding amount claimed is less than the total from Form W-2 and/or W-2G

      2. See IRM 3.14.1.6.9.8, Community Property Allocation

      3. ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡

  6. Excess Social Security and Railroad Retirement Tax Amount (RRTA) Tax Withheld.

    1. If a taxpayer has more than one employer for the current tax year and the total Social Security Wages is over the current year limitation(can be found in IMF National Job Aids 2533-002, FICA, Medicare, and SE Tax Chart), the employers may have withheld too much social security tax. If so, a credit can be taken for the excess on the "Excess Social Security tax and Tier 1 RRTA tax withheld" line of the Form 1040, U.S. Individual Income Tax Return.

    2. Effective on returns processed after January 1, 2007, Excess FICA is separated from Federal Withholding at the Master File level, and posts to the tax module as a TC 766 with Credit Reference Number (CRN) 252.

    3. Any necessary adjustments to Excess FICA should be made based on how it originally posted (either by TC 806 or TC 766).

    4. Use Form W-2, Wage and Tax Statement, documents or CC IRPTR and the table below to verify excess credit. Also available is the Excess Social Security and RRTA Tax Worksheet, in the IMF Tax Worksheets, by applicable year.

    If the taxpayer Then
    Filed a joint return Each spouse must figure excess Social Security withholding separately. Do not combine the social security withholding of the primary taxpayer with the secondary taxpayer.

    1. Has ONLY ONE employer and the employer withheld more than the annual maximum, OR

    2. Has two or more employers, but ONLY ONE employer caused the excess by withholding more than the entire annual maximum

      Note:

      Different EINs should be treated as separate employers even if business names are the same.

    		 Disallow the credit. The taxpayer must seek reimbursement from the employer.
    Has multiple Form W-2, Wage and Tax Statement, documents from only one employer, and Box C of those Form W-2, Wage and Tax Statement, documents state "Agent For" Allow the credit. Input the adjustment using override code N and Reason Code 055.
    Did contribute excess Social Security tax through the deductions of two or more employers (two or more W-2s required.) Allow the credit. See the Notice Review Job Aid 2534-002, Excess Social Security Tax Worksheet to figure the excess credit amount.

  7. Pension Plan — Employers report participation in a pension plan on Form W-2, Wage and Tax Statement, box 13. If the taxpayer has an IRA deduction, use Publication 590 to determine any limitations and for the IRA worksheet.

3.14.1.6.12.2 (01-01-2026)
Standard Deduction, Additional Deductions, and Schedule A Errors

  1. Taxpayer and IRS processing errors often relate to Standard Deduction, Age-Blind Indicator (ABI), Schedule A Itemized Deductions. Consult the following sections for guidance in reviewing and resolving these errors.

  2. Taxpayers frequently claim incorrect amounts for Standard Deduction for their filing status, make math errors on Schedule A, or have subtraction issues. See the following sections of the IRM for specific types of deductions. Review the table below for some commonly misapplied TPNCs for standard deduction and Schedule A and when to use them.

    TPNC When to Use
    190 The taxpayer made an error on their Schedule A and the IRS is now using the standard deduction because it results in lower taxes for the taxpayer. This must be used with another Sch A TPNC (where the error occurred on the Sch A).
    192 The taxpayer claimed an incorrect number of ABI indicators, multiplied the ABI indicators incorrectly, or did not include the additional ABI with their standard deduction.
    194 The taxpayer left the standard deduction blank or the amount was wrong for the filing status (if either of these are true, even if the taxpayer is blind or over 65 this is the correct TPNC).
    731 The taxpayer made an error subtracting standard deduction or Schedule A Itemized Deductions from their AGI (whether or not they are claiming QBID).

3.14.1.6.12.2.1 (01-01-2026)
Standard Deduction Limits

  1. The Standard Deduction is for taxpayers who don't itemize their deductions on Schedule A, Form 1040, U.S. Individual Income Tax Return. See the table below and Pub 501 for more information on Standard Deductions.

    Year Single or Married Filing Separately Married Filing Joint or Qualifying Surviving Spouse Head of Household
    2025 $15,750 $31,500 $23,625
    2024 $14,600 $29,200 $21,900
    2023 $13,850 $27,700 $20,800
    2022 $12,950 $25,900 $19,400
    2021 $12,550 $25,100 $18,800
    2020 $12,400 $24,800 $18,650
    2019 $12,200 $24,400 $18,350

  2. Verify the taxpayer's filing status and verify that the taxpayer is not claiming an additional amount for Standard Deduction with an Age-Blind Indicator (ABI). If intent to claim an ABI is present on the return, refer to IRM 3.14.1.6.12.2.2, Age-Blind Indicator (ABI).

3.14.1.6.12.2.2 (01-01-2026)
Age-Blind Indicator (ABI)

  1. The Age-Blind Indicator (ABI) increases the standard deduction amount if a taxpayer is 65 or older, and/or blind, at the end of the tax year (December 31 of the tax year or before). Separate check-boxes appear for age and for blindness on the Form 1040 , U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, and Form 1040-SR, U.S. Income Tax Return for Seniors, with one set of checkboxes available for each spouse. A married couple filing a joint return can have as many as four ABIs on a given return.

  2. Review each TPNC assigned by ERS from the point of error. Review all lines, forms, and schedules affected by the error. The error must lead to the standard deduction amount. If the point of error is before or applies to standard deduction review the following:

    1. Verify if the taxpayer(s) are 65 and/or older, and/or blind at the end of the year,

    2. If the taxpayers qualify for one or more ABIs, adjust the account,

    3. Retype or label the notice but be sure to send the correct TPNC.

      Note:

      If the taxpayer is eligible for one or more ABIs but calculated their total standard deduction incorrectly (forgot to include ABIs or miscalculated), the correct TPNC is 192. If the taxpayer used the incorrect standard deduction for their filing status regardless of ABI eligibility or calculation, the correct TPNC is 194.

  3. Common ABI errors may result from the taxpayer:

    • Claiming the incorrect number of ABI indicators, multiplying the ABI indicators incorrectly, or not including the additional ABI with the standard deduction (TPNC 192).

    • Using the incorrect standard deduction amount for the filing status or entering no standard deduction (TPNC 194).

  4. Use the chart below to apply the appropriate year's amounts for one ABI for each filing status. If multiple ABI indicators are checked, multiply the amount accordingly.

    Reminder:

    The amounts below are per checkbox. Carefully review the number of Age-Blind Indicator boxes checked for the primary and secondary taxpayer when applicable.

    Return Year Single FS-1 Married Filing Joint FS-2 or Qualifying Surviving Spouse FS-5 Married Filing Separately FS-3 Head of Household FS-4
    2025 $2,000 $1,600 $1,600 $2,000
    2024 $1,950 $1,550 $1,550 $1,950
    2023 $1,850 $1,500 $1,500 $1,850
    2022 $1,750 $1,400 $1,400 $1,750
    2021 $1,700 $1,350 $1,350 $1,700
    2020 $1,650 $1,300 $1,300 $1,650
    2019 $1,650 $1,300 $1,300 $1,650

3.14.1.6.12.2.3 (01-01-2026)
Enhanced Deduction for Seniors (Tax Years 2025-2028)

  1. For tax years 2025 through 2028, the passage of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBA) granted an additional or enhanced deduction for seniors. This enhanced deduction for seniors is in addition to standard deduction and Age-Blind Indicator (ABI) or in addition to Schedule A, Itemized Deductions. The enhanced deduction for seniors is claimed on Schedule 1-A.

  2. To qualify for the credit taxpayers must:

    • Be 65 years of age or older (before the end of the tax year),

    • Have a valid SSN assigned before the due date of the return, and if applicable

    • File married filing jointly (FS-2) if married. If only one taxpayer is claiming the enhanced deductions for seniors, only that taxpayer needs to have an SSN; the other taxpayer on an FS-2 return can have a different TIN type.

      Note:

      Married Filing Separately (FS-3) taxpayers do not qualify for this credit.

  3. The enhanced deduction for seniors is $6,000 per individual. Therefore, if both taxpayers on an FS-2 return meet the requirements the enhanced deduction is $12,000.

    Exception:

    The enhanced deduction for seniors phases out for taxpayers with modified adjusted gross income over $75,000 ($150,000 for joint filers).

  4. Review errors related to retirement age carefully (TPNCs 131, 192) and review ABI boxes on the return. The IRS is responsible for adjusting the account and granting the enhanced deduction if the taxpayer forgot to claim it. See TPNC 637 below.

  5. When reviewing notices with errors for enhanced deduction for seniors, ensure the correct TPNC has been applied to the notice. See the table below for TPNCs for enhanced deduction for seniors including a brief description. See IRM 3.12.3-1, Taxpayer Notice Codes, for the full TPNC wording.

    Taxpayer Notice Code (TPNC) Number Brief Description of the TPNC
    543 We changed the amount of TXI because:

    • You didn’t complete Schedule 1-A, or

    • You didn’t attach Schedule 1-A to your return.
    637 You qualify for this deduction. We calculated the deduction for you. We’ve made the necessary changes to your return.
    638 We didn’t allow the deduction: your filing status was FS-3, you or your spouse’s SSN was missing or didn’t match, you or your spouse has an ITIN, you or your spouse’s SSN wasn’t assigned before the tax return due date.
    639 We changed the amount you calculated for the deduction because it was incorrect.

3.14.1.6.12.2.4 (01-01-2026)
No Tax on Tips - Tip Income Deduction (Tax Years 2025-2028)

  1. Effective for tax periods 2025 through 2028, employees and self-employed individuals may deduct qualified tips received in occupations listed by the IRS as customarily and regularly receiving tips that are reported on a Form W-2, Form 1099, or other specified statement furnished to the individual or reported directly by the individual on Form 4137, Social Security and Medicare Tax on Unreported Tip Income.

  2. The deduction is available in addition to itemizing (Schedule A) and non-itemizing (standard deduction) and is claimed on Schedule 1-A. Self-employed individuals in a Specified Service Trade or Business (SSTB) under section 199A are not eligible. Employees whose employer is in an SSTB also are not eligible.

  3. In addition to the above qualifications, taxpayers must:

    • Have a valid SSN assigned before the due date of the return.

    • File Married Filing Jointly (FS-2) if they are married. If only one taxpayer is claiming the tip deduction, only that taxpayer needs to have an SSN; the other taxpayer on an FS-2 return can have a different TIN type.

      Note:

      Married Filing Separately (FS-3) taxpayers do not qualify for this credit.

  4. The deduction is allowed up to $25,000 for qualified tips for individuals in traditionally and customarily tipped industries.

  5. The tip income deduction phases out for AGI over $150,000 ($300,000 for FS-2).

  6. Employers and other payers must report, to the employee and IRS, tips paid. Review IRP data to verify the tip deduction information.

  7. When reviewing notices with errors for tip income deduction, ensure the correct TPNC has been applied to the notice. See the table below for TPNCs for tip income deduction including a brief description. See IRM 3.12.3-1, Taxpayer Notice Codes, for the full TPNC wording.

    Taxpayer Notice Code (TPNC) Number Brief Description of the TPNC
    543 We changed the amount of TXI because:

    • You didn’t complete Schedule 1-A, or

    • You didn’t attach Schedule 1-A to your return.
    611 We changed the amount of no tax on tips because:

    • FS-3,

    • ITIN,

    • SSN doesn’t match, or

    • SSN wasn’t issued before the return due date.
    612 We changed the amount of not tax on tips because you are FS-2 and you and your spouse:

    • Have an ITIN,

    • Failed to provide an SSN or the names don’t match, or

    • SSNs weren’t issued before the return due date.
    613 We changed the amount of no tax on tips because it was incorrect.

3.14.1.6.12.2.5 (01-01-2026)
No Tax on Overtime - Overtime Income Deduction (Tax Years 2025-2028)

  1. Effective for tax periods 2025 through 2028, individuals who receive qualified overtime compensation may deduct the pay that exceeds their regular rate of pay (such as the “half” portion of “time-and-a-half” compensation) that is required by the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) and reported on a Form W-2, Form 1099, or other specified statement furnished to the individual.

  2. The deduction is available in addition to itemizing (Schedule A) and non-itemizing (standard deduction) and is claimed on Schedule 1-A.

  3. In addition to the above qualifications, taxpayers must:

    • Have a valid SSN assigned before the due date of the return.

    • File Married Filing Jointly (FS-2) if they are married. If only one taxpayer is claiming the overtime income deduction, only that taxpayer needs to have an SSN; the other taxpayer on an FS-2 return can have a different TIN type.

      Note:

      Married Filing Separately (FS-3) taxpayers do not qualify for this credit.

  4. The maximum annual deduction is $12,500 ($25,000 for joint filers).

  5. The overtime income deduction phases out for taxpayers with modified adjusted gross income over $150,000 ($300,000 for FS-2).

  6. Employers and other payers must report, to the employee and IRS, qualified overtime paid. Review IRP data to verify qualified overtime paid information.

  7. When reviewing notices with errors for overtime income deduction, ensure the correct TPNC has been applied to the notice. See the table below for TPNCs for overtime income deduction including a brief description. See IRM 3.12.3-1, Taxpayer Notice Codes, for the full TPNC wording.

    Taxpayer Notice Code (TPNC) Number Brief Description of the TPNC
    543 We changed the amount of TXI because:

    • You didn’t complete Schedule 1-A, or

    • You didn’t attach Schedule 1-A to your return.
    634 We changed the amount claimed for the No Tax on Overtime Deduction because:

    • FS-3,

    • ITIN,

    • SSN doesn’t match, or

    • SSN wasn’t issued before the return due date.
    635 We changed the amount claimed for the No Tax on Overtime Deduction because it was incorrect.

3.14.1.6.12.2.6 (01-01-2026)
No Tax on Car Loan Interest - Car Loan Interest Deduction (Tax Years 2025-2028)

  1. Effective for tax periods 2025 through 2028, individuals may deduct interest paid on a loan used to purchase a qualified vehicle, provided the vehicle is purchased for personal use and meets other eligibility criteria.

  2. The deduction is available in addition to itemizing (Schedule A) and non-itemizing (standard deduction) and is claimed on Schedule 1-A. The taxpayer must include the vehicle identification number (VIN) of the vehicle on the tax return for any year the deduction is claimed.

    Caution:

    ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡

  3. To qualify the loan must:

    • Have originated after December 31, 2024,

    • Be used to purchase a new vehicle(used vehicles do not qualify)

    • Be for a personal use vehicle (not business or commercial), and

    • Be secured by a lien on the vehicle.

  4. To qualify the vehicle must:

    • Be a car, minivan, van, SUV, pick-up truck, or motorcycle,

    • Be a personal use vehicle,

    • Have a gross vehicle weight rating of less than 14,000 pounds, and

    • Have undergone final assembly in the United States.

  5. The maximum amount of interest deduction allowed is $10,000.

  6. The deduction amount is phased out by $200 for every $1,000 of the taxpayer’s modified AGI is over $100,000 ($200,000 for joint filers).

  7. Lenders must file information returns with the IRS and furnish statements to taxpayers showing the total amount of interest received during the taxable year.

  8. When reviewing notices with errors for car loan interest deduction, ensure the correct TPNC has been applied to the notice. See the table below for TPNCs for car loan interest deduction including a brief description. See IRM 3.12.3-1, Taxpayer Notice Codes, for the full TPNC wording.

    Taxpayer Notice Code (TPNC) Number Brief Description of the TPNC
    543 We changed the amount of TXI because:

    • You didn’t complete Schedule 1-A, or

    • You didn’t attach Schedule 1-A to your return.
    635 We changed the amount claimed as No Tax on Car Loan Interest Deduction because it was incorrect.

3.14.1.6.12.2.7 (01-01-2026)
Charitable Contribution in Adjustments to Income

  1. Charitable contribution for taxpayers who do not itemize their deductions expired December 31, 2021. Tax year 2022 through 2025 taxpayers must claim charitable contributions, or gifts to charity, on Schedule A, Itemized Deductions.

  2. For Tax Year 2021, if the amount on Form 1040, line 12b, is greater than $600 for FS-2 (greater than $300 for all other filing statuses) determine if Schedule A is attached and itemized deductions are claimed on Form 1040, line 12a.

  3. For Tax Year 2020, if the amount on Form 1040, U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, line 10b, is greater than $300 (FSC 3/6, greater than $150), determine if Schedule A is attached and itemized deductions are claimed on Form 1040, U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, line 12. If greater than $300 and Schedule A is not attached or Schedule A is not being used ERS will assign a TPNC 168, review the return accordingly.

  4. For FSC 3 or 6, if the amount on Form 1040, U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, line 10b is greater than $150 and Schedule A is not attached, taxpayers must itemize deductions to claim more than $150 in charitable contributions.

3.14.1.6.12.2.8 (01-01-2026)
Schedule A Errors

  1. Schedule A errors are most often attributed to a taxpayer doing one or more of the following:

    1. Incorrectly totaling the Itemized Deductions.

    2. Incorrectly applying AGI figures from Form 1040, U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, to the Medical and Dental section.

    3. Incorrectly multiplying the AGI by percentages shown in the Medical and Dental section.

    4. Incorrectly limiting the deduction for state and local taxes (SALT)

    5. Omitting any other forms which are required to substantiate certain Itemized Deductions.

    6. Using an incorrect year Schedule A, which would contain incorrect thresholds and percentages.

    7. Forgetting to check the "Itemized Election" box, or checking it in error.

  2. If changes are made to AGI, Schedule A may need to be adjusted.

  3. If an FS-3 taxpayer uses Schedule A figures that are below the Standard Deduction but does not check the "Itemized Election" box, follow TP intent that their spouse also itemizes, and allow the Schedule A amount to stand, despite it being less than the Standard Deduction.

  4. More detailed information as to how ERS handles these determinations can be found in IRM 3.12.3.23.10, Error Code 250 and 550, Taxable Income.

3.14.1.6.12.2.8.1 (01-01-2026)
Schedule A State and Local Tax (SALT)

  1. The passage of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBA) increased the Federal limit, or cap for State & Local Tax (SALT) deduction on the Schedule A, Itemized Deductions, for tax years 2025-2029.

  2. The cap was $10,000 in 2024. The new cap for tax year 2025 is $40,000 for all filing statuses except married filing separately (FS-3), which is $20,000.

  3. The SALT cap is phased out based on Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI). The MAGI phaseout begins at $500,000 and continues to a maximum phase out at $600,000 MAGI.

    Note:

    The SALT MAGI phaseout deduction does not decrease the cap below $10,000.

3.14.1.6.12.3 (01-01-2026)
Earned Income Credit (EIC)

  1. Earned Income Credit (EIC) is a refundable credit available for certain low-income taxpayers who meet earned income, adjusted gross income (AGI), and certain other requirements. EIC greater than the tax liability is refunded to the taxpayer. See IRM 3.14.1.6.12.3.2, EIC - Eligible Individuals, IRM 3.14.1.6.12.3.4 EIC - Qualifying Child Eligibility, and Pub 596 for specific eligibility requirements.

  2. For prior year EIC rules and regulations, and worksheets, refer to EIC worksheets, paper publications, or schedules, for the appropriate tax year.

    Note:

    For tax year 2021 only, the age restriction for taxpayers with no qualified children has been modified. There is no maximum age limit, and the minimum age limit is at least age 19 as of December 31, 2021. The minimum age is 24 for specified students. Qualified former foster youth or qualified homeless youth can check the box on line 27a of Form 1040, U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, and qualify for self EIC at 18 years old.

  3. When EIC has been disallowed during processing, but taxpayer(s) and dependents appear to meet all qualifications, refer to IRM 3.14.1.6.12.5.10, Credit Recertification, for recertification requirements.

  4. Verify Form(s) W-2, 1099, and all other types of earned income. The determined earned income amount will be used to calculate EIC and other eligible credits. See Notice Review IMF National Job Aid 2534-002, EIC: Types of Income, for more information.

    1. Disability income is considered earned income for EIC purposes if the taxpayer is under age 65. Qualified disability income is shown on Form 1099-R, Distributions From Pensions, Annuities, Retirement or Profit-Sharing Plans, IRAs, Insurance Contracts, etc., in Box 2a, with a Distribution Code 3 in Box 7. See IRM 3.12.8.5.33 , Section 06 Document Code 98 Format Code 025, Form 1099-R, Distributions From Pensions, Annuities, Retirement or Profit-Sharing Plans, IRAs, Insurance Contracts, etc., for more Box 7 codes.

    2. Advanced Earned Income Credit, (2010 and prior), was a payment made by employers to employees throughout the year. This amount appears on Form W-2, Box 9, and must be reported on the tax return.

  5. Taxpayers assigned an Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN) cannot receive EIC. To be eligible for the credit, all relevant parties (primary taxpayers, secondary taxpayers, and children) must have valid SSNs issued by the Social Security Administration.

  6. If a taxpayer is eligible to claim EIC, compute the EIC based on any qualifying children that the taxpayer is allowed to claim. Keep the following in mind when reviewing and correcting EIC:

    1. Schedule EIC must be filed with the return to receive Earned Income Credit for qualifying children. If the schedule is not included, disallow the credit.

    2. Until tax year 2021, a Married Filing Separate (FS3) taxpayer could not receive EIC. Beginning in tax year 2021, an FS3 taxpayer can only receive EIC if they attach Schedule EIC and check the box at the top of the form certifying their eligibility to claim the EIC on a separate return.

    3. All other filing statuses regardless of qualifying children may receive EIC if both AGI and earned income are less than the current year limitation. See IRM 3.14.1.6.12.3.2, EIC - Eligible Individuals.

    4. A taxpayer claimed as a dependent on another return is not eligible to receive EIC.

    5. Include the SE Tax deduction when computing earned income. See Pub 596 or Notice Review Job Aid 2534-002 for more information on figuring earned income and examples of earned and investment income.

      Example:

      Schedule C line 31 income of 5,200 has SE Tax of $735. The SE Tax deduction is $367.00. If this is the only income the taxpayer has, the earned income is $4,833.

    6. Adjust EIC cases, when necessary, using guidelines in IRM 3.14.1.7.6, Tax Adjustments.

    7. Prevent the refund from generating when decreasing EIC. See IRM 3.14.1.7.1.1, Refund Intercepts.

    8. For EIC claims of Married Filing Jointly (FS2) with no qualifying child, allow EIC if taxpayer’s age (either primary or secondary) is within age guidelines and other qualifications are met.

  7. Review all EIC cases according to the following:

    • IRM 3.14.1.6.1, General Review Procedures

    • IRM 3.14.1.6.12.1, Items to Review on All Math Error Notices

    • IRM 3.14.1.7.8, Notice Disposition

  8. Path Act applies to this credit See IRM 3.14.1.6.1.1.1, Protecting Americans from Tax Hikes.

3.14.1.6.12.3.1 (01-01-2026)
EIC - Use of Prior Year Earned Income (PYEI) to Compute EIC

  1. Qualified individuals may use their Prior Year Earned Income (PYEI), instead of their earned income for the taxable year.

  2. The legislative allowance for disaster zone relief requires the qualified individual use their prior year earned income to figure EIC. The qualified individual must use the same calculation to compute the ACTC credit (presuming the eligibility to claim both exists). This stipulation only applies to individuals whose main home was in:

    • the Hurricane Harvey disaster area on August 23, 2017,

    • the Hurricane Irma disaster area on September 4, 2017,

    • the Hurricane Maria disaster area on September 16, 2017,

    • the California wildfire disaster area on October 8, 2017,

    • a Presidentially declared disaster that occurred in 2018 or 2019, but before December 21, 2019 issue or request.


    Exception: The Taxpayer Certainty and Disaster Tax Relief Act of 2020 (TY 2020) allows the use of prior year income for EITC and/or ACTC. Taxpayers are not required to use the same calculation for each credit.
    Caution: If the taxpayer is using PYEI to compute current year EIC, do not include current year wages, Schedule C, Schedule F (partnership or small corporation) or line 21 earned income in computation.

  3. Tax Year 201912 - Tax Year 201712 Prior Year Earned Income (PYEI) is notated with the taxpayer’s earnings next to Form 1040, line 18b (TY 18, line 17; TY 17, line 66a and line 67; Form 1040A, line 42a, and line 43). Taxpayers are instructed to also use their PYEI amount on Schedule 8812, line 6a (TY 17, Schedule 8812, line 4).

    Note:

    Taxpayers who elect to use their prior year earned income to figure their EIC must use the same earned income calculation for ACTC on their TY 2019 - TY 2017 tax return.

  4. Tax Year 2020, PYEI (Prior Year Earned Income) is notated with the taxpayer’s earnings next to Form 1040, line 28. TY 20, taxpayers may elect to use their 2019 earned income to compute EIC and/or ACTC.

  5. For tax year 2021, taxpayers could elect to use their 2019 earned income only if their 2019 earned income was more than their 2021 earned income.

  6. Verify that the EIC credit was correctly figured using the Prior Year Earned Income. If the credit is incorrect, adjust the account accordingly using CC REQ54 with:

    1. The appropriate Blocking Series, Source Code, Reason Code, Hold Code and Item Reference Codes for an EIC adjustment.

    2. Activity: "EIC-PYEI."

    3. Remarks: "TP error figuring EIC using Prior Year Earned Income" (PYEI).

3.14.1.6.12.3.2 (01-01-2026)
EIC – Eligible Individuals

  1. To determine if an individual is eligible to claim EIC, follow the chart below for specific requirements. See (2) below for AGI and investment limitations.

    If the taxpayer Then the taxpayer is eligible if all the following apply
    Has a valid SSN (For EIC purposes, an SSN obtained by an alien so that they can receive a federally funded benefit for which they are eligible is not a valid SSN) Both taxpayers must have a valid SSN on a joint return. Caution: An ITIN is not an SSN. A Social Security Card issued solely so that the taxpayer (or spouse) could receive a federally funded benefit also does not qualify. This type of SSN will state "Not Valid for Employment Purposes."
    Has a filing status other than Married Filing Separately (FS3 or FS6) Both taxpayers must have a valid SSN on a joint return. Caution: An ITIN is not an SSN. A Social Security Card issued solely so that the taxpayer (or spouse) could receive a federally funded benefit also does not qualify. This type of SSN will state "Not Valid for Employment Purposes."
    Has a filing status of Married Filing Separately (FS-3 or FS-6) Tax year must be 2021 or later and MFS taxpayers who meet certain requirements must indicate by checking a box on Schedule EIC. If the box is checked EIC is allowed with valid SSNs.
    Has investment income less than current year limitations Investment income includes:

    • The sum of all positive entries on lines for taxable and non-taxable interest, ordinary dividends, and all capital gains.

    • Income from rental of personal property on Form 1040, U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, other income, minus SE Tax deduction 1040, reported on adjustments to income.

    • Royalty income on Schedule E, minus the related Schedule E expenses.

    • Passive Income minus Passive Losses Schedule E, lines 29a(h), 34a(d), and 39 minus 29b(g), 34b(c), and 40. Caution: If NPA is noted or if both royalty and rental income are included in the amount on line 26 the computer cannot accurately compute investment income

    • If present, when figuring investment income amount, the amount on Form 1040/SR, line 6 will be reduced by any positive amount from Form 1040/SR, line 6 will be reduced by any positive amount from Form 4797, line 7. If no amount is present on Form 4797, line 7 then the amount on Form 1040, line 6 will be reduced by any positive amount on Form 4797, line 9.

    • See Publication 596 or the Notice Review Job Aid 2534-002 for examples of investment income.
    Has earned income of at least one dollar Taxpayer qualifies if all other eligibility requirements are met. See Publication 596 or Notice Review Job Aid 2534-002 for examples of earned income and investment income.
    Is not a qualifying child of another person See Publication 596 or Notice Review Job Aid 2534-002.
    Has no qualifying children

    • Both the Earned Income and AGI must be less than the return year limitation

    • The taxpayer (either primary or secondary spouse if married filing jointly) must be at least age 25 and under age 65 as of December 31st of the tax year

      Exception:

      For tax year 2021 only, the age restriction for taxpayers with no qualified children was modified. There was no maximum age limit, and the minimum age limit was at least age 19 as of December 31, 2021. The minimum age is 24 for specified students. Qualified former foster youth or qualified homeless youth can check the box on line 27a of Form 1040 and qualify for self EIC at 18 years old.

    • The taxpayer (and either primary or secondary spouse if married filing jointly) cannot be claimed as a dependent on someone else’s tax return

    • The taxpayer must have lived in the United States for more than half of the tax year

    Exception:

    U.S. military personnel stationed outside the U.S. on extended active duty are considered to live in the U.S. during that duty period.

    Note:

    Taxpayers whose qualifying children do not have valid SSNs are considered to have qualifying children for purposes of determining eligibility for EIC (no age requirement). The children cannot be claimed for EIC but the taxpayer can still qualify for EIC without children.
    Has one or more qualifying children The AGI must be less than the return year limitations and Schedule EIC must be attached. See AGI information below.

  2. In addition to the eligibility requirements above, taxpayers must also be under the maximum threshold for AGI and investment income. See below for the limits for tax year, filing status, and whether or not the taxpayer is claiming children for EIC.
    2025

    • $19,104 ($26,214 married filing jointly) if no qualifying child

    • $50, 434 ($57,554 for married filing jointly) if one qualifying child

    • $57,310 ($64,430 for married filing jointly) if two qualifying children

    • $61,555 ($68,675 for married filing jointly) if three or more qualifying children

    • maximum investment income $11,950


    2024

    • $18,591 ($25,511 for married filing jointly) if no qualifying child

    • $49,084 ($56,004 for married filing jointly) if one qualifying child

    • $55,768 ($62,688 for married filing jointly) if two qualifying children

    • $59,899 ($66,819 for married filing jointly) if three or more qualifying children

    • maximum investment income $11,600


    2023

    • $17,640 ($24,210 for married filing jointly) if no qualifying child

    • $46,560 ($53,120 for married filing jointly) if one qualifying child

    • $52,918 ($59,478 for married filing jointly) if two qualifying children

    • $56,838 ($63,398 for married filing jointly) if three or more qualifying children

    • maximum investment income $11,000


    2022

    • $16,480 ($22,610 for married filing jointly) if no qualifying child

    • $43,492 ($49,622 for married filing jointly) if one qualifying child

    • $49,399 ($55,529 for married filing jointly) if two qualifying children

    • $53,057 ($59,187 for married filing jointly) if three or more qualifying children

    • maximum investment income $10,300

3.14.1.6.12.3.3 (11-12-2019)
EIC – Non-Qualifying Conditions

  1. The following conditions result in a taxpayer not qualifying for EIC:

    Non-Qualifying Conditions. Do not allow EIC if any of the following conditions exist on a tax return:

    • If Schedule EIC is not included when children or dependents are claimed for EIC.

    • Earned income or AGI are equal to or more than the current limitations.

    • The taxpayer lived outside of the U.S. for half the year or more.

    • Amish, Mennonite, or "Exempt due to Form 4029" is noted on or near the EIC line. (Form 4029 , Application for Exemption From Social Security and Medicare Taxes and Waiver of Benefits)

    • Form 2555, Foreign Earned Income, or Form 2555–EZ, Foreign Income, is included with the tax return.

    • A "No" , a dash ("–" ), or a zero ("0" ) appear on the EIC line.

    • The taxpayer (or spouse if married filing jointly) does not have a valid SSN.

    • The taxpayer (or spouse, if married filing jointly) has a valid SSN, but that SSN was issued solely so that the taxpayer (or spouse) could receive a federally funded benefit (Social Security card states, “Not valid for employment.”).

    • Does not have at least $1.00 of earned income. Self-Employment non-passive income is considered earned income if the taxpayer pays Self-Employment Tax, or the Self-Employment income is under $434.
      Exception: For church employee income, less than $108.28. See IRM 3.14.1.6.12.1.4 , Self- Employment (SE) Tax Computation – TPNC 580, for assessing Self-Employment tax due to EIC claims with or without an ERS assigned TPNC 580.

3.14.1.6.12.3.4 (01-01-2026)
EIC – Qualifying Child Eligibility

  1. Use the following table to help determine a child's eligibility to qualify for EIC:

    Criteria Specifics of the Criteria that must be met for qualifying child(ren)
    Specific relation to the taxpayer The taxpayer's:

    • child

    • adopted child

    • stepchild

    • brother, stepbrother, half-brother

    • sister, stepsister, half-sister

    • or a descendent of any of these relatives

    • or be an eligible foster child

    An eligible foster child is defined as:

    • Any child placed with the taxpayer by an authorized placement agency; or by judgment, decree, or any court of competent jurisdiction and lived with the taxpayer for more than half the year

    Note:

    Parents, grandparents, aunts, uncles, cousins, boy/girlfriends or their children, or any other persons not defined above, are not qualifying dependents for EIC eligibility.

    Note:

    A married child cannot be a qualifying child unless the taxpayer is entitled to claim a dependency exemption for the child or would be entitled were it not for IRC Section 152(e)(2) or IRC Section 152(e)(4), which provides for the assignment of a dependent to an ex-spouse.
    Age limitations

    • 18 or younger

    • Must be younger than the taxpayer claiming the credit. Note: For TY 09 and later except in the case of permanently and totally disabled children, EIC will be allowed only for a child who is younger than the taxpayer. The child must have been born in a year after the taxpayer's year of birth. Children born in the same year as the taxpayer are not considered younger than the taxpayer. If the filing status is joint, the EIC will be allowed if one taxpayer is older than the child.

    • 23 or younger and a full-time student (at least five months) at an accredited institution of higher learning or taking an on-farm training program through a school or a state, county, or local government agency.

      Example:

      High school, junior college, college, university, or a technical, trade, or mechanical school. Correspondence schools and on-the-job training courses do not count.

    • Any age, if totally and permanently disabled at any time during the tax year

      Note:

      The disability must be a physical or mental condition that prevents the person from engaging in any substantial gainful activity.
    Reside with the taxpayer

    • An eligible foster child must have lived with the taxpayer for more than half the year. Check the "Number of Months" line on Schedule EIC

    • A child who was born or died during the year, is considered to have lived in the home the entire year

    • Temporary absences because of school, vacation, or medical care count as time living with the taxpayer

    • The taxpayer and child must live in the United States

      Exception:

      U.S. military personnel stationed outside the U.S. on extended active duty are considered to live in the U.S. during that duty period.

      Note:

      Exceptions apply to certain cases, such as children of divorced parents, or for kidnapped children. See Publication 501 for more information.

3.14.1.6.12.3.5 (01-01-2026)
EIC – Non-Qualifying Conditions for Children

  1. To qualify for EIC children must have a valid SSN and Schedule EIC must be attached to the tax return. Do not allow EIC if the child:

    1. Does not have a valid SSN (For EIC purposes, an SSN obtained by an alien so that they can receive a federally funded benefit for which they are eligible is not a valid SSN)

    2. Does not have an SSN, and "applied for" , "SSA 205(c)" , or "NRA" is entered in lieu of an SSN

    3. Has an Adoption Taxpayer Identification Number (ATIN) or ITIN in lieu of an SSN

    4. The qualifying child/dependent must live with the taxpayers for more than half of the relevant year.
      Exception: A child who was born and died in the same year is considered to have lived in the home the entire year. Taxpayers must provide documentation in the form of birth certificate, or hospital records that includes all information. Proof of live birth is required to receive the credit.

  2. Qualifying children who do not have valid SSNs are not considered qualifying children for purposes of computing the amount of the EIC. However, the taxpayer whose qualifying children do not have SSNs is treated as having qualifying children for purposes of determining eligibility without children for EIC. For example, a taxpayer whose qualifying children have ITINs would not need to meet the age requirements applicable to taxpayers without qualifying children.

3.14.1.6.12.4 (01-01-2026)
Dependent TIN-Related Errors

  1. A TIN is a taxpayer identification number. This general term includes SSN's, ITIN's, ATIN's, and IRSN's. Valid SSN's, ATIN's, and ITIN's. Not all TIN types qualify for all credit types.

  2. The most common areas of the return affected by dependent TIN errors are:

    • Filing Status IRM 3.14.1.6.1.1.11

    • Credit for other dependents (ODC) IRM 3.14.1.6.12.5.5

    • Child and Dependent Care Credit IRM 3.14.1.6.12.5.9

    • Child Tax Credit (CTC) IRM 3.14.1.6.12.5.2

    • Additional Child Tax Credit (ACTC) IRM 3.14.1.6.12.5.6

    • Earned Income Credit (EIC) IRM 3.14.1.6.12.3

    • Education Credits IRM 3.14.1.6.12.5.7

      Note:

      See each section for specific TIN requirements for each credit.

  3. If a TIN is missing or invalid, search the return, attachments, and forms and schedules, for the missing TIN, or a correct TIN, before denying any corresponding credits.

3.14.1.6.12.5.1 (03-10-2025)
Health Coverage Tax Credit (HCTC)

  1. To qualify for the Health Coverage Tax Credit (HCTC), the taxpayer must be under 66 years of age at the end of the tax year and be an eligible recipient of either the Trade Adjustment Assistance (TAA), alternative (ATAA), or Pension Benefit Guarantee Corporation (PBGC), and must have paid premiums to a qualified Health Care plan. See IRM 3.12.3.31.9.6, Form 8885, Health Coverage Tax Credit (HCTC) TY21-TY02 only (EC 358) or IRM 21.6.3.4.2.9.1, Health Coverage Tax Credit (HCTC) - Eligibility, for additional information.

  2. If taxpayers are claiming the HCTC, they should check the appropriate box in the Payments section on Form 1040, U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, enter the amount claimed, and attach Form 8885, Health Coverage Tax Credit (HCTC).

  3. Determine if the taxpayer is entitled to HCTC based on the following:

    ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡

    • Add TC 971/172

    • Post the HCTC with TC 766 CRN 250

    • Reverse the eligibility indicator with a TC 972/172.

    If there is an Unallowable Code 89 on the account do not adjust the return.

    If there is no Unallowable Code 89 on the account, the HCTC did not post and the HCTC claimed was above tolerance. See the work leader.

3.14.1.6.12.5.2 (01-01-2026)
Child Tax Credit (CTC)

  1. Child Tax Credit (CTC) was instituted in 1998. CTC is a credit applied against tax (TC 150 or TC 290) for taxpayers with a qualifying child(ren). Age restrictions apply and vary by year. The credit is also phased out as AGI increases. See the table below and Pub 17 for more information.

  2. To qualify for the credit, the child must:

    • Be claimed as a dependent on the return,

    • Be the taxpayer's son, daughter, stepchild, eligible foster child, brother, sister, stepbrother, stepsister, or a descendant of any of them,

    • Be under age 17 at the end of the calendar year,

      Exception:

      The child must be under age 18 for tax year 2021 only.

    • Be a U.S. citizen, U.S. national, or a resident of the United States,

    • Have lived with the taxpayer more than half of the tax year,

    • Have not provided over half of their own support for the tax year.

  3. For tax year 2025 and later, in addition to the qualifying child having a valid SSN assigned on or before the return due date (no extensions), the taxpayer claiming the qualifying child must have a valid SSN issued on or before the due of the return (no extensions) to claim the CTC and ACTC. In the case of a joint return (FS-2), one of the taxpayers, either the primary or the secondary must have a valid SSN (the other parent can have an ITIN). Taxpayers with valid ITINs continue to be eligible for the ODC. See IRM 3.14.1.6.12.5.5, Credit for Other Dependents (ODC) for more information.

  4. For tax year 2018 and later, a qualifying child for CTC must have a valid SSN assigned by the return due date or extended return due date, if a valid extension was filed.

  5. For tax years 2017 and prior, a valid ITIN or SSN was allowed for one or all the following primary and secondary (if joint return), and the child(ren) to claim CTC. The maximum CTC for 2017 was $1,000 per child.

  6. Advance Child tax Credit payments were early payments from the IRS of 50 percent of the estimated amount of the Child Tax Credit that taxpayers could claim on their 2021 tax return during the 2022 filing season. IRM 3.14.1.6.12.5.3, Advance Child Tax Credit (CTC), for more information.

  7. Follow the table below for CTC by tax year, maximum age, allowable TIN type by year (child and taxpayer), and maximum AGI allowed before phasing out of the credit.

    Note:

    A valid SSN must be assigned on or before the due date of the tax return for a child to qualify for CTC. Before 2025, extension dates apply.

    Tax Year Amount of CTC Maximum Age Child TIN Allowed? Primary TIN Allowed? Secondary TIN Allowed? Maximum AGI Before Credit Phase Out Begins
    2025 $2,200 16 SSN only SSN

    Exception:

    For FS-2 only, one ITIN is allowed but one taxpayer must have an SSN either the primary or secondary.

    		 SSN

    Exception:

    For FS-2 only, one ITIN is allowed but one taxpayer must have an SSN either the primary or secondary.

    • $400,000(FS-2)

    • $200,000 all other filers
    2024 $2,000 16 SSN only ITIN or SSN ITIN or SSN

    • $400,000(FS2)

    2023 $2,000 16 SSN only ITIN or SSN ITIN or SSN

    • $200,000 all other filers
