3.14.1.6.14.2 (01-01-2026)
$10 Million or More Refund Transcripts

  1. Any refund of $10 (ten) million dollars or more must be issued as a manual refund.

  2. Accounts that generate this transcript should be worked by the leads within 24 hours to minimize the amount of overpayment interest. If the refund should be released, Notice Review must request the manual refund using the IAT Manual Refund Tool and route to Accounting per IRM 3.14.1.6.6.3, Preparing and Monitoring Manual Refunds — Form 5792 and CC RFUNDR.

  3. Verify any unclaimed payments.

  4. Review for possible Identity Theft (IDT). The following items are potential IDT indicators:

    • Withholding claimed is less than what is on IRPTRL for the taxpayer (which keeps the amount under tolerances)

    • Direct deposit is claimed when not claimed in prior years

    • Taxpayer filed an extension (TC 460) in the current and prior years, paid a substantial Form 4868, Application for Automatic Extension of Time to File U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, (extension) payment (TC 670 matching the DLN of the TC 460), but did not claim the payment on the posted return.

    • TC 460 posts after the TC 150.

3.14.1.6.14.3 (01-01-2026)
Million $ Refund Transcripts

  1. Accounts with overpayment amounts between $1 million and less than $10 Million will appear as a $1 million Refund Transcript.

  2. Systemic refunds will generate(TC 846) for refunds under $10 million, unless a manual refund is required (certain freeze codes).

  3. Accounts that appear as this transcript will have the refund temporarily frozen TC 570 with "55555" blocking series.

  4. Accounts that appear as this transcript should be worked by the lead or SME expeditiously to minimize the amount of overpayment interest.

  5. Verify any unclaimed payments and look for possible Identity Theft (IDT). If the following conditions are identified, suspend the case(stopping the refund)and forward to a manager or lead for review:

    • Withholding claimed is less than what is on IRPTRL for taxpayer (which keeps the amount under our tolerances)

    • Direct deposit claimed when not claimed in prior years

    • Taxpayer has filed for an extension (TC 460) in current and prior years and pays a substantial 4868 payment not claimed on current return.

    • TC 460 posts after the TC 150.

3.14.1.6.14.4 (01-01-2026)
Refund S Transcripts

  1. Master File generates Refund S transcripts for an overpayment that may result in a refund being issued in a cycle other than the posting cycle of the TC 150. Review the posted transactions of the tax module from the current cycle backwards (newest to oldest) to determine the cause of the overpayment.
    Caution: Look for possible Identity Theft (IDT) and suspend the case, stop the refund, and forward for manager/lead to review if these conditions are present:

    1. Withholding claimed is less than what is on IRPTRL for taxpayer (which keeps the amount under our tolerances),

    2. Change in patterns, when direct deposit was not claimed in prior years,

    3. TC 460 filed, but substantial 4868 payment not claimed on current return,

    4. Extension (TC 460) filed after TC 150 posted.

  2. Research documents, images, and case notes available through AMS.

    Note:

    If a payment is in question, review AMS and EUP for amended returns.

  3. Allow the refund (standard release refund in AMS) if:

    1. Taxpayer submitted two TC 670 payments: 2nd notice sent before the 1st payment posted, and the taxpayer paid the 2nd notice unaware of the offset of the 1st payment.

    2. TP submitted two TC 670 payments, one is a levy: 2nd notice sent before the 1st payment posted, and the taxpayer paid both.

    3. A TC 640 or TC 670 is refunding and was released by a TC 290 .00, blocking Series 55 or 65 (Underreporter Adjustment).

    4. The refund was released by a TC 300 .00 with Disposal Code 01 or 02 (no change in tax liability or refundable credit).

      Exception:

      Prevent the refund from generating if Disposal Code 01, blocking series 700 or 790 (additional tax assessed) is used.

  4. Research and possibly prevent refunds from generating under any of the following circumstances:

    Circumstances Guidelines
    Two TC 670 non-levy payments, same amounts posted to the module. Verify payments in RTR or CC EFTPSE. Check for a possible duplicate credit. If the reason for the second TC 670 cannot be determined, Suspend for Additional Research in AMS. Send a 1687C letter. Follow IRM 3.14.1.7.4 Notice Review Sent Taxpayer Correspondence-Reply and No Reply Procedures.
    TC 670 payment is refunding after TC 846 has posted. If the payment was sent in with an amendment return (1040X) Check AMS Alerts or EUP to review the 1040X (if available). Hold the refund for the pending amended return.

    Exception:

    If a 105C letter is notated on TXMOD or ENMOD for the transcript module release the refund. A 105C letter is a 1040X disallowance letter sent to the taxpayer.
    TC 670 payment is refunding with a Designated Payment Code (DPC) 64 Verify the payment in RTR or CC EFTPSE to look for an indication of an IRC 965 payment. Review IMFOLM for MFT 30 Tax Periods 201712 and 201812 to determine if a credit transfer to a different module is needed for IRC 965 Liability. Prevent the refund from generating if a credit transfer is needed. See IRM 3.14.1.6.9.16.4, Command Code IMFOL IRC 965.
    TC 670 payment is refunding after TC 846 has posted, and the reason for the payment cannot be determined. Suspend for Additional Research in AMS. Look up documents/images/case notes available through AMS, to verify taxpayer’s intent. Verify payments in RTR or CC EFTPSE. Check for a possible misapplied ES payment for the next tax year. If the taxpayer did not claim the payment on their return and the payment module cannot be determined, correspond for the questionable payment by sending a Letter 1687C- Unidentified Payment/Credit. If the taxpayer does not respond to the correspondence and payment cannot be determined, refer to IRM 3.14.1.7.4 Notice Review Sent Taxpayer Correspondence-Reply and No Reply Procedures, IRM 3.14.1.6.8, Excess Collections (XSF), and Unidentified Remittance (URF) Files.
    TC 670 payment submitted is for TC 460 extension If the amount of payment is unreasonable, or if it’s posted after the TC 846, verify the extension through AMS or RTR if available. If Identity Theft is suspected, suspend the case, stop the refund, and forward for manager/lead to review. See, IRM 3.14.1.6.9.5 RIVO (Return Integrity and Verification Operation) for more information.
    TC 670 is refunding (usually Key 041, 045, or 052 Transcripts), and an Audit Information Management System (AIMS) indicator (Exam indicator on , CC TXMOD) is present indicating a tax increase Prevent the refund from generating. Close the case using Closing Action Module Situation Resolved without selecting any transactions in the window in AMS. Indicate in the case notes that the case was closed to Exam.
    Refund was released by a TC 300 .00 with disposal code 01 and blocking series 700-790 Close the case using Closing Action Module Situation Resolved without selecting any transactions in the window in AMS. Indicate in the case notes the case was closed to Exam.
    Refund was release by a TC 300 .00 and the disposal code is not 01, 02, 20, 21, or 22. Close the case Module Situation Resolved without selecting any transactions in the window in AMS. Indicate in the case notes the case was closed to Exam.
    Two TC 610 payments posted, and one is refunding. Check for a possible duplicate credit by verifying payments in RTR or CC EFTPSE. Review for vouchers, notes in the check memo line, and for timeliness for a future module. Also, carefully review IDRS and AMS history notes for a possible bad check. One check may have been sent to replace a payment the taxpayer knows will not clear the bank. If the research above has been performed, and no indication of a bad check can be found, release the refund.
    IDRS shows a pending tax increase or credit decrease Check for possible duplicate adjustment. If the adjustment appears reasonable, prevent the refund from generating. Close the case Module Situation Resolved. Indicate in the case notes a pending transaction is present.
    A TC 640 (AUR) or TC 680 amount matches the overpayment amount Prevent the refund from generating. Close the case Module Situation Resolved to hold the payment until Underreporter can complete review of the module and assess more taxes if required.

    Exception:

    Allow the refund to generate if the TC 640 or TC 680 was released by a TC 290 for .00, blocking Series 55 or 65 (Underreporter Adjustment).
    A TC 640 or TC 670 is refunding and the reason for the payment cannot be determined. Use RTR or EFTPSE to research the payment. If the taxpayer did not claim the payment on their return and the payment module cannot be determined, correspond for the questionable payment by sending a Letter 1687C- Unidentified Payment/Credit. If the taxpayer does not respond to the correspondence and payment cannot be determined, refer to IRM 3.14.1.7.4 Notice Review Sent Taxpayer Correspondence-Reply and No Reply Procedures and IRM 3.14.1.6.8, Excess Collections (XSF) and Unidentified Remittance (URF) Files.
    A TC 922 and a TC 670 or TC 640 posted to the module with no tax increase (TC 922 is an indication that Automated Underreporter (AUR) is reviewing the module) Review TXMOD for TC 922 closing codes. If there is an open AUR Control Base, and the processing code indicates that the case is still being reviewed then Close to URP/AUR in AMS.

    Exception:

    If the TC 922 processing code listed on TXMOD is 70-73 or 91- 93, or there is a second TC 922 with processing code 87, release the refund using Standard Release Refund in AMS.
    A TC 766 (refundable credit) is being released by a TC 577 that is generated by TC 421 with Disposal Code 29 (missing return) Close Module Situation Resolved without selecting any transactions in AMS. Hold the refund and indicate in the case notes a pending transaction is present.
    Prior year credit elect is refunding, a TC 150 posted to the next year, and penalties, additions to tax, and interest have accrued on that module that will abate when the credit elect posts. Check for debt indicators for possible TOP Offset using CC INOLES, see IRM 3.14.1.6.4.3, Treasury Offset Program (TOP) Offsets — TC 898/899 for more information. If no debt indicators are found close Module Situation Resolved in AMS. Perform the credit elect credit transfer using the Credit Transfer IAT Tool, see IRM 3.14.1.7.7, Credit Transfers for more information. If debt indicators are found close Standard Release Refund.
    Prior year credit elect is refunding, a TC 150 posted to the next period, and the module has a debit balance Close Standard Release Refund. The refund will be systemically applied to IRS and other Federal debt.
    Prior year credit elect is refunding, the credit is claimed on the next year, and the credit elect field of that year is inconsistent. Check for debt indicators for possible TOP Offset using CC INOLES, see IRM 3.14.1.6.4.3, Treasury Offset Program (TOP) Offsets — TC 898/899 for more information. If debt indicators are found close Standard Release Refund. If no debt indicators are found close Module Situation Resolved in AMS. Before performing the credit elect credit transfer verify the taxpayer intent by reviewing AMS history notes and viewing the return on IDRS or by other electronic means. Once the correct credit elect amount is verified transfer using the IAT Credit Transfer Tool. See IRM 3.14.1.7.7, Credit Transfers for more information.
    If a TC 666/667 (systemic transfer) and a TC 670/672 payment has posted resulting in a refund. Research the secondary accounts to look for balance due status. If a module is in balance due status, close Module Situation Resolved in AMS. Transfer the TC 670 back to originating spousal account with a balance due.

    Note:

    Both payments will be transferred with the same date. Check RTR or EFTPSE to validate.

    See IRM 3.14.1.6.11.6, ES Spousal Freeze D- Code for more information.

3.14.1.6.14.5 (01-01-2026)
Refund E Transcripts

  1. Master File generates a Refund E transcript when the overpayment is $100 or more than the amount claimed by the taxpayer and there is no math error, payment discrepancy, or duplicate return (–A freeze)
    Caution: Look for possible IDT and suspend the case by stopping the refund for manager to review for potential IDT if these conditions are present:

    1. Withholding claimed is less than what is on IRPTRL for taxpayer (which keeps the amount under our tolerances),

    2. Change in patterns, such as changing to direct deposit, which was not claimed in prior years,

    3. TC 460 filed, but substantial 4868 payment not claimed on current return,

    4. Extension (TC 460) filed after TC 150 posted.

  2. Research documents, images, and case notes available through AMS.

    Note:

    If a payment is in question review AMS and EUP for amended returns.

  3. Allow the refund (standard release refund in AMS) if:

    1. Wrong line/transcription error: TC 610 payment was identified /transcribed on the wrong line of the return.

    2. Transferred incorrectly: The overpayment was caused by transposed figures in the payment balance due amount.

    3. Overpayment was caused by the difference in penalty and interest computation between taxpayer and IRS figures: Check page two (R2) of Form 1040/RTVUE and verify any attachments.

    4. Math Error: The taxpayer added the ES Penalty amount twice into the amount owed, when figuring the payment with return (TC 610).

    5. Taxpayer received two CP notices and paid twice, unaware of the offset by the first payment. Look for a TC 700 or TC 716 with an additional TC 670 refunding.


    When an overpayment should be refunded, close the case using Closing Action Standard-Release Refund in AMS.

  4. If a refund transcript generated because the refund does not match the taxpayer figures due to a required First-Time Home Buyer repayment, send a Letter 544C with the following information:

    Add paragraphs I and Q

    For paragraph I type the following verbiage in the open paragraph: The refund you expected on your Federal tax return has been reduced by the amount of the repayment installment due for the First-Time Home Buyer Credit you received in 2008. The installment payment should have been claimed as an addition to tax on your return. No further action is required on your part to correct the account.

  5. Research and possibly prevent the refund from generating under any of the following circumstances:

    1. A TC 640 or TC 670 is refunding and the reason for the payment cannot be determined. Use RTR or EFTPSE to research the payment. If the taxpayer did not claim the payment on their return and the payment module cannot be determined, correspond for the questionable payment and send Letter 1687C. If the taxpayer does not respond to the correspondence and payment cannot be determined, refer to IRM 3.14.1.6.8 Excess Collections (XSF) and Unidentified Remittance (URF) Files.

    2. The refunding amount is a TC 670 payment submitted with an Extension of Time to File (TC 460). If the amount is not reasonable or if the extension posted after the return, verify the extension.

    3. Prior year credit elect is refunding, a TC 150 posted to the next year, and penalties, additions to tax, and interest have accrued on that module that will abate when the credit elect posts. Close the case using Closing Action "Credit Transfer Needed" and select appropriate transaction(s) in the window in AMS or perform necessary transactions outside of AMS and close using Module Situation resolved.

    4. Prior year credit elect is refunding, a TC 150 posted to the next period, and the module has a debit balance. Close the case using Closing Action "Credit Transfer Needed" and select appropriate transaction(s) in the window in AMS.

    5. Prior year credit elect is refunding, the credit is claimed on the next year, and the Credit Elect field of that year is significant. Refer to IRM 3.14.1.6.4.1, Credit Elect – TC 836/716 or TC 830/710.

    6. A future year ES voucher amount is refunding. The TC 610 amount overpaid the account by an amount (approximately) equal to one ES payment for the following year (of the current year’s tax liability).

    7. A TC 610 payment substantially overpaid the module but does not match any amount on the return and does not appear to be intended for the next tax period. Look for any pending debit action for which the overpayment may be intended. Check other modules on the taxpayer’s account for debit balances that match the overpayment.

    8. There is an unsubstantiated refundable credit (TC 766 — other than withholding or ES payments) or the taxpayer entered total credits on the wrong line and the amount was transcribed as a TC 766. Watch for double credit situations.

    9. There is a Dishonored Check (TC 611, TC 641, TC 661, or TC 671) pending. Prevent the refund from generating. Close the case using Closing Action "Module Situation Resolved" without selecting any transactions in the window in AMS. Indicate in the case notes a dishonored check is present.

  6. The following table defines the transcript name by "key" numeric extension and criteria for Master File to generate a Refund-E transcript.

3.14.1.6.14.6 (04-17-2024)
Other Refund Transcripts

  1. Master File generates a third type of Refund Transcript, which is when an overpayment differs by $200 or more from the overpayment claimed by the taxpayer, and there is no math error or estimated tax payment discrepancy.

  2. Look for possible IDT. Suspend case (stopping the refund) for manager or lead to review for potential IDT if these conditions are present:

    • ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡

    • direct deposit claimed when not claimed in prior years

    • taxpayer has filed for extension (TC 460) in current and prior years and pays a substantial 4868 payment (TC 670 with DLN matching the TC 460)

    • extension 4868 posts after a return

  3. Research documents, images, and case notes available through AMS.

    Note:

    If a payment is in question review AMS and EUP for amended returns.

  4. Allow the refund under any of the following circumstances:

    1. For Key 50, if there are no transcription or posting errors and withholding is accurate.

    2. The amount of the TC 610 payment is an amount found on any line of the return or attached schedules, meaning that the taxpayer used the wrong line for tax due.

    3. The overpayment was caused by transposed figures in the payment balance due amount.

    4. The refunding amount is due to a difference in the taxpayer’s penalty and interest computations. Check page two of Form 1040 and verify any attachments.

    5. The taxpayer added the ES Penalty amount twice into the amount owed, when figuring the payment with return (TC 610).

    6. The refund is caused by a TC 670 intended to pay a previous taxpayer notice (see notice history on the IDRS tax module) and the taxpayer is unaware of an offset that had either satisfied the module or reduced its balance. Look for a TC 700 or TC 706 with a subsequent TC 670 refunding.

    When an overpayment should be refunded, close the case using Closing Action Standard-Release Refund in AMS.

  5. Research and possibly prevent the refund from generating under any of the following circumstances:

    1. A Key 50, if there are transcription or posting errors and/or withholding is inaccurate.

    2. A TC 640 or TC 670 is refunding and the reason for the payment cannot be determined. Use RTR or EFTPSE to research the payment. If the taxpayer did not claim the payment on their return and the payment module cannot be determined, correspond for the questionable payment and send Letter 1687C- Unidentified Payment/Credit. If the taxpayer does not respond to the correspondence and payment cannot be determined, refer to IRM 3.14.1.6.8, Excess Collections (XSF) and Unidentified Remittance (URF) Files.

    3. A TC 670 payment submitted with an Extension of Time to File (TC 460) is refunding. If the amount is not reasonable or if the extension posted after the return, verify the extension.

    4. A prior year credit elect is refunding, a TC 150 is posted to the next year, and the UNAPPLD-CR-ELECT> field on TXMODA contains an amount; review INOLES for a debt indicator before performing a Credit Transfer. If Married Filing Jointly (FS2) review INOLES for the primary and secondary TIN. If INOLES field DEBT IND is N (no debt), and interest and penalties will abate when the credit elect posts, or the credit elect needs to be moved forward multiple years, move the unapplied credit elect amount using the IAT credit transfer tool. If the INOLES debt indicator is not N (I, IRS debt; F, other Federal debt; B, both IRS and other Federal debt) do not perform a credit transfer. For more information see IRM 3.14.1.7.7, Credit Transfers. If performing a credit transfer, close the case Module Situation Resolved; if not performing a credit transfer, close the case Standard Release Refund. IDRS will offset any overpayment as needed when a debt indicator is present.

    5. A prior year credit elect is refunding, a TC 150 is posted to the next period, and the next module has a debit balance. Close Standard Release Refund. IDRS will offset any overpayment as needed when a debt indicator is present.

    6. A future year ES payment is on the transcript module and that is the amount refunding. The amount overpaid the account by an approximately one ES payment for the following year (of the current year’s tax liability).

      Reminder:

      If the payment was misapplied to the current year but is intended as a future year ES payment, the payment may have posted to the transcript module as a TC 610 or TC 670. If the payment will be moved to the future year as an ES payment be sure to change the TC code to 660.

    7. A TC 610 payment substantially overpaid the module but does not match any amount on the return and does not appear to be intended for the next tax period. Look for any pending debit action for which the overpayment may be intended. Check other modules on the taxpayer’s account for debit balances that match the overpayment. Review AMS Alerts and History for indication of where the payment belongs.

    8. There is an unsubstantiated refundable credit (TC 766 — other than withholding or ES payments) or the taxpayer has mistakenly entered total credits amount on more than one line of Form 1040 or 1040-SR and the amount was transcribed. Beware of double credit situations.

    9. There is a Dishonored Check (TC 611, TC 641, TC 661, or TC 671) pending. Close the case using Closing Action "Module Situation Resolved" and ensure the TC 570 box is checked to prevent the refund from generating. Indicate in the case notes a dishonored check is present.

3.14.1.6.14.7 (01-01-2017)
Working Priority Refund Transcripts Manually

  1. If AMS is down for four hours, and upon HQ guidance, Notice Review tax examiners will use the manual input system. Management will access the "Daily Refund Transcript" file in Control D folder 38101-xx to obtain a list of the transcripts that were available for that day. HQ Analysts will help in understanding the Control-D report and how to determine which cases to work. tax examiners will indicate the manual action they performed on IDRS for each case on the NR Manual Action Sheet. See Exhibit 3.14.1-12 for the NR Manual Action Sheet. When the system comes back up, before the tax examiners can get back into AMS, the clerical personnel will input the work sheets on AMS.

3.14.1.6.15 (01-01-2023)

Reviewing Non–Math Error Balance Due Notices — CP 14

  1. A CP 14 generates when a balance due return with no math errors posts to the Master File. The balance due may include any combination of the amount of tax owed (per the taxpayer), penalties, and underpayment interest.

  2. CP 14 – Notice elements:

    • Balance due of $5 or more

    • No math error or credit discrepancy

      Note:

      Master File does not generate a CP 14 for less than $5.

  3. The most common Selection Keys for the CP 14 are 002, 008, 070–078 and 092. Keys 070–078 include pending transactions. Key 092 reviews are requested during peak processing to ensure that remittances or installment agreement requests are not attached to the return. Use the Selection Key description to determine where to begin reviewing the notice.

  4. Follow IRM 3.14.1.6.1, General Review Procedures and IRM 3.14.1.6.1.1, Verifying Return Information to review the return, if available. See IRM 3.14.1.6.2.1.1 , Pending Doc 54/47 Transactions for all notices and IRM 3.14.1.6.2.1.2 , Pending Credit or Debit Transactions for all notices.

  5. Review the case for any pending transactions using CC RECON, IMFOL and the Control D NRPS package Appended Data Sheet.

    Caution:

    CP 14 notices worked prior to Friday may not accurately reflect all pending transactions to the module. Some transactions do not show as pending on Control-D or TXMOD until after Master File posts on Thursday evening.

    1. If a payment or adjustment is either AP, PN, CU, or on the TEP file, use CC RECON, INTST, COMPA(F), PIEST and/or PIFTF to check for penalty and/or interest recomputations, and use the following chart:

      The tax will be paid in full Only ES Penalty remains on the module Retype to a CP 11 if a math error
      The module will remain in balance due status (for $5 or more) The FTF (TC 16X) or ES (TC 17X) penalties will recompute Apply Label 2. Refer to IRM 3.14.1.7.8.5, Labeling Notices
      The module will remain in balance due status (for $5 or more) The FTF (TC 16X) or ES (TC 17X) penalties will NOT recompute Retype the notice to reflect the credit. Refer to IRM 3.14.1.7.8.5Use Label 3 only when retyping is not possible.

      Example:

      When OLNR retype screen response time is very slow

      There is a pending Doc Code 54 or 47 tax adjustment With Hold Code "2" , "3" , or "4" Retype the notice

    2. If there is an unpostable transaction on the account that is a TC150, print the notice with no changes.

    3. If a payment or adjustment is either UP or on the GUF file, use CC UPTIN to check on the status of the transaction, and use the following chart:

      Note:

      Out of region unpostables require the @ with service center code after the TIN. (example: CC UPTIN XXX-XX-XXXX@18)

      The Unpostable is open Not Applicable Use CC UPCASZ to enter information to facilitate posting of the transaction. Input CC STAUPS for eight cycles. See IRM 3.14.1.6.24, Command Code STAUPS, for more information.
      The Unpostable is closed, check the Unpostable Resolution Code (URC) to determine if the payment will post to the notice module If the payment will post on the notice module Follow instructions in IRM 3.14.1.7.8, Notice Disposition

    4. If a payment is RS or UP, CC INTST reflects only the payment. Penalty and interest must be manually recomputed.

    5. If a payment or adjustment is pending on another module or account:

      If a Payment or Adjustment is Then
      Pending on another module or account

      • Wait for the payment or adjustment to post

      • When the TC 570 or the TC 841 posts, input CC STAUPS for up to eight cycles on the notice module. See IRM 3.14.1.6.24, Command Code STAUPS, for more information.

      • Reduce the STAUPS to five cycles.

      • Follow notice disposition instructions. See IRM 3.14.1.7.8, Notice Disposition

3.14.1.6.16 (01-01-2026)

Reviewing Non-Compute Notices – CP 51A, CP 51B, and CP 51C

  1. Taxpayers have the option to submit a return referred to as a Non-Compute. A valid Non-Compute return is one in which the taxpayer has requested the IRS compute their tax and any credits to which they may be entitled (e.g., EIC or Credit for the Elderly and Disabled). If the taxpayer clearly indicates such a request with a written statement, or it is clearly the intent of the taxpayer, IRS will compute their tax and/or credits.

  2. There are three types of Non-Compute notices:

    • CP 51A is a Balance Due.

      Note:

      Taxpayers with a balance due must file timely to be eligible for the 30 day penalty and interest free period.

    • CP 51B is an Overpayment.

    • CP 51C is an Even Balance.

  3. TPNCs are not allowable on a CP 51.

  4. Consider the return to be a true Non-Compute if it is a current year return, timely filed by the due date, and all the conditions below are present:

    1. The return has entries at least through the Adjusted Gross Income (AGI) line (follow the taxpayer’s intent - meaning, if they enter all their pertinent information up to the AGI, but do not provide a total).

    2. No math errors are present that would change any AGI or TXI fields provided by the taxpayer.

    3. The Taxable Income (TXI) is less than $100,000 and greater than zero.

    4. There are no entries on any tax, balance due, or refund line. "Zero" , "none" , 0, or a dash (–) are considered entries.

    5. Withholding on any attached Form W-2, Wage and Tax Statement, document(s) is present on the return.

    6. No schedules other than B, H, R, or EIC are attached.

      Note:

      The taxpayer must write "EIC" to the left of the EIC line, or "CFE" to the left of the Credit for Elderly or Disabled line, if they wish for IRS to figure those credits for them.

  5. The only forms allowed on a non-compute return a shown below. If other forms are attached it is not a true non-compute return.

    • Form 1116, Foreign Tax Credit

    • Form 2439, Notice to Shareholder of Undistributed Long-Term Capital Gains

    • Form 2441, Child and Dependent Care Expenses

    • Form 3800, General Business Credit

    • Form 3903, Moving Expenses

    • Form 4136, Credit for Federal Tax Paid on Fuels

    • Form 4797, Sales of Business Property

    • Form 4835, Farm Rental Income and Expenses

    • Form 4952, Investment Interest Expense Deduction

    • Form 5329, Additional Taxes on Qualified Plans (Including IRAs) and Other Tax-Favored Accounts

    • Form 8396, Mortgage Interest Credit

    • Form 8586, Low-Income Housing Credit

    • Form 8859, Carryforward of the District of Columbia First-Time Homebuyer Credit

    • Form 8863, Education Credits (American Opportunity and Lifetime Learning Credits)

    • Form 8880, Credit for Qualified Retirement Savings Contributions

    • Form 8903, Domestic Production Activities Deduction

  6. Follow instructions in IRM 3.14.1.6.1, General Review Procedures.

  7. Verify the income and withholding with the information on any attached Form W-2, Wage and Tax Statement, document(s).

  8. Math-verify the entire tax return, including Schedules B, EIC, and R, if attached.

  9. Correct any erroneous figures on the notice:

    1. If there is a math error discovered during review, which impacts AGI and/or TXI figures provided by the taxpayer, retype the notice to the appropriate math error notice and assign the necessary TPNCs, even if the return is otherwise a non-compute.

      Example:

      If the taxpayer has an apparent non-compute return with AGI and TXI fields completed, and a wage error is discovered, the AGI and TXI fields would then be changed by an adjustment. The taxpayer must now be informed of the wage error on a math error notice. Retyping the CP 51 is not appropriate, because it would reflect inconsistent AGI and TXI figures when compared to the taxpayer's records, and no explanation would be on the non-compute notice. Retype to the appropriate math error notice.

  10. On a CP 51B, follow Erroneous Refund procedures per IRM 3.14.1.6.7, Erroneous Refunds, if necessary. If the case does not meet Category A Erroneous Refund criteria:

    • Use Hold Code" 0 " on the adjustment

    • Apply Label 1 in OLNR in the current cycle

    Note:

    ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡

  11. Follow instructions in IRM 3.14.1.7.8, Notice Disposition.

  12. Void or correct any Associated notices affected by an adjustment.

  13. Occasionally, returns that should have been processed as Non–Computes are processed normally, and a math error notice with TPNC 209 or TPNC 218 is issued to the taxpayer, rather than a true Non-Compute Notice. Follow guidelines for IRM 3.14.1.6.16.3, Converting Another Notice to a CP 51.

3.14.1.6.16.1 (01-01-2018)
CP 51 Notice Disposition

  1. Void a CP 51 or retype it to another notice if:

    1. Taxable income is:

      •negative
        •zero ("0" )
        •a dash ("–" )
        •"none"
        •computed to be negative or zero and the remaining lines are blank, "zero" or "none" , excluding any entry in the payments section of the return

    2. If the return was received after the Return Due Date, convert the CP 51 to a CP 11 if there is a balance due, or a CP 12 if there is a credit balance, and assign TPNC 218. Follow guidelines in IRM 3.14.1.6.16.2, Converting a CP 51 to Another Notice.

    3. The return has a CCC "B" that was entered by ERS.

      If there is Then
      No math error or the refund matches the taxpayer’s figures Void the notice if it is a CP 51B or CP 51C
      A math error or a balance due Retype the CP 51 to another notice type
      A pending REQ54 and a second refund will go out Use Label 5 if it is a CP 51B

      Note:

      Verify that the Pay-By-Date on the retype screen of OLNR is saved as the later of RDD or the 23C date plus 21 days, before converting a CP 51 to any other notice type.

3.14.1.6.16.2 (01-01-2026)
Converting a CP 51 to Another Notice

  1. If converting a Non-Compute notice , a CP 51 with either an alpha A, B or C, to a different notice type, keep the following in mind:

    1. ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡

    2. The CP 51 is the only notice in the OLNR Retypes application that allows the user to edit the "Pay-By-Date" field.

  2. If the original notice is a CP 51A, and the notice is being converted into another balance due notice, the Pay-By-Date must be addressed prior to the notice conversion:

    1. ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡

    2. The "Pay-By-Date" field must be edited in the OLNR CP 51 retype screen PRIOR to selecting the new notice for conversion, since the new notice will not allow the "Pay-By-Date" field to be edited. This is a systemic limitation.

    3. "Save" the updated "Pay-By-Date" field in OLNR, before converting the CP 51 to the new notice type.

  3. If converting the CP 51 to a math error notice:

    1. Ensure that all TPNCs are properly assigned, including those that inform the taxpayer that IRS figured their tax (and/or credits) for them.

    2. Follow guidelines for addressing the "Pay-By-Date" field, if appropriate, as described in Item (2) above.

Converting Another Notice to a CP 51

  1. Retype another notice to a CP 51A when all the following are true:

    1. The return is a true Non-Compute. See IRM 3.14.1.6.16 (4) for Non-Compute criteria.

    2. There is a balance due.

    3. ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡

3.14.1.6.17 (01-01-2015)

Reviewing Notices with Specific Selection Keys

  1. This subsection contains instructions related to specific selection keys used in the Notice Review process.

3.14.1.6.17.1 (01-01-2018)
Key 001 — Overpayment Notices of $100,000 or More

  1. Always use IDRS to work this key.

    1. Check for balance due accounts.

    2. If there is an open control base on IDRS, contact the controlling tax examiner before making any changes to the module.

    3. To avoid paying additional interest to the taxpayer, verify all payments and extensions before the Thursday NOREFP deadline.

    4. Unclaimed payments may be intended for BMF accounts for Form 706, United States Estate (and Generation-Skipping Transfer), Tax Return (MFT 52), or Form 709, United States Gift (and Generation-Skipping Transfer), Tax Return (MFT 51).

    5. Research these accounts, using the SSN in TXMOD, followed by a "V" (valid segment) or "W" (invalid segment) for debit balances, or any other indications that the payments belong on Form 706, United States Estate (and Generation-Skipping Transfer), or Form 709, United States Gift (and Generation-Skipping Transfer), Tax Return, tax modules.

      Note:

      For joint returns, research both SSNs (valid and invalid).

  2. If the payments belong on the BMF accounts, use the following procedures:

    1. Prevent the refund from generating on the IMF notice module.

    2. Transfer the credit to the correct BMF tax module.

    3. Input CC STAUPS on the Form 706, United States Estate (and Generation-Skipping Transfer), or Form 709, United States Gift (and Generation-Skipping Transfer), Tax Return, tax module, if necessary. See IRM 3.14.1.6.24, Command Code STAUPS, for more information.

    4. For Form 709, United States Gift (and Generation-Skipping Transfer), Tax Return, only: if no extension is posted on the BMF tax module, input the extension n the BMF account. Refer to IRM 3.14.1.6.25, Extensions and IRM 3.14.2-11, Adding Extensions Using FRM77, for more detail.

  3. If the notice reflects overpayment or underpayment interest of $100,000 or more and the review indicates the notice is correct, print the notice timely.

3.14.1.6.17.2 (01-01-2018)
Key 003 — Overpayment Adjustment Notices of $100,000 or More

  1. Always use IDRS to work this key.

    1. Check for balance due accounts.

    2. If there is an open control base on IDRS, contact the controlling tax examiner before making any changes to the module.

    3. Verify that no duplicate or erroneous transactions or adjustments have posted or will post to the notice module.

3.14.1.6.17.3 (01-01-2026)
Key 004 — ES Discrepancy Notice with Incomplete or Out of Balance Payment Data

  1. Out-of-Balance payment data usually results from a dishonored check, credit reversal(s) that does not match by date or amount, or credit reversal(s) completed using multiple transaction codes.

    Caution:

    Review the below information carefully. Depending on the situation the notice may be printed, voided, or retyped.

  2. One of the most common conditions for Key 004 is part taxpayer error and part IRS system limitation:

    1. The ES discrepancy exists because the taxpayer submits an ES payment, realizes it will be dishonored, and then sends in a replacement payment. The replacement payment, however, often contains an additional amount to cover the bad check penalty, but the taxpayer doesn't claim that extra amount when they file the return.

    2. The out-of-balance condition exists, because current programming places a negative entry for a "Dishonored Check" in the payments table of OLNR but does not include the credit amount for the originally posted payment. This is because the transaction code of the original payment is converted by Master File (e.g., a TC 660 payment that is dishonored for insufficient funds becomes a TC 663 when the Dishonored Check TC 661 posts) and the notice programming does not allow this data to display for Notice Review.

    3. If after reviewing the payment discrepancies, any pending transactions, and dishonored check penalties, the IDRS account balance matches the notice balance (regardless of payment data) and the taxpayer still needs to receive a notice, print the notice. When Key 004 notices are not changed in OLNR, the correct payment data is sent to the taxpayer.

  3. If the ES discrepancy is due to a credit transfer completed with inappropriate transaction codes and no other discrepancy exists on the account, and there is no balance due and the taxpayer is receiving the refund they are expecting, void the notice. Follow IRM 3.14.1.6.1, General Review Procedures. Also follow instructions for IRM 3.14.1.6.13, Reviewing Estimated Tax (ES) Discrepancy Notices.

  4. When retyping the notice for changes other than a credit reversal out-of-balance condition, use the table below.

    Note:

    Do not retype the notice if the only reason for the difference is a dishonored check causing an out-of-balance condition. If all other information is correct and the taxpayer needs the notice choose print (e.g., balance due). If the TP has replaced the payment, paid the bad check fee, and there is no balance due, void the notice, ensuring to leave a history item.

    If And Then
    A Dishonored Check (debit amount) is present The total ES payments do not match the total from the payments list

    1. Add the corresponding payment (credit) for the dishonored check in the payment tab.

    2. Verify the notice amounts.
    A Prior Year Credit amount is present (as a debit) The total ES payments do not match the total from the payments list

    1. Add or edit the corresponding credit.

    2. Verify the notice amounts.
    A payment is not reflected in the payment list, but is in the total ES payments amount The Other Payments field reflects the reversal of the ES payment

    1. Edit out the offsetting debit and credit amounts.

    2. Retype or Void the notice if the ES discrepancy no longer exists.

    3. Verify the notice amounts.

3.14.1.6.17.4 (01-01-2024)
Key 008 — Balance Due Notices of $100,000 or More

  1. Always use IDRS to work this key.

    1. If there is an open control base on IDRS, contact the controlling tax examiner before making any changes to the module.

    2. Look for available credits or misapplied payments to apply to the notice module if necessary.

    3. If the taxpayer is claiming payments, use all available resources to locate the missing credits.

    4. Missing payments may have been misapplied to BMF Form 706, United States Estate and Generation-Skipping Transfer Tax Return (MFT 52), or Form 709, United States Gift and Generation—Skipping Transfer Tax Return (MFT 51). Form 706 is filed under the decedent’s Social Security Number (SSN). When researching IDRS, input a "V" behind the decedent’s SSN (i.e., 000-00-0000V). The MFT is 52 and the tax period consists of six zeros (000000). Although the return is filed under the decedent’s SSN, research via BMF CC such as BMFOL and BRTVU. Input a “W’ behind the decedent’s SSN to research accounts on the invalid segment.

    5. Research these accounts, using the SSN followed by a "V" (valid segment) or "W" (invalid segment) for payments that belong on the Form 1040, U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, notice module.

      Note:

      For joint returns, research both SSNs (valid and invalid).

  2. If payments are found, use the following procedures:

    1. Verify that the payments have not already refunded.

    2. Use CC BRTVU to verify that the payments are not claimed on the Form 706 or the Form 709.

    3. Prevent the refund from generating on the Form 706, U.S. Estate Tax Return, or Form 709, United States Gift (and Generation - Skipping Transfer) Tax Return, tax module, if necessary.

    4. Transfer the credit to the IMF notice module.

    5. Input CC STAUPS on the Form 1040, U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, notice module, if necessary. See IRM 3.14.1.6.24, Command Code STAUPS, for more information.

    Example:

    Use CC URINQ to search for unidentified payments. If the taxpayer has a history of filing in another Submission Processing Campus, contact that, Campus. Search for payments posted to any of the taxpayer’s other accounts.

  3. If the notice reflects credit or debit interest of $100,000 or more, follow IRM 3.14.1.6.17.1, Key 001 Overpayment Notices of $100,000 or More.

3.14.1.6.17.5 (01-01-2018)
Key 009 — Balance Due Adjustment Notice of $100,000 or More

  1. Always use IDRS to work this key.

    1. If there is an open control base on IDRS, contact the controlling tax examiner before making any changes to the module.

    2. Look for available credits or misapplied payments to apply to the notice module if necessary.

    3. Correct the entity if necessary.

  2. Verify that no duplicate or erroneous transactions or adjustments have posted or will post to the notice module.

3.14.1.6.17.6 (01-01-2015)
Key 010 — Dependent TIN TPNC Assigned to Pre-199612 Return

  1. Key 010 will select any Math Error notice for a tax period prior to 199612 that includes a Math Error Authority EIC or Dependent TIN issue.

  2. These TPNCs are 234, 235, 291, 580, 604, 605,701, 702, 743, and 745.

  3. These TPNCs should never be assigned to a return for a tax period prior to 199612. ERS instructions are to allow the exemption, credit, etc. related to the math error condition, even if an SSN is invalid or missing. In the case of TPNC 580, self-employment tax should not be assessed.

  4. If one or more of these TPNCs are assigned to a return for a tax period prior to 199612, route the case to the Examination Function.

  5. If the Examination Function does not accept the case, adjust the account, returning to the taxpayer’s figures in all areas directly related to the TPNC. Retype or void the notice as required.

    Example:

    If TPNC 604 is assigned on a 199512 notice and the Examination Function does not accept the case, correct the account to allow the exemption, even if the dependent’s SSN is invalid. Retype or void the notice.

3.14.1.6.17.7 (01-01-2026)
Key 060 — Tax Period More Than 2 Years Prior to Current Tax Year

  1. NRPS Selects under Key 060 as a quality measure, to ensure the accurate adjustments were made to the return during processing, based on the tax year filed.

  2. In 2026, tax years 2025 (current), and prior years 2024 and 2023 can be systemically calculated by ERS systems.

  3. Any time a return is processed that is more than two tax years prior to the current year, ERS must manually recalculate all items on the return.

  4. Follow general review procedures on these cases, ensuring the correct filing year, figures and tables are being appropriately used during recalculation.

  5. A high percentage of the errors in this Key are due to incorrect tax year figures being applied. Verify the following items on notices selected in this key: Standard Deduction and/or Exemption amounts, Total tax, including self-employment tax, EIC, ACTC, and other refundable credits.

3.14.1.6.17.8 (03-01-2023)
Key 061 — Multiple Math Error Explanations

  1. The computer printed explanation of the error(s) made on the return is called a Math Error Explanation.

  2. Systemic limitations prevent more than five explanations from being printed on a notice. If there are more than five errors to be assigned, ERS will enter the last TPNC as a TPNC 100. In situations where there are five TPNCs and none of the codes are a TPNC 100, NRPS will select the notice under Key 061.

3.14.1.6.17.9 (01-01-2019)
Key 065 — Loose Schedule H

  1. Taxpayers may use Schedule H, Household Employment Taxes, to report employment taxes on cash wages paid to household employees.

  2. In specific, infrequent circumstances, taxpayers may file Schedule H without an accompanying Form 1040, U.S. Individual Income Tax Return. This is known as a "loose Schedule H" .

  3. When a loose Schedule H is received in processing, a dummy Form 1040, U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, (coded with RPC "Y" ) is created to allow the Schedule H to post to the Master File. If the taxpayer later files a Form 1040, U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, it generates a CP 36 and is processed as a duplicate return.

    1. The most common problem arising from a taxpayer filing a loose Schedule H, followed by a Form 1040, U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, in a later cycle, is that any Estimated Tax payments on the account will be released (and possibly refunded) by the posting of the dummy Form 1040, U.S. Individual Income Tax Return.

      Note:

      Code and Edit instructions require that CCC "3" be edited on all dummy Schedule H returns to freeze any overpayment.

    2. Carefully review all notices selected by Key 065. If there is a refund caused by unclaimed Estimated Tax payments (usually accompanied by a CP 24), prevent the refund from generating and void or retype the notice as appropriate.

    3. Follow IRM 3.14.1.6.1, General Review Procedures.

    4. If a CP 25 is generated due to a dummy Form 1040, void the notice.

3.14.1.6.17.10 (01-01-2015)
Key 074 — Pending Merge Transaction

  1. Treat the account and the notice as though the merge will post.

3.14.1.6.17.11 (01-01-2015)
Key 091 — Selection Requested by Error Resolution (ERS)

  1. The Error Resolution System (ERS) has no provision for correcting a record after the document has been completed. If a record needs to be corrected, ERS will notify Notice Review to retype or void the notice.

    1. An ERS tax examiner will prepare Form 3465, Adjustment Request, and send it with the return to Notice Review.

    2. Use Key 091 on the Local Control File and the information on the Form 3465, Adjustment Request, to select the notice for review. See IRM 3.14.1.3.8, NRPS Local Control File

    3. Follow normal review procedures for this key.

3.14.1.6.17.12 (01-01-2026)
Key 100 — TPNC Explanations Not Computer Generated

  1. TPNC 100 has been discontinued due to language programming constraints.

  2. If there are more than five TPNCs that are applicable, ERS will assign a TPNC 100. Notice Review tax-examiners must identify the five best TPNCs and retype the notice accordingly.

  3. All cases must be retyped to the TPNCs with the most impact to the taxpayer and the TPNC 100 must be removed.

  4. Follow IRM 3.14.1.6.1, General Review Procedures.

3.14.1.6.17.13 (01-01-2015)
Keys 101–998 — Taxpayer Notice Codes (TPNC)

  1. Use the information throughout IRM 3.14.1, IMF Notice Review, Publication 17, and IRM 3.12.3, Error Resolution to review Math Error Notices selected under TPNC Selection Keys (IRM 3.12.3-1, Taxpayer Notice Codes). The main purpose of this review is to reduce unnecessary burdens on the taxpayer and to deliver a quality product.

3.14.1.6.18 (01-01-2017)

Reviewing Adjustment Notices — CP 21, CP 22, CP 30, CP 30A, CP 60, and CP 62

  1. Adjustment notices generate to inform the taxpayer of an account adjustment made on the notice module. These adjustments result from one or more of the following actions:

    • Examination Action (Doc Code 47)

    • DP Adjustments Action (Doc Code 54)

    • Failure to File (FTF — TC 166/167)

    • Estimated Tax (ES — TC 176/177) Penalty Assessment/Recomputation

    • Credit Transfer Actions (Doc Code 24, 34, or 48)

  2. Because the notice informs the taxpayer of action(s) taken on the notice module after initial processing, it is extremely important that Notice Review tax examiners carefully review all aspects of the notice module.

    Caution:

    Void an Adjustment notice only if the taxpayer has already been advised of the action(s) or would be confused by the notice.

  3. NRPS selects Adjustment notices if pending transactions or Refund S criteria exist on the notice module. For information on definer codes 041–050, 051–053, and 056, review IRM 3.14.1.6.14, Reviewing Priority Refund Transcripts in Accounts Management Services (AMS).

  4. Notice Review tax examiners are responsible for determining the effects that any pending or unpostable transactions will have on the notice module. The module should be reviewed for possible duplicate transactions. Use this information to determine the proper notice disposition.

    Caution:

    Adjustment notices worked prior to Friday may not accurately reflect all pending transactions to the module. Some transactions do not show as pending on Control-D or TXMOD until after Master File posts on Thursday evening.

3.14.1.6.18.1 (01-01-2015)
CP 21 and CP 22 — Notice of DP Adjustment or Examination

  1. CP 21 and CP 22 notices are computer generated notices that inform the taxpayer that an adjustment was made to the tax module. For this reason, these notices are commonly referred to as adjustment notices.

3.14.1.6.18.1.1 (01-01-2015)
CP 21 and CP 22 — Issuance Criteria

  1. The CP 21 is an Examination or DP tax adjustment notice that generates when an adjustment results in an overpayment, an even balance, or a balance due of $5 or more.

    Note:

    If the notice shows a balance due of $5 or more, the module must have been in TDA (22, 24, or 26) or Installment (60) status prior to the adjustment to generate a CP 21.

  2. The CP 22 is an Examination or DP tax adjustment notice that generates when an adjustment results in a balance due of $5 or more if the tax module was not in TDA (22, 24, or 26) or Installment (60) Status prior to the adjustment.

  3. Systemic assessment or recomputation of Failure to File or Estimated Tax Penalties will also generate a CP 21 or CP 22.

3.14.1.6.18.1.2 (01-01-2015)
CP 21 and CP 22 Notice Elements

  1. The following is a short description of each type of Adjustment notice:

    CP Cause Balance Other Information
    CP 21A A DP tax adjustment or a penalty recomputation (Doc Code 54) Balance due of $5 or more The notice module was in TDA (22, 24, or 26) or Installment (60) status prior to the adjustment.
    CP 22A A DP tax adjustment or a penalty recomputation (Doc Code 54) Balance due of $5 or more The notice module was in a status other than 22, 24, 26, or 60.
    CP 21B A DP tax adjustment or a penalty recomputation (Doc Code 54) Overpayment of $1 or more Not Applicable
    CP 21C A DP tax adjustment or a penalty recomputation (Doc Code 54) Overpayment of less than $1 or balance due of less than $5 Not Applicable
    CP 21E An Exam (Doc Code 47) adjustment Any balance If there is a balance due of $5 or more, the notice module was in TDA (22, 24, or 26) or Installment (60) Status prior to the adjustment.
    CP 22E An Exam (Doc Code 47) adjustment Balance Due of $5 or more The notice module was in a Status other than 22, 24, 26, or 60.

3.14.1.6.18.1.3 (11-12-2019)
CP 21 and CP 22 Notice Disposition

  1. Retyping CP 21 and CP 22 adjustment notices is more complex than other notice types. CP 21A and CP 22A are status driven. Refer to Appendix B of the Notice Review Job Aid 2534-002 for additional information and instruction for editing OLNR fields to reflect the addition or removal of payments on the module.

  2. Follow the same notice disposition and labeling procedures for refunding, overpaid, even balance, and balance due Adjustment notices.

  3. Recompute all penalties to ensure correct notice disposition.

  4. Review adjustment notices on IDRS to accurately determine the notice disposition.

  5. Verify the correctness of the adjustment only if the adjustment is for an unreasonable amount or appears to be a duplicate.

  6. Compare the adjustment item against the source document if requested and/or available.

  7. If the adjustment was input incorrectly, contact the originator for advice in taking corrective action (e.g., voiding/retyping the notice). If the originator cannot be contacted, void, label, or retype the incorrect notice as appropriate. Follow erroneous refund procedures, if necessary.

  8. When a tax module shows a TC 300 .00 adjustment, look for a TC 640 (Advanced Payment of Determined Deficiency) on the module.

  9. Refer to IRM 3.14.1.7.8.5, Labeling Notices for examples of the labels referenced in this section.

3.14.1.6.18.2 (01-01-2026)
CP 30 — Estimated Tax (ES) Penalty Notice

  1. A CP 30 generates on an overpaid module if the computer generated ES Penalty (TC 176) is greater than the taxpayer’s self-assessed penalty and there is no math error or ES discrepancy or when the module balance is in balance due that is less than or equal to the assessed ES penalty amount (TC 176) and no other taxpayer settlement notice issuance except a Non-Compute (CP 51).

  2. Accept the TC 176 amount unless at least one of the following conditions is present on the return:

    If Then
    There is an entry in any box on:

    • Form 2210, Underpayment of Estimated Tax by Individuals, Estates and Trusts, lines A through E

    • Form 2210–F, Underpayment of Estimated Tax by Farmers and Fishers, part 1a or 1b

    1. Reduce the ES Penalty to the taxpayer's figures. See Item (4)(c) below

    2. Apply Label 5 in OLNR if the CP 30 is the only notice being issued. Use the If/Then chart in (5) below to determine how to handle CP 30 cases with associated notices
    The taxpayer entered one of the following, either on Form 2210, Underpayment of Estimated Tax by Individuals, Estates and Trusts, or beside the line marked "ES Tax Penalty" on Form 1040, U.S. Individual Income Tax Return:

    • "Waiver"

    • "Annualized Income" (AI)

    • "Actual Withholding"

    • "Not Liable" or "Exempt"

    • "Farmer" or "Fisherman"

    1. Reduce the ES Penalty to the taxpayer's figures. See Item (4)(c) below

    2. Apply Label 5 in OLNR if the CP 30 is the only notice being issued. Use the If/Then chart in (5) below to determine how to handle CP 30 cases with associated notices
    None of the above apply, and reasonable cause is not present on the return

    1. Accept the TC 176 amount

    2. Print the notice

    Note:

    Any of the above conditions require that Code & Edit assign CCC "P" to the return, forcing the computer to accept the taxpayer’s ES Penalty figures. If any of these special conditions are present and the return did not receive a CCC "P" , reduce the ES Penalty to the taxpayer’s figures.

  3. If reasonable cause for underpayment of Estimated Tax is present on the return, check for CCC "7" (Reasonable Cause denied):

    If CCC "7" Then
    Is present

    1. Accept the computer’s figures

    2. Print the notice
    Is not present

    1. Route the case to Accounts Management on Form 3465, Adjustment Request, for consideration of Reasonable Cause

    2. Print the notice

  4. To reduce the ES Penalty:

    1. Input CC REQ54 on IDRS.

    2. Use Blocking Series 05.

    3. Input TC 171 for the difference between the TC 176 and the taxpayer’s amount. This goes in the same TC area as a TC 290.

    4. Use Source Code 4.

    5. Use Reason Code 065 in the first position and use Penalty Reason Code 045 in the fourth position.

    6. Use Hold Code "0" .

    7. Enter the following in the remarks: "Abate ES Penalty per IRM 3.14.1.6.18.2"

  5. Because a CP 30 can have associated notices CP 45 (Reduced Credit Elect) and/or CP 49 (Overpayment Offset), use the following If/Then chart to determine what Hold Code to use when inputting TC 171 on the CC REQ54 screen to abate the ES penalty, and what disposition to use for the notice(s) on OLNR.

    If the CP 30 And Then
    Is the only notice being issued Not Applicable

    1. If the adjustment to increase the refund is input before 6 P.M. local time on Monday, retype the notice to reflect the change and use Hold Code “3”.

    2. If the adjustment to increase the refund is input after 6 P.M. local time Monday, use a Hold Code “0” on the adjustment and Label 5 in OLNR.
    Has an associated CP 45 only, and the TC 171 will satisfy the entire Unapplied Credit Elect An additional refund check will not generate Use Hold Code "3" on the TC 171, void both notices and input a history item on IDRS.
    Has an associated CP 45 only, and the TC 171 will satisfy the entire Unapplied Credit Elect An additional refund check will generate

    1. If the adjustment to increase the refund is input before 6 P.M. local time on Monday, retype the notice to reflect the change and use Hold Code “3”.

    2. If the adjustment to increase the refund is input after 6 P.M. local time Monday, use a Hold Code “0” on the adjustment and Label 5 the CP 30 notice in OLNR.

    3. Void the CP 45 and input a history item on IDRS.
    Has an associated CP 45 only The TC 171 will only partially satisfy the Unapplied Credit Elect Use Hold Code "3" , retype both notices
    Has an associated CP 49 only Not Applicable

    1. If the adjustment to increase the refund is input before 6 P.M. local time on Monday, retype the notice to reflect the change and use Hold Code “3”.

    2. If the adjustment to increase the refund is input after 6 P.M. local time Monday, use a Hold Code “0” on the adjustment and Label 1 the CP 30 notice in OLNR.
    Has both a CP 45 and CP 49 associated The CP 49 has no remaining balances Use Hold Code "3" on the TC 171; Retype all 3 notices
    Has both a CP 45 and CP 49 associated The CP 49 still shows remaining balances

    1. If the adjustment to increase the refund is input before 6 P.M. local time on Monday, retype the notice to reflect the change and use Hold Code “3”.

    2. If the adjustment to increase the refund is input after 6 P.M. local time Monday, use a Hold Code “0” on the adjustment and Label 1 the CP 30 notice in OLNR.

    3. Print the CP 45 and CP 49

A CP 30A is an overpaid notice, generated when the computer reduces or abates the ES Penalty figured by the taxpayer and there is no math error or ES discrepancy or when the module balance is in balance due that is less than or equal to the assessed ES penalty amount (TC 176) and no other taxpayer settlement notice issuance except a Non-Compute (CP 51).

  3. When the taxpayer prepays an estimated tax penalty of $100 or more, and the computer does not agree with the amount the taxpayer has computed, there may be a problem with the taxpayer’s filing status, prior year estimated tax base, or both.   5. If the notice module Prior Year Estimated Tax Base is zero (.00), use the Control D NRPS package or CC RTVUE or IMFOL to determine if the prior year module has a TC 150.

3.14.1.6.18.4 (03-10-2025)
CP 60 — Notice of Credit Reversal

  1. CP 60 is a computer generated notice that informs the taxpayer of a credit reversal on the tax module. The notice generates when both of the following criteria exist:

    1. The debit side of a credit reversal transaction (TC 612, TC 642, TC 662, or TC 672) posts without an accompanying TC 570 to a zero or credit balance module.

    2. The transaction results in a debit balance of $5 or more.

  2. Use the Control D NRPS package and/or IDRS to review CP 60 notices to resolve the debit balance.

  3. Check all tax modules and pending (AP, PN, RS, UP, and TP) transaction data intended for the notice module. See IRM 3.14.1.6.2.1.1 , Pending Doc 54/47 Transactions and in addition, see IRM 3.14.1.6.2.1.2 , Pending Credit or Debit Transactions.

    If the credit is Then
    Located and available Transfer the credit to the debit balance module
    If the credit will Then
    Satisfy the entire debit balance Void the CP 60. Input CC STAUPS for eight cycles. See IRM 3.14.1.6.24, Command Code STAUPS, for more information.
    Not satisfy the entire debit balance Retype notice to reflect the credit. Input CC STAUPS if necessary.
    Unpostable Input CC STAUPS for eight cycles. Use CC UPTIN, UPDIS, and UPCASZ to notify the Unpostables Function if any corrective action is needed. See IRM 3.14.1.3.2, Resolving Unpostable Transactions See above for disposition.

  4. If another module shows one or more offsets (TC 826) generated in the notice cycle for the amount of the credit transfer, reverse enough of the offset to cover the debit balance, if available.

    Caution:

    Do not reverse a TC 826 that posted in a prior cycle unless credit is refunding or is otherwise available for reversal since the taxpayer has already been notified of the offset.

  5. Keep the following in mind when reviewing CP 60 notices:

    CP 60 Review Reminders

    1. A TC 570 on the debit side of a credit transfer will suppress a CP 60, but will not suppress a CP 21 or a CP 22

    2. Hold Code 3 will not suppress a CP 60

    3. Always use CC ACTON to input a history item when voiding a CP 60

    4. Use the LCF, See IRM 3.14.1.3.8, NRPS/Local Control File and IRM 3.14.1.3.8.2 ,CC NRP97 Input Information to intercept a CP 60 when preventing a refund from generating because of a pending credit reversal.

  6. If a TC 856 (offset of generated interest) is present, use the IAT Credit Transfer tool to reverse it with a TC 731/851. Then use CC REQ54 with a Hold Code 3 to reverse the TC 776 (generated interest) with a TC 772. When the offset of overpayment principal and or overpayment interest is through manual actions(s), either fully or partially reversed. Master File will not systemically adjust the overpayment interest. See IRM 20.2.4.7.1, Interest on Offsets.

    Caution:

    The credit must be available. If it is refunding, prevent the refund from generating and wait until the TC 841 posts or use a posting delay code to perform the adjustment.

  7. Void the CP 60 and CP 49 if all the offset was reversed. If only part of the offset was reversed, retype the CP 49 and void the CP 60.

  8. Input a TC 570 on both sides of the credit reversal to prevent the refund from generating any additional offsets or notices. Input CC STAUPS for eight cycles if the refund will be prevented from generating. See IRM 3.14.1.6.24, Command Code STAUPS, for more information.

3.14.1.6.18.5 (01-01-2026)
CP 62 — Notice of Located and Transferred Payment

  1. CP 62 is a computer generated notice that informs the taxpayer that a missing payment has been located and moved to a specific tax module. The CP 62 generates when the credit portion of a Doc Code 34, credit transfer, posts with a Correspondence Received Date (CRD). The CRD is input to notate that a taxpayer called or sent in a request for a payment to be applied to a specific module. A CP 62 can reflect any balance (overpaid, even, or balance due) and can generate without a posted TC 150.

    Caution:

    Since CP 62 notices generate to notify the taxpayer, a payment was credited to a particular module, at least one payment must show as a credit (positive) on the notice in OLNR, even after retype.

  2. Review the CP 62 for the following:

    • The tax periods involved,

    • All credits and debits on the tax modules,

    • The assessed tax, prepayment credit, penalty, and interest amounts, and

    • The current module balance.

      Caution:

      Sometimes payments are moved in and out of CP 62 account modules, both systemically and manually. Carefully review both sides of each credit transfer looking for erroneous refunds and balance due accounts. Notice Review must make every possible attempt to correct all modules involved with the CP 62.

  3. Use the Control D NRPS package and IDRS to review CP 62 notices to resolve any remaining debit balance and to verify that the taxpayer’s credits are posted correctly.

  4. CP 62 notices are generally selected by NRPS due to pending transactions. Identify and verify pending debit and credit transactions that may require a notice retype or label in OLNR. See the table in IRM 3.14.1.6.18.5 (7) for CP 62 OLNR notice disposition.

    • Verify pending credits are being applied to the module correctly.

    • Verify debit transactions will generate another notice or retype the current notice to reflect them.

  5. Systemic spousal payment transfers, identified with a TC 666 / TC 667, can cause balance and notice issues. These payments can be moved manually (TC 660 /TC 662) in error before the systemic transfer can occur. Review all secondary modules on joint returns (FS-2) to ensure that primary taxpayer account is not overpaid due to an incorrect credit transfer and balance due situation on the secondary taxpayer account. Also, carefully review married filing separately (FS-3) accounts for misapplied payments. See IRM 3.14.1.6.11.6, ES Spousal Validation Freeze (D-) and IRM 21.5.7.3.2.2, Spousal Payments, for more information.

  6. If a missing payment is found, apply the payment to the correct account module in IDRS using the IAT credit transfer tool. Be careful to freeze any credits that need to be held so the credit transfer can be performed.

  7. Anytime a CP 62 notice needs to be retyped it must contain at least one payment credited to the account, even if that payment has since been moved out.If the applied payment has been moved out of the module, the payments need to show in the payment section of OLNR as a payment applied (example TC 670 $500.00) and a payment removed (example TC 672 $500.00-).If both payments are removed the notice will error out in processing and the taxpayer will not receive a notice. Use the table below for CP 62 OLNR notice disposition.

    Caution:

    Never void a CP 62 unless it will be combined with another CP 62.

    Note:

    Prior module balances other than debit will not be passed from Master File to the taxpayer notices. Therefore, do not retype OLNR field Prior Balance – Est. unless the original notice is balance due.

    If And Then in OLNR
    One or more credits are pending and will be applied to the notice module A balance due will be decreased and FTF and/or ES penalties will recompute Label 2
    One or more credits are pending and will be applied to the notice module A balance due will be decreased and FTF and/or ES penalties will not recompute Label 3
    One or more credits are pending and will be applied to the notice module An overpayment or refund will be increased and FTF and/or ES penalties will not recompute

    • If the refund was frozen during processing or by another area and remains frozen, Label 4.

    • If the taxpayer received a refund and another refund will be released, Label 6.

    • If no TC 150 has posted, retype the notice to reflect the pending credits by adding them to the payment tab in OLNR.
    A TC 29X or TC 30X credit transaction is pending on the notice module The module is refunding

    • If the adjustment hold code is 3 or 4, Label 17 .

    • If the adjustment hold code is 0 or 1, Label 1.
    A TC 29X or TC 30X (debit or credit transaction) is pending on the notice module There is no refund

    • If no additional notice will generate (adjustment hold code 3 or 4), retype the notice and add the adjustment value to the Prior Balance – Est. field in OLNR.

    • If the adjustment hold code is 0 or 1, Label 1.
    One or more debits are pending and will be removed from the notice module A balance due will be increased with or without penalties

    • Retype the notice,

    • Add the debit (removed) payments as negative payments on the payment tab in OLNR. The payments should be input on the payment tab with a minus (-) in front of the dollar amount.

      -$5,000.00.

    • Do not remove any corresponding original posted payments from the payment tab.

    • Update interest and penalties as applicable.

    • Retype the notice,

    • Add the debit (removed) payments as negative payments on the payment tab in OLNR. The payments should be input on the payment tab with a minus (-) in front of the dollar amount.

      Example:

      -$5,000.00.

    • Do not remove any corresponding original posted payments from the payment tab.

The payments should be input on the payment tab with a minus (-) in front of the dollar amount.

      Example:

      -$5,000.00.

    • If the refund has been issued (posted TC 846), follow Erroneous Refund Procedures in IRM 3.14.1.6.7.

  8. Correct all errors found during review.

3.14.1.6.19 (01-01-2026)

Tolerances

  1. Tolerances Notice Review will apply when determining whether to adjust an account, or leave the account as it stands, with respect to tax and certain credits common on the return.

    1. All tolerances for true Non-Compute returns are $1 see IRM 3.14.1.6.16, Reviewing Non-Compute Notices — CP 51A, CP 51B, and CP 51C.

    2. For all other returns, tolerance can be applied to either the Posted Tax or Tax-Per-Taxpayer, depending on account conditions.

    3. This tax tolerance applies to all taxes and credits that make up the Total Tax, including Self-Employment Tax, Alternative Minimum Tax, Form 8615, Tax for Certain Children Who have Unearned Income, Non-Refundable Credits, and "Other Taxes" .

    4. All taxpayers should receive the same fairness in the application of the tolerance, whether their tax was changed erroneously during processing or not.

    5. The tolerance amount cannot be applied against a potential tax adjustment which already exceeds tolerance

      Example:

      If the tax will increase by $1,000 do not subtract the $100 tolerance and assess only $900.

    6. First, determine if the Tax-Per-Taxpayer was unchanged, increased, or decreased during processing. Then, use the appropriate Tolerance Table below to decide when and how to correct the tax, or apply the tolerance.

      Note:

      If the Tax-Per-Taxpayer is correct as filed, adjust the tax accordingly, regardless of amount. Tolerance does not apply when the taxpayer is correct.

3.14.1.6.20.1 (01-01-2021)
Recomputations of Penalties and Interest – General

  1. A manual penalty adjustment prevents the automatic recomputation.

  2. See IRM 20.2, Interest, for information on computing interest. Even though this IRM has instructions for manually adjusting penalty and interest, input manual restrictions only after determining that the computer cannot correctly assess and/or abate penalty or interest.

  3. See IRM 20.1, Penalty Handbook for information on computing penalties and reasonable cause criteria. If the taxpayer requests abatement due to reasonable cause, see IRM 3.14.1.6.9.1 Taxpayer Correspondence.

    Note:

    Disaster and bankruptcy may affect penalty and/or interest recalculations. Disaster dates can be seen on CC IMFOLE and ENMOD.

  4. The computer will assess and abate penalties on the Master File when:

    1. An Examination adjustment posts.

    2. A DP tax adjustment posts.

    3. An approved Extension of Time posts after the tax and penalties were computer assessed.

    4. An adjustment to a refundable credit posts.

    5. A payment posts or is transferred to or from the account.

  5. ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡

    1. ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡
