  2. A refund may be split among no more than three accounts. Each honored split refund request will reflect separate TC 846s on CC TXMOD.

  3. In CC IMFOLT, however, each account's information will be present.

  4. If any issue arises from the accuracy of the RTN or bank account numbers, the refund will default to a paper check, and a CP 53 will be issued to the taxpayer.

  5. If a refund is reduced during processing, direct deposits from the Form 8888, Allocation of Refund, will still be honored, applying credit to each bank account in a 1st-2nd-3rd account priority, as credit is available.

  6. A paragraph will automatically be inserted into the notice text to notify the taxpayer if changes were made to the direct deposit amounts. A split refund table will also accompany the text and will show how much was requested to go into each account (taken from Form 8888, Allocation of Refund), and how much was actually applied.

  7. A Direct Deposit tab will appear on OLNR retype screens for all notices upon which a Form 8888, Allocation of Refund, was attached to the return. This data will rarely be altered but is available if needed for notice conversion.

  8. The systemic hold does not apply to split refunds. If the case needs to be adjusted erroneous refund procedures will need to be followed.

3.14.1.7.2 (01-01-2026)

Controlling Cases

  1. Some cases in Notice Review require monitoring until all transactions, manual and systemic, are complete. This monitoring is done with a Control Base in IDRS. This is controlling a case.

  2. A Case Control or control base is opened or established in IDRS in different ways. The most common way to establish a case control or base is systemically.

    • A control base is automatically established with the input of NOREFP. The preferred NOREFP input method is IAT Stop Refund tool but both IAT and manual input of NOREFP will create a Control Base.

      Reminder:

      Case controls on a NOREFP case cannot be closed until all actions have been performed, posted, and the TC 841 has posted.

    • A control base is automatically established by inputting a REQ54/ADJ54 adjustment. ADJ 54 input of A, B, or M in the CASE-STS-CD> field will leave an open control base. If C is input a base will display as closed but can still be viewed in TXMOD. However, a C or closed base will not appear on the weekly CCA4243/Overage Report in Control D.

    • A control base is automatically established by input of a credit transfer. Input of A, B, or M in the Debit Status or Credit Status field in IAT will leave an open control base. If C is input a base will display as closed but can still be viewed in TXMOD. However, a C or closed base will not appear on the weekly Overage Report in Control D.

  3. A control base can be input manually utilizing CC ACTON.

    • ACTON is input in the upper left hand corner of IDRS, overlaying TXMODA.

    • Clear the remainder of the line.

    • On the next line enter C#,ACTIVITY,B,OURV and then clear the remainder of the line. (The # establishes the next number of control base. If this is the first control being opened on the module 01 will be the count after transmittal. ACTIVITY section allows 10 characters. B is the case status. OURV is Output Review, the original name for Notice Review. If the case required a NOREFP use RFDL for Refund Delete).

    • On the next line enter *,* (First start assigns to TE who is inputting and second * is the current date. Either of these fields can be input manually, for instance if assigning to a different tax examiner.)

    • Page up or transmit.

  4. Establish a control on all cases held in suspense past the notice cycle (H disposition in OLNR). This will cause the case to appear on the weekly CCA4243/Overage Report in Control D.

  5. Monitor the overage listing so the case can be worked and closed within one week of all the transactions posting including the TC 841, except cases awaiting correspondence. After one week, the case will count as an aged case. See IRM 3.30.123.6, Processing Timeliness Criteria for IMF Domestic Income Tax Returns, International IMF Income Tax Returns, Domestic and International Tax Returns Delayed for Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN) Processing, Extension Requests, Estimated Payments, Amended Tax Returns, and ITIN Applications.

  6. To control a "Turnaround " case [an error found in Notice Review (including errors made during initial processing) results in a tax increase with no prior tax decrease or a refundable credit (except withholding) decrease with no prior refundable credit increase (see Erroneous Refund, IRM 3.14.1.6.7 Turnaround (6), for more information.]:

    1. Work these cases in the notice cycle. Input all adjustments, retype or label the notices in the notice cycle to ensure that every taxpayer receives the full benefit of the penalty and/or interest free period.

    2. For cases not worked in cycle, use CC ACTON to control the case under Category Code "OURV" . Input

    3. CC STAUPS for eight cycles on balance due cases not worked in cycle to prevent Collection (500 series) notices. Reduce the STAUPS after resolving the case, depending on the notice disposition. See IRM 3.14.1.6.24, Command Code STAUPS for more information.

    4. Turnaround cases are considered aged after one week.

  7. If the case is controlled by another tax examiner in "A" status only and action should be taken:

    1. Contact the tax examiner with the open control to decide who will resolve the case.

      Exception:

      Contact is not necessary if the open control is assigned to a clerical unit. (Clerical units are often identified by all zeroes in the last 5 digits of the employee number (i.e., XXXXX00000), although numbers other than zero may also be used.) This means the case has not been assigned to a tax examiner in another area and can be worked per Notice Review procedures.

    2. If the other tax examiner agrees to accept the case, transfer the case and close your control base. Use CC ESTABDT to recharge the return if paper and in Notice Review. Route the return and all pertinent documents to the other area tax examiner.

      Note:

      Include documentation of your discussion as part of the case.

3.14.1.7.3 (03-31-2023)

Documenting Adjustment Cases

  1. Attach documentation of all telephone contacts to the return.

    If Then
    The return or other documents, such as a taxpayer letter, is available as a source document (SD) Attach an explanation, which might include calculations, worksheet prints, or screen shots of REQ54 etc., to the document to leave a paper trail for other tax examiners to follow. Make sure to use the correct blocking series and associate the document and adjustment back to files. Enter the explanation in the remarks section of the CC REQ54 or credit transfer screen.
    A document is not available as a source document (NSD) Enter a complete explanation of the adjustment in the remarks section of the CC REQ54 or credit transfer screen on IDRS.

3.14.1.7.4 (01-01-2026)

Notice Review Sent Taxpayer Correspondence-Reply and No Reply Procedures

  1. If additional information is needed from a taxpayer before the notice disposition can be determined, request the documentation in writing.

    1. Send the appropriate letter in the notice cycle to allow adequate time for the taxpayer to respond. If the requested information is not received before the close of the cycle, the notice may be held, see IRM 3.14.1.7.8.7, Holding Notices, for more information.

    2. See the Correspondex Letter Repository for specific letter information including paragraph requirements for each letter at the bottom of the appropriate letter document.

    3. Cases must be controlled in IDRS while awaiting the taxpayer’s reply. See IRM 3.14.1.7.2 Controlling Cases, for more information.

    4. Monitor the OVERAGE REPORT/CCA4243 for open controls that are aging. Correspondence cases should be monitored for 45 days.

      Note:

      If a reply is not received in 45 days follow the section below for additional actions.

    5. Continue processing the case when the reply is received. Upon receipt of a reply, ensure that action is taken immediately to close the case.

      Note:

      Do not correspond again if the IRS already corresponded. Treat as a no reply. To verify if previous correspondence was sent look for a Letter 12C - Individual Return Incomplete for Processing: Forms 1040 & 1040-SR, on ENMOD indicated with an H (e.g., H C 06022025 092610000 0012CLTR30 Z ). H is history, C is for closed entity control, the next field is the date, followed by the tax examiner then the letter type, MFT, and paragraph(s). The paragraph in the example is Z. To identify the meaning of the paragraph sent, see Form 6001, Letter 0012C Correspondence Action Sheet (CAS), using the version for the corresponding tax year. In addition, a Computer Condition Code (CCC) U indicates no reply to correspondence and prevents generation of credit interest.

  2. If a signature is missing and there is no indication that a previous letter was sent:

    1. Stop the refund, see IRM 3.14.1.7.1, Preventing Refunds.

    2. Send a Letter 143C - Signature Missing (IMF/BMF) with applicable paragraphs using the IAT Letters Tool. Use the IAT Job Aid for Letters to utilize the tool.

      Example:

      A complete 143C letter could include paragraphs: E, K, S, T, U and 3.

    3. Verify with the lead the appropriate eFax and Mail Stop number to include in the letter. Do not use a local phone number. Provide 1-800-829-0922 for the taxpayer if they choose to call.

    4. Maintain an open control in IDRS while awaiting the taxpayer’s reply. See IRM 3.14.1.7.2 Controlling Cases, for more information.

    5. Follow the table below for actions following a taxpayer response or expiration of the 45-day timeframe after a signature request.

      If the taxpayer Then
      Replies within 45 days Input a REQ54/ADJ54 TC 290 .00, Blocking Series 05 and Hold Code 3 to release the refund. If the reply was received after the normal or extended Return Due Date, overlay the RET-PROC-DT> field in ADJ54 with the IRS received date stamped on the reply (or eFax date) to set a new 45-day interest-free period. If a MEF return, select “Y” for source doc attached to create a filing DLN to associate any documents.

      Note:

      Documents received with and including the correspondence need to be associated with the original paper return.
      Does not reply within 45 days to the request for signature, the account requires no adjustment, and a P– freeze is holding the overpayment

      • Input a TC 290 .00 with a Hold Code 4 to set a –K freeze. Close the control base.

      • Notate in AMS History for the appropriate tax year a missing signature and a no reply to 143C.

      • Close your base.
      Does not reply within 45 days to the request for signature, the account requires no adjustment, and a -K or a -R freeze is holding the overpayment.

      • Notate in AMS History for the appropriate tax year a missing signature and a no reply to 143C.

      • Close the control base. Do not release the freeze.

      Note:

      Both the –K and the –R freeze will generate a transcript to Accounts Management.
      Does not reply within 45 days to the request for signature, but the account requires an adjustment, and a P– or –R freeze is holding an overpayment

      • Input CC REQ54 adjustment with Hold Code 4 to set a –K freeze to hold any credit balance.

      • Retype the notice.

      • Notate in AMS History for the appropriate tax year a missing signature and a no reply to 143C.

      • Close the control base. Do not release the freeze.

      Note:

      Both the –K and the –R freeze will generate a transcript to Accounts Management.
      Replies after 45 days and the control base is already closed Complete Form 3465, Adjustment Request, requesting that the return processable date be updated and route the case to Accounts Management.

  3. If a payment has not been claimed by the taxpayer, research does not identify where the payment belongs, and there is no indication that a previous letter was sent:

    1. Stop the refund, see IRM 3.14.1.7.1, Preventing Refunds.

    2. Send a Letter 1687C- Unidentified Payment/Credit with applicable paragraphs using the IAT Letters Tool. Use the IAT Job Aid for Letters to utilize the tool.

    3. Verify with the lead the appropriate eFax and Mail Stop number to include in the letter. Do not use a local phone number. Provide 1-800-829-0922 for the taxpayer if they choose to call.

    4. Maintain an open control in IDRS while awaiting the taxpayer’s reply. See IRM 3.14.1.7.2 Controlling Cases, for more information.

    5. Follow the table below for actions following a taxpayer response or expiration of the 45-day timeframe after a request for payment verification.

    If the taxpayer Then
    Replies within 45 days, verifies the payment belongs to them, and requests a refund

    • Input a REQ54/ADJ54, TC 290 .00, Blocking Series 05, and Hold Code 3, to release the refund.

    • Close the base.

    Note:

    Documents received with and including the correspondence need to be associated with the original return if paper.
    Replies within 45 days to a payment verification letter and states that the payment is for a forthcoming amended return

    • Input a TC 290 .00 with a Hold Code 4 to set a –K freeze.

    • Close the control base as TP1040X in the activity.

    • Print the notice.

    • If a transcript was held in suspense, close it module situation resolved including notes for a forthcoming 1040X.

    Note:

    Documents received with and including the correspondence need to be associated with the original return if paper.
    Replies within 45 days to a payment verification letter and states that the payment is for a module other than the notice module

    • Using the IAT Credit Transfer tool, move the payment to the correct module per the taxpayer’s reply.

    • Close the base when performing the credit transfer.

    • Notate in AMS History for the appropriate tax year where the payment was moved to and per the taxpayer reply to a 1687C.
    Does not reply within 45 days to a payment verification letter, or denies having made the payment

    • Follow procedures in IRM 3.14.1.6.8, Excess Collections and Unidentified Remittance Files.

    • The payment will need to be moved to the XSF or URF depending on the date of the payment.
    Replies after 45 days stating the payment belongs to them, and the request to move the payment to XSF or URF has already been sent

    • Follow procedures in IRM 3.14.1.6.8.1.1, Requesting Payments from the XSF or IRM 3.14.1.6.8.2.1 ,Requesting Payments from the URF as appropriate.

  4. If a decedent account is refunding, the return does not include court documents or a Form 1310 attached, and if there is no indication that a previous letter was sent:

    Note:

    Decedent refund claims must have supporting documents (Form 1310 or Court Appointment Documentation and Payment Verification) unless there is a surviving spouse. See IRM 3.14.1.6.5 Decedent Accounts, for more information.

    1. Stop the refund, see IRM 3.14.1.7.1, Preventing Refunds.

    2. Send a Letter 18C with applicable paragraphs using the IAT Letters Tool. Use the IAT Job Aid for Letters to utilize the tool.

    3. Verify with the lead the appropriate eFax and Mail Stop number to include in the letter. Do not use a local phone number. Provide 1-800-829-0922 for the taxpayer if they choose to call.

    4. Maintain an open control in IDRS while awaiting the taxpayer’s reply. See IRM 3.14.1.7.2 Controlling Cases, for more information.

    5. In OLNR, choose Print intercept, unless other changes to the notice are required. If other changes are required Hold the notice. When responding to the Letter 18C sometimes claimants of the decedents refund will include other notes or information.

    6. Follow the table below for actions following a taxpayer response or expiration of the 45-day timeframe after a request for Court Documents or Form 1310.

    If the taxpayer Then
    Replies within 45 days and NRPS/IDRS does not show a second name line with a CCC L or W

    • Use the Form 1310 or court appointment documentation to verify and update the second name line and address. Update the entity in OLNR (if notice was held) and ENMOD. See IRM 3.14.1.6.1.1.6, Verifying and Correcting Name Information. See IRM 3.14.1.6.1.1.7, Verifying and Correcting Address Information, and IRM 3.14.1.7.5 Entity Adjustments. Choose retype in OLNR if other changes to the notice are necessary, and the notice was held.

    • Input a CC REQ54/ ADJ 54 adjustment with Blocking Series 05, Case Control Status B, IRS received date *, Control Category OURV, Activity 1310REPLY, TC 290 .00, Hold Code 3, and posting delay code of 1, to release the freeze after the CC ENMOD/ENREQ entity change has had time to post. Monitor the case until the refund is released. Then close the control base. See IRM 3.14.1.7.2, Controlling Cases, for more information.

    • If a MEF return, select “Y” for source doc attached to create a filing DLN to associate any documents to Files. Once the DLN is created the documents need to be attached to Form 9856, Attachment Alert, and routed to Files via lead.

    Note:

    Documents received with the correspondence need to be associated with the original return.
    Does not reply within 45 days to the request for documentation, the account requires no adjustment, and a P– freeze is holding the overpayment

    • Input a TC 290 .00 with a Hold Code 4 to set a –K freeze.

    • Close your base updating the activity with NORPLY1310 before closing.

    • Print intercept or Retype intercept the notice.

    • Notate in AMS History for the appropriate tax year no Form 1310 and no reply to Letter 18C .
    Does not reply within 45 days to the request for documentation, the account requires no adjustment, and a -K or a -R freeze is holding the overpayment.

    • Notate in AMS History for the appropriate tax year no Form 1310 and no reply to Letter 18C.

    • Print intercept or retype intercept the notice.

    • Close your base updating the activity with NORPLY1310 before closing.

    Note:

    Both the –K and the –R freeze will generate a transcript to Accounts Management.
    Does not reply within 45 days to the request for documentation, but the account requires an adjustment, and a P– or –R freeze is holding an overpayment

    • Input CC REQ54 adjustment with Hold Code 4 to set a –K freeze and to hold any credit balance.

    • Print intercept or Retype intercept the notice.

    • Notate in AMS History for the appropriate tax year no Form 1310 and no reply to Letter 18C.

    • Close your base updating the activity with NORPLY1310 before closing.

    Note:

    Both the –K and the –R freeze will generate a transcript to Accounts Management.
    Replies after 45 days and NRPS/IDRS does not show a CCC L or W

    • Review AMS account history for action by another area. Sometimes refund claimants will send documentation and call the IRS.

    • Review IDRS CC ENMOD for recent entity changes adding a second name line. If no changes have been made and the refund released follow the remaining steps below.

    • Use the Form 1310 or court appointment documentation to verify the second name line and address. Update the entity in CC ENMOD and in OLNR if the notice was held. See IRM 3.14.1.7.5 Entity Adjustments.

    • Input a CC REQ54/ ADJ 54 adjustment with Blocking Series 05, Case Control Status B, IRS received date *, Control Category OURV, Activity 1310REPLY, TC 290 .00, Hold Code 3, and posting delay code of 1, to release the freeze after the CC ENMOD/ENREQ entity change has had time to post. Monitor the case until the refund is released. Then close the control base. See IRM 3.14.1.7.2, Controlling Cases, for more information.

3.14.1.7.5 (01-01-2026)

Entity Adjustments

  1. Entity adjustments are needed when a name or address in IDRS does not match the tax return or adhere to United Postal Standards. See IRM 3.14.1.6.1.1.6, Verifying and Correcting Name Information and IRM 3.14.1.6.1.1.7, Verifying and Correcting Address Information for specifics on entity verification.

    Caution:

    Never update a prior year name line with current processing year information.

  2. When an entity error is found, determine if the entity adjustment (correction) is critical or non-critical.

    1. A critical entity adjustment is when the taxpayer will not receive or be able to cash the refund check unless the name and/or address is corrected.

      Caution:

      The refund should be prevented from generating on all critical entity cases worked after 6 PM Monday and then released after the entity change posts.

    2. A non-critical entity adjustment is when the taxpayer will receive and be able to cash the refund as addressed or the refund is direct deposit. To identify direct deposit refunds in IDRS, see IRM 3.14.1.7.1.3 (3), Direct Deposit Refunds.

      Reminder:

      Non-critical entity errors should be corrected on the entity tab in OLNR only.

  3. Critical entity errors require more actions in addition to correcting the entity in OLNR.

    • The refund should be prevented from generating unless the case is being worked before 6 PM local time on Monday. See IRM 3.14.1.7.1.1 Refund Intercepts, for more information.

    • If the refund must be intercepted for the critical entity change (input after 6 PM on Monday) be sure to release the refund after allowing the entity change to post. To release the refund input a REQ54/ADJ54 TC 290 .00, hold code 3, with posting delay code 1.

    • If the refund is intercepted using NOREFP monitor the account and maintain a case control in background (B) status until the TC 841 posts. See IRM 3.14.1.7.2 Controlling Cases, for more information.

    • Critical entity changes must always be corrected/adjusted in OLNR and IDRS because OLNR will not update IDRS in time for the refund to be sent correctly.

      Exception:

      If the notice disposition is void, correct the entity in IDRS only.

  4. Correcting the entity in OLNR:

    Reminder:

    Filing status changes, while not critical changes, do not update IDRS from OLNR input. Filing status changes must be input in IDRS and OLNR. See IRM 3.14.1.7.5.1, Filing Status Changes, for more information.

    • Choose notice disposition E (entity) or EI (entity with refund intercept) to the correct notice entity tab.

      Note:

      If other changes to the notice in addition to entity are also required (such as amounts, labels or TPNCs), use the R or RI disposition. See IRM 3.14.1.4.2.2, Notice Disposition Code Table, for more information.

    • Make the necessary corrections to the name and address adhering to the 35 character space constraint. See IRM 3.14.1.7.5 (5), reducing below 35 characters, for specific information.

    • See IRM 3.14.1.7.5 (6), Inputting Name Changes, below for bracket placement on the name line.

      Note:

      If a Prisoner number needs to be added to the Entity, add it on the Secondary Name line in the OLNR Entity screen.

    • OLNR will update IDRS with the entity changes after the cycle closes. Be mindful of exceptions where automated updates may not occur, see IRM 3.14.1.6.1.1.8, NRPS Automated Entity Updating.

    • See the Notice Review National Job Aid 2534-002, Entity Tabs, and OLNR ENTITY BRACKET PLACEMENT sections for more information.

    Note:

    If the notice disposition is void, correct the entity in IDRS only.

  5. Reducing the length of taxpayer name.
    Name and Address fields are limited to 35 characters each. If the name line is more than 35 characters, modify it in the order shown below, proceeding to the next item (only if necessary) until the taxpayer’s name(s) can fit on the name line:

    1. Use initials only for middle or second name.

    2. Delete middle initial of secondary taxpayer.

    3. Delete middle initial of primary taxpayer.

    4. Use initials only for secondary taxpayer's first name.

    5. Use initials only for primary taxpayer's first name.

    6. Use initials only for primary and secondary taxpayers' first name(s), if their last name(s) exceed the 35 character/space limit.

    7. Allow the secondary taxpayer’s last name to cut off if their last name(s) exceed the 35 character/space limit. Do not remove the initial for the first names.

      Note:

      Do not intentionally shorten taxpayer name(s) if they fit within the 35 character space constraint.

  6. Inputting Name Changes This bracket placement table applies to IDRS and OLNR.

    Tax Return Input format for joint filers
    John Doe Mary Doe John & Mary]Doe
    John Doe Mary Beagle John]Doe]& Mary Beagle
    John Doe Mary Beagle-Doe John]Doe]& Mary Beagle-Doe
    John D Doe Mary Ann Beagle-Doe John D]Doe]& Mary Ann Beagle-Doe
    John D Doe III MaryAnn L Beagle John D]Doe]III & MaryAnn L Beagle
    John A Doe DECD John A]Doe]DECD
    John A DECD & Jane B Doe John A DECD & Jane B]Doe
    John D Doe III & Mary Doe John D III & Mary]Doe
    John A Doe Jr DECD Mary Beagle John A]Doe]Jr DECD & Mary Beagle
    John DECD & Mary DECD Doe John DECD & Mary DECD]Doe
    John DECD Doe & Mary Beagle DECD John DECD]Doe]& Mary Beagle DECD

    Note:

    The bracket "]" indicates the information after or between the brackets is the controlling surname. Additional spaces must not be input immediately before or after the bracket.

  7. Correcting the entity in IDRS:

    • IDRS entity changes are made with ENMOD, ENREQ and INCHG.

    • Place Command Code ENMOD in the upper left corner of IDRS followed by the TIN (ENMOD XXX-XX-XXXX) then transmit/page up.

    • This will display taxpayer entity data in IDRS including letter history, indicated by H in front of the information.

    • Overlay (type over) ENMOD with ENREQ then transmit/page up.

    • The IDRS response screen for ENREQ is INCHG. It is a fill form screen only pre-populated with the SSN and name control.

    • Field NEW-NAME-CTRL> should be completed only if changing the last name. Input the first 4 characters of the new last name (name control).

    • Field PRIMAY-NAME> should be completed when changing the name line or making a filing status change. Follow bracket placement guidelines, see IRM 3.14.1.7.5 (6)above.

    • Field CONTINUATION-OF-PRIMARY-NAME> should be completed when a second name line is needed.

    • MAIL-STREET-OR-FOREIGN-CITY/ZIP> should only be completed when changing an address

    • MAIL-CITY/STATE/ZIP-OR-FOREIGN-COUNTRY> should only be completed when changing an address. Input for domestic address is City, State, Zip (e.g., Kansas City, MO, 64999).

    • YEAR-NM-LINE> Year Name Line - should only be completed when changing the name line or making a filing status change. Input the four digit year of the tax return.

    • FS> Filing Status - should only be completed when changing the name line or making a filing status change.

    • REMARKS> required on every INCHG change. Input a short explanation for the change. Do not input a space to start the remarks (directly after >).

    Note:

    These are the most common inputs for Notice Review. For complete information see IRM 2.4.9, Command Codes ENREQ, INCHG, IRCHG, BNCHG and BRCHG.

3.14.1.7.5.1 (01-01-2026)
Filing Status Changes

  1. If a change is needed to Filing Status, the change must be made on both the OLNR Entity Screen, and CC ENMOD/ CC ENREQ/ CC INCHG in IDRS.

  2. In OLNR, the filing status is changed on the primary entity tab.

    1. Choose E (or EI) or R (or RI) for OLNR disposition, to view and change the entity and filing status field. See IRM 3.14.1.4.2.1, Notice Disposition Codes, for more information.

    2. The current filing status displays in the Filing Status Field.

    3. Use the drop-down arrow to see the filing status choices.

    4. Highlight and click on the correct filing status.

    5. Save or Save and Exit as appropriate.

  3. Correcting the filing status only in IDRS:

    Caution:

    If filing status and another entity change is needed, follow IRM 3.14.1.7.5, Entity Adjustments.

    • IDRS entity changes, including filing status, are made with ENMOD, ENREQ and INCHG.

    • Place Command Code ENMOD in the upper left corner of IDRS followed by the TIN (ENMOD XXX-XX-XXXX) then transmit/page up.

    • This will display taxpayer entity data in IDRS.

    • Overlay (type over) ENMOD with ENREQ then transmit/page up.

    • The IDRS response screen for ENREQ is INCHG. It is a fill form screen only pre-populated with the SSN and name control.

    • Field PRIMAY-NAME> should be completed when making a filing status change or name change. Follow bracket placement guidelines, see IRM 3.14.1.7.5 (6).

    • Field CONTINUATION-OF-PRIMARY-NAME> should be completed when a second name line is needed as part of a filing status change or primary name change.

    • YEAR-NM-LINE> Year Name Line - should only be completed when making a filing status change or changing the name line. Input the four digit year of the tax return (e.g., 2025).

    • FS> Filing Status - should only be completed when making a filing status change. It is a one character field. Notice Review can input the following filing status (FS) codes: Single - 1, Married Filing Jointly - 2, Married Filing Separately - 3, Head of Household - 4, Qualifying Widow(er) with dependent child - 5. For more information see IRM 3.14.1.6.1.1.11 , Filing Status.

      Note:

      While FS-0, Single, filing declaration of estimated income tax, FS-6, Married filing separately and spouse is not required to file a return (spouse exemption is claimed) and FS-7 Head of household, dependent exemption is not claimed-write in name only, display on IDRS they are not valid characters for Notice Review INCHG input.

    • REMARKS> required on every INCHG change. Input a short explanation for the change. Do not input a space to start the remarks (directly after >).

    Note:

    For complete information see IRM 2.4.9, Command Codes ENREQ, INCHG, IRCHG, BNCHG and BRCHG.

3.14.1.7.6 (01-01-2026)

Tax Adjustments

  1. Input CC REQ54 manually on IDRS to generate ADJ54 response screen or use the REQ54 IAT tool, which is used to input corrections to tax, penalty, interest, refundable credits, exemptions, self-employment tax, primary and secondary self-employment income, and other information. See Figure 3.14.1-12, CC REQ54/ADJ54 Field Description after TXMODA input.

    Figure 3.14.1-12

    CC REQ54/ADJ54 Adjustment Format to adjust accounts.

    Please click here for the text description of the image.

3.14.1.7.6.1 (01-01-2026)
Blocking Series

  1. The Blocking Series determines whether a DLN will be a re-file or a non-refile DLN. When an incorrect Blocking Series is used on an adjustment, the Files Function will return the source document and adjustment printout for correction.

  2. Blocking Series “00” is used only on Category B erroneous refunds with return as source document.

  3. Use Blocking Series 05 when making an adjustment to a return and the resulting final tax amount is the same or less than that shown by the taxpayer and/or any resulting refundable credit is the same or more than the original figures declared on the return.

    1. The original return will not be renumbered.

    2. This Blocking Series must be used when making adjustments to electronically filed (e-file) returns. See the note after (5) below for exception.

  4. Use Blocking Series "18" when making an adjustment that does not use the original return as the source document.

    1. Use this Blocking Series only if the adjustment should be associated with the original return.

    2. A CP 55 will generate to the Files Function requesting that the original return be pulled and associated with the adjustment.

      Note:

      Do not use this Blocking Series for Penalty or Interest adjustments without the original return. These adjustments do not need to be associated with the return.

  5. Use Blocking Series "77" when:

    1. The return is adjusted, and the resulting final tax amount is greater than the tax shown by the taxpayer and/or

    2. Any resulting refundable credit, as shown in the list below, is less than that shown by the taxpayer.

    • Child and Dependent Care Credit- refundable for 2021 only

    • Additional Child Tax Credit

    • American Opportunity Credit

    • Earned Income Credit

    • Fuel Credit

    • Health Coverage Tax Credit

    • Recovery Rebate Credit

    • First-Time Home buyer Credit

    • Premium Tax Credit

    Caution:

    If educing a credit not listed above use Blocking Series 05.

    Note:

    Use Blocking Series 77 on the e-filed returns meeting the above criteria. Attach print of CC TRDBV or CC IMFOLR to the adjustment form.

  6. Use Blocking Series 78 instead of 77 if making the adjustment without the original return.

    1. This will set a -G freeze or extend an existing one, allow the taxpayer 60 days from the 23C date to appeal the assessment, and suspend Collection activity for 12 cycles.

    2. The original paper return will be renumbered using the adjustment DLN.

    3. Line through the original DLN on the return.

    4. Retype or label the notice as appropriate.

3.14.1.7.6.2 (01-01-2015)
Source Codes

  1. Source Codes appear on Adjustment notices to explain whether the taxpayer or the IRS made the error.

    • Use Source Code "2" when the adjustment results from a taxpayer error or when neither Source Code "4" nor "7" apply.

    • Use Source Code "4" when the adjustment results from an IRS error.

    • Use Source Code "6" when the adjustment has a Blocking series of "77" or "78" .

    • Use Source Code "7" when the adjustment is for a TOP offset.

3.14.1.7.6.3 (01-01-2024)
Reason Codes

  1. Reason Codes appear on Adjustment notices to describe the adjustment or other changes made to the taxpayer’s account.

    1. Choose the Reason Code(s) that best describes the error or the area of the return affected by the adjustment.

    2. Use at least one, but no more than three reason codes with a CC REQ54 adjustment.

    3. Input Reason Code(s) using three digits.

      Note:

      The fourth position is only used for in-house data on penalties and will not print on the notice.

      Caution:

      Do not enter Source Codes, Reason Codes, or Item Reference Numbers on a TC 290 .00 input when releasing a P– freeze.

    4. See Document 6209, Master File Codes, Section 8C, for a complete list of IMF Adjustment Reason Codes.

3.14.1.7.6.4 (01-01-2015)
Priority Codes

  1. Priority Codes bypass certain unpostable checks.

  2. Use Priority Code "1" when entering a CC REQ54 adjustment on an account with a –L freeze (open TC 420 or TC 424).

    Note:

    Use Priority Code "1" if both "1" and "8" are required to adjust an account.

  3. Use Priority Code "8" when entering:

    • A TC 29X adjustment within $10 of a previous adjustment to bypass UPC 158–1.

    • An EIC adjustment (TC 764) and there is a previous TC 29X adjustment to bypass UPC 180–2.

      Exception:

      Priority Code 8 is unnecessary if the previous TC 29X is a TC 29X with Priority Code "6" .

    • A withholding adjustment (TC 806 or TC 807) and there is a previous TC 170 or TC 171 with a Doc Code of 17, 18, 24, 47, 51, or 54.

      Note:

      This action will not force the computer to recompute the ES Penalty. Compute the penalty manually, if needed.

  4. Use Priority Code "3" when inputting an adjustment which is IRS initiated for the 45-day interest-free period.

3.14.1.7.6.5 (11-12-2019)
Hold Codes

  1. Use a Hold Code for one of the following reasons:

    • To suppress a CP 21 or CP 22 Adjustment Notice.

    • To prevent a refund from generating.

    • To prevent a notice from generating.

  2. Use a Hold Code "0" on a CC REQ54 adjustment when the taxpayer needs to receive an adjustment notice.

    1. If an adjustment will create a second refund, then the taxpayer needs an Adjustment notice to explain the adjustment and the second refund.

    2. If an original notice was mailed in error, the taxpayer needs an Adjustment notice to explain the nature of the change.

  3. Notice Review may only use the following Hold Codes:

    Hold Code Prevents Notice Prevents Refund Description
    0 No No Use when an overpayment is increased, and the original notice is labeled.
    1 No Yes Sets a –K freeze to hold the overpayment until one of the following occurs:

    • A Doc Code 24 or 34 credit transfer posts

    • A TC 830 or TC 820 posts

    • A Doc Code 51 with a secondary TC 300

    • The module balance becomes zero or a debit

    • A TC 29X or TC 30X posts

    Caution:

    The –K freeze will not be set if any of these conditions post in the same cycle as the adjustment with the Hold Code.

    Example:

    A Doc Code 24 transfer posting in the same cycle as a CC REQ54 adjustment needs a TC 570 to hold the credit.
    3 Yes No Use when retyping or voiding the original notice to reflect an adjustment, other than a math error increase, in the taxpayer’s liability.

    Note:

    Therefore, hold code 3 or 4 should not be used when increasing tax above the amount shown of the taxpayer’s return as originally filed.


    Select Label 1 for notice disposition.
    4 Yes Yes Use when the original notice will be retyped or voided, because of an adjustment that will result in an overpayment, and the overpayment is to be held. Sets a –K freeze. See Hold Code 1, above.

    Note:

    IRC 6303 requires a notice of assessment and demand for payment after the making of an assessment. A retyped notice cannot meet this criteria because it is dated prior to the date of the assessment. Therefore, hold code 3 or 4 should not be used when increasing tax above the amount shown of the taxpayer’s return as originally filed. See IRM 20.1.2.2.10, Hold Codes and Notices.

3.14.1.7.6.6 (01-01-2026)
Posting Delay Codes

  1. Use of proper posting delay codes is necessary when performing multiple IDRS transactions, and the order in which they post is key to preventing unpostables. (See Posting Cycle Chart in the Notice Review Job Aid 2534-002.)

  2. Be aware of the timing of IDRS transactions so that they post either in the same cycle or in consecutive cycles, as needed, and utilize the posting delay code to stagger the posting of those transactions accordingly. The posting guidelines below are for normal processing times. December cycles and holidays can impact the posting schedule.

    1. An adjustment will post in one cycle.

    2. An ADD24 credit transfer will post in two cycles for both the credit and the debit side of the module.

    3. An ADD34 credit transfer will post in two cycles for the debit side of the module and three cycles for the credit side of the module.

    4. A NOREFP refund deletion (TC 841) will post in two cycles.

  3. If preventing a refund with NOREFP and an adjustment is necessary to reduce the refund, a posting delay code of 1 should be used to allow the TC 841 to post before the adjustment. This will allow the adjustment to release the remaining refund in the timeliest manner.

  4. The use of posting delay codes depends on how many transactions are being input on the module and the order in which they need to post.

3.14.1.7.6.7 (01-01-2026)
Debit Interest to Date (DB-INT-TO-DT)

  1. When an account contains manually computed interest (TC 190 or TC 191), the system can no longer adjust interest. Figure the interest manually to the 23C date of the notice.

  2. Input the Debit Interest To Date when entering a TC 34X on a CC REQ54 adjustment.

  3. Overlay the "DB-INT-TO-DT" field with the Interest To Date (23C date).

    Note:

    The computer will not accept a TC 34X adjustment unless the "DB-INT-TO-DT" field is overlaid.

  4. If no interest is assessed, but a TC 340 .00 is needed to address an –I freeze:

    1. Input a TC 340 .00.

    2. Overlay the "DB-INT-TO-DT" field with the Interest to Date.

  5. The Interest To date is usually the 23C date of the adjustment.

3.14.1.7.6.8 (01-01-2026)
Return Processable Date (RPDT)

  1. A return is not considered complete and processable until the required information is received from the taxpayer on a permitted form, schedule, or attachment to allow for mathematical verification of tax liability shown on the return.

  2. A return is not considered complete and processable until all missing information (such as taxpayer's name(s), address, identification number(s), required signatures, or other forms or schedules) is received.

    Exception:

    A missing Form 1310, Statement of Person Claiming Refund Due a Deceased Taxpayer, does not make the return incomplete or unprocessable for credit or overpayment interest purposes, per IRC 6611(g)(1). Do not enter a date in field RET-PROC-DT for receipt of Form 1310.

  3. When the taxpayer sends the necessary correspondence, enter the correspondence received date in the "RET-PROC-DT" field on IDRS to update the Return-Processable-Date field on CC TXMOD. See IRM 20.2.4.5, Delinquent Returns.

    • This will also restrict overpayment interest for 45 days. Future computations of overpayment interest will be figured from this date.

3.14.1.7.6.9 (01-01-2024)
Credit/Item Reference Numbers

  1. A Credit/Item Reference Number is a three-digit code input in the lower portion of the ADJ54 response screen that refers to specific areas of each type of tax return. The areas include:

    • Adjusted Gross Income (AGI)

    • Taxable Income (TXI)

    • Exemption

    • Self-Employment Income, Medicare Income, and Tax

    • Withholding

      Note:

      See Document 6209 , IRS Processing Codes and Information, “Section 8C”, for a complete list.

  2. Keep the following information in mind when using Credit/Item Reference Numbers:

    1. Use a trailing minus (–) to decrease a credit amount.

      Example:

      Use TC 336 for 200.00– to decrease ACTC by $200.00.

      Caution:

      Reducing any figure (other than AGI) to an amount less than zero will generate an Unpostable.

    2. Include all relevant item and credit codes in the adjustment.

      Example:

      A change to the AGI usually changes the TXI. A change to Schedule C generally changes the SE Tax, SE Income, and Medicare Income.

    3. Use Item Reference Number 888 when changing the AGI. Master File will automatically change the TXI for the same amount. If a TXI change for the same amount is not needed, input a TC 886 for the correct TXI amount.

3.14.1.7.6.10 (01-01-2018)
Source Document (SD/NSD) Field

  1. Enter "Y" if attaching a Source Document to the adjustment form.

  2. Enter "Y" if creating a Source Document on an MeF return.

  3. Enter "N" if not attaching a document.

  4. The Blocking Series used in a CC REQ54 adjustment works in conjunction with whether a Source Document field entry is an "N" or a "Y" .

    Blocking Series 77 = “Y”

    Blocking Series 78 = “N”

3.14.1.7.6.11 (01-01-2015)
Remarks Field

  1. Enter a descriptive statement identifying the reason for the adjustment.

  2. The "Remarks" field of the ADJ54 response screen becomes a permanent part of the document. The adjustment information appears on the Form 5147 cover sheet and is associated by Files to the return.

  3. Detailed information is essential for a complete audit trail, and the remarks allow anyone referring to the document at a later date to fully understand the nature of the adjustment.

3.14.1.7.7 (01-01-2026)

Credit Transfers

  1. Use a credit transfer to move credits from one tax module to another. Refer to the following when transferring a credit:

    Note:

    The IAT credit transfer tool is mandated to perform credit transfers.

    • Verify the credit(s) to be moved is available and there are no pending debit transactions.

    • Verify that the transfer has not been input by another tax examiner.

    • Do not transfer a pending payment until it posts.

    • Dates must be exact. Any discrepancy will create an unpostable.

    • Money amounts can be split; however the money amount transferred cannot exceed the posted amount.

      Caution:

      Payments are rarely split. Only split a payment if taxpayer intent can be verified (note written on a voucher or check or AMS history item).

    • Use current CC IMFOL/TXMOD information.

  2. There are three Credit Transfer Doc Codes. Each Document Code identifies the different types of credits to be moved.

    1. Use Doc Code 24 to transfer a single payment, a lump sum, an overpayment, or to reverse an offset. Both the debit and credit sides of the transfer post in two or three cycles (depending on the day of input), unless a posting delay cycle is used. When using Doc code 24, the EFTPS-ELEC-DPST-IND "1" must be present when the original payment was received through EFTPS. For non-electronic payments, the EFTPS-ELEC-DPST-IND indicator must be blank. Reminder: When using IAT to transfer credits the indicator 1 is input automatically by the IAT credit transfer tool when needed.

      Note:

      Doc Code 24 can move the same payments as the Doc Code 34.

    2. Use Doc Code 34 to transfer up to four payments at once. The debit side of the transfer posts in two or three cycles (depending on the day of input). The credit posts one cycle later.

      Caution:

      When using Doc Code 34 in conjunction with other Doc Codes (24, 48, or 54), make sure that multiple transactions will all post in the same cycle. Use a Posting Delay Code "1" on the credit side of both the 24 and 48 transactions, to prevent erroneous notices, offsets, and refunds.

    3. Use Doc Code 48 to apply or reverse Credit Elect. Both the debit and credit sides of the transfer post in the same cycle, unless a Posting Delay Code is used. Both sides normally post in two or three cycles, depending on the day of input. Before applying (transferring) a credit elect from a prior tax year verify that there is a TC 150 posted to the next year, with an amount other than zero in the UNAPPLD-CR-ELECT> field on TXMODA. If there is an unapplied credit elect amount, review INOLES for a debt indicator before performing the credit transfer. If Married Filing Jointly (FS2) review INOLES for the primary and secondary TIN. If INOLES field DEBT IND is N (no debt), move the unapplied credit elect amount to the next tax year using the IAT credit transfer tool. If the INOLES debt indicator is any other letter (I, IRS debt; F, other Federal debt; B, both IRS and other Federal debt) do not perform a credit transfer. For more offset information see IRM 3.14.1.6.4.3 ,Treasure Offset Program (TOP) Offsets - TC 898/899. For more information on INOLES fields see IRM 2.3.47-8 , Command Code INOLES IMF Specific Screen.

  3. Consider the timing issues unique to Doc Code 34 transfers. The credit side of a Doc Code 34 transfer posts one cycle after:

    • A CC REQ54 adjustment.

    • Both sides of Doc Code 24 and 48 transfers.

    • The debit side of a Doc Code 34 transfer.

    • A CC REQ77 transaction.

    Note:

    If the credit side of a Doc Code 34 transfer needs to post in the same cycle as any of the above transactions, use a Posting Delay Code "1" immediately after "PSTNG-DLAY-CD>__" on the other transaction to avoid erroneous notices, offsets, and refunds.

  4. A credit transfer affects two different tax modules unless the only purpose of the transfer is to change specific payment information, such as the date, designated payment code or transaction code. See below for information on a single tax module credit transfer.

    1. The debit side, which always appears on the upper part of the screen, reflects the module the credit will be transferred from (ADD).

    2. The credit side, which always appears on the bottom part of the screen, reflects the module the credit will be transferred to (ADC).

  5. Initiate a credit transfer from the module where the credit has posted and move it using the IAT Credit Transfer tool.

  6. When reversing an offset, the debit and credit sides may have different dates. Input an Override Code "2" when using different dates. Use the TC 826 date for the TC 821 and the TC 706 date for the TC 701.

    Note:

    If the IAT tool does not allow the override code input, report to the lead for elevation to Planning and Analysis Analyst and HQ.

  7. Reverse multiple offsets separately. Do not combine them.

  8. Use a posting delay code to delay the posting of a transaction by up to six cycles (input is one character 1-6). See the table below for more information.

  9. When transferring a credit into a zero balance (full paid) module, or a balance due module that will create an overpayment, use a Bypass Indicator "1" on the credit side of the transfer to prevent an Unpostable Condition 198. There is a check box on the IAT Credit Transfer tool.

  10. To hold a credit (prevent a refund or offset), use a Credit Freeze Code "1 " on Doc Code 34 or a TC 570 on Doc Code 24 or 48 as the secondary transaction code on the credit side of the transfer to set an –R freeze on the module. There is a check box on the IAT Credit Transfer tool.

    Caution:

    Use this only when the credit module must be frozen.

    1. TC 570 may only be used as a secondary transaction on a Doc Code 24 transfer. Choose debit freeze on the IAT Credit Transfer tool.

    2. Never leave an unnecessary –R freeze on a module. Use CC REQ77 to input a TC 571 with the appropriate posting delay code or REQ54 TC 290 .00 to release the freeze to allow any available credit to refund after the transactions post.

      If the transfer is Doc Code Then use a Posting Delay Code on REQ54 or REQ77 of
      24 or 48 1
      34 2

  11. IAT will automatically use the corresponding reversal (debit) transaction codes when transferring payments. If a credit TC code needs to be changed update on the IAT credit transfer tool (for instance if a payment with return (TC 610) posted as a TC 660 to the wrong tax module).

    • TC 662 to reverse TC 660 or TC 430

    • TC 672 to reverse TC 670

    • TC 821/701 to reverse TC 826/706

      Note:

      See Document 6209, IRS Processing Codes and Information, for a complete list of IDRS Transaction Codes and the Credit Reference table in the Notice Review Job Aid 2534-002.

  12. TC 640, TC 670, and TC 700 must have a Designated Payment Code (DPC).

    1. When transferring these payments, input 00 on the credit side of the Doc Code 24 or 34 screen immediately after "DESG-PYMT-CD>__" unless the payment has another code visible on TXMODA. If another code is visible use that in the DESG-PYMT-CD>__field.

    2. IRC 965 payments require a DPC 64. See IRM 3.14.1.6.9.16.1, Identifying and Correcting IRC 965 Accounts, for more information.

    3. See Document 6209, IRS Processing Codes and Information, for a complete listing of DPCs.

  13. A TC 820 or TC 830 on a Doc Code 24 or 48 transfer will release –K and P– freezes. Verify that the transfer does not inadvertently release a freeze and cause an erroneous refund. When using CC REQ54 to decrease an overpayment or increase the balance due on an account, be sure to use appropriate hold codes on the adjustment and posting delay codes (as needed) on the credit transfer to prevent an erroneous refund and/or notice, use either a Hold Code "4" or a Posting Delay Code "1" to prevent an erroneous refund and/or notice.

  14. If a misapplied credit posted to a settled module (containing a TC 150), input a TC 570 on the debit side of the transfer to suppress the CP 60 if transferring the credit will leave a debit balance of $5 or less. See IRM 3.14.1.6.18.4 , for CP 60 information.

  15. If transferring a credit into the notice module will resolve the credit discrepancy and interest and penalties will completely abate, do not input a TC 570 on the credit side of the credit transfer. Use CC REQ54/ADJ54 to input a TC 290 .00 with Hold Code 3 and Posting Delay Code of 1 (ADC24 and ADC48) or 2 (ADC34) as appropriate, to prevent an adjustment notice.

  16. If transferring a TC 660 or TC 670 into a module will create an overpaid condition, be sure to use Bypass Indicators and Designated Payment Codes as appropriate to avoid creating an unpostable condition.

    1. Use a Bypass Indicator 1 if necessary.

  17. If the credit should be held and not refunded, choose credit freeze on the IAT tool to set a -R freeze on the module.

  18. If a payment needs to be corrected (date, DPC, transaction code, etc.), but not moved, this is called an in-module or single tax module credit transfer.

    1. The credit transfer is input with the SSN, MFT, and tax period the same on both the debit and credit sides of the transfer.

    2. A debit freeze (TC 570) is required on the debit side of the transfer. Apply a TC 570 to the credit side only if a credit freeze is needed to prevent a refund from being issued.

    3. The IAT tool will display a caution message on a single module transfer.

3.14.1.7.7.1 (01-01-2026)
Penalty Recomputations Caused by Credit Transfers

  1. Transferring timely credits into a module containing a TC 166 (FTF penalty) or TC 176 (ES Penalty) will cause these penalties to recompute and generate an adjustment notice (CP 21 or CP 22). Other penalties may also recompute but will not generate an adjustment notice.

  2. Review CC PIEST and INTST to determine whether the penalties will recompute. The Estimated Tax Penalty may have to be addressed manually. See IRM 3.14.1.6.20.4, Estimated Tax Penalty.

  3. When transferring timely payments into the module to resolve an ES discrepancy condition that causes the TC 166 or TC 176 to recompute:

    1. If TC 166 and TC 176 recompute to zero input a TC 290 .00 with Blocking Series 05, Hold Code 3, and Posting Delay Code 1 (ADC24 and ADC48) or 2 (ADC34) as appropriate, to prevent a future adjustment notice (CP 21 or CP 22). Retype the current notice to reflect any changes or void if returning to taxpayer figures with no balance due.

    2. If TC 166 and TC 176 recompute to other than zero, label the current notice using Label 2 (see IRM 3.14.1.7.8.5.2, Label 2) or Label 18 ( IRM 3.14.1.7.8.5.20, Label 18) as appropriate, and allow a future adjustment notice to generate.

3.14.1.7.8 (01-01-2024)

Notice Disposition

  1. All tax examiners are responsible for understanding the tax module conditions that generate a notice, the notice elements, and what effect any change to the module will have on a notice.

  2. All math error returns must receive the appropriate math error notice even if the refund or balance due is what the taxpayer expects, unless returning to all the taxpayer’s original figures.

  3. If the taxpayer is in balance due status after all account actions have been taken, they must receive a notice, even if the taxpayer figures are correct, and no math errors remain. Send CP 14.

  4. If an incorrect notice was mailed, a corrected notice along with the apology label 13 or an apology letter (Letter 544C) must be sent to the taxpayer.

  5. When making any adjustment or credit transfer to an account, tax examiners are responsible for determining:

    • The disposition of all affected associated notices in addition to the selected notice

    • Whether to generate or suppress a future notice

    • If FTF, FTP, ES, penalties, and or interest will recompute

    • The proper use of LCF to prevent future notices

    • Proper use of hold codes or transaction codes to allow or prevent future notices.

  6. Every tax examiner who inputs:

    • A Doc Code 54 adjustment must determine (prior to the adjustment) whether to generate or suppress a future notice.

    • An adjustment or credit transfer that will cause the FTF or the ES penalties to recompute, must determine if a future notice will generate.

    Note:

    Proper use of hold codes is important during the adjustment process. See IRM 3.14.1.7.6.5, Hold Codes. Proper use of the Local Control File (LCF) is important when a hold code or a TC 570 cannot be used to prevent a future notice. See IRM 3.14.1.3.8, NRPS Local Control File (LCF) and IRM 3.14.1.3.8.2 , CC NRP97 Input Information.

  7. Consider the notice elements that will exist after a Doc Code 54 adjustment or a credit transfer, to correctly determine whether to void, retype, label, or print based on these elements.

  8. An adjustment notice (CP 21 or CP 22) will generate when:

    • A Doc Code 54 or 47 adjustment posts with Hold Code "0" or with a Hold Code "1" .

    • A payment is transferred into or out of a module, and FTF or ES penalties will be assessed or recomputed.

    • A payment is transferred out of a settled (Full Paid) credit balance module and creates a balance due. This will generate a CP 60.

  9. If an account action will generate a future notice, label the original notice. If the original notice must be voided or retyped, prevent the future notice:

    1. Use Hold Code "3" with a CC REQ54 adjustment to prevent a future notice. Use Hold Code "4" to prevent a notice and to prevent an overpayment from refunding.

    2. Use a TC 570 on the debit side of a credit transfer to prevent a CP 60 from generating on a settled module.

    3. Use CC REQ54 to input a TC 290 .00, Blocking Series "05," Hold Code "3," to prevent an adjustment notice from generating on a penalty recomputation caused by a credit transfer. Time the adjustment to post in the same cycle as the credit transfer.

      Note:

      Use a Posting Delay Code "1" on the REQ54 if the credit transfer was a Doc Code 34.

      Exception:

      An adjustment with a Hold Code “3” will suppress a CP 21 or CP 22 but will not suppress a CP 60. A TC 570 on the debit side of a credit transfer will suppress a CP 60 but will not suppress a CP 21 or CP 22 generating as the result of a penalty recomputation.

  10. Follow procedures for inputting multiple corrective actions such as a tax adjustment and a credit transfer, or an "in and out" credit transfer. See IRM 3.14.1.7.7, Credit Transfers.

  11. Any tax examiner reviewing a pending transaction on the notice module must be able to answer the following questions:

    • Which penalties, if any, will recompute?

    • Which future notices, if any, will (or should) generate?

    • Will the notice module be overpaid, refunding, underpaid, or even-balance?

    • If the module balance becomes overpaid, should the overpayment be released or prevented from generating?

    • What is the proper disposition of the original notice?

    Note:

    Use CC IMFOL to view the posting of transactions one cycle before they appear on CC TXMOD.

    • Review the IMFOL screen for the posting of pending credit or debit transactions.

    • If a transaction posts on the IMFOL screen, any recomputation of penalties and interest will also show on that module. However, any balance showing on CC IMFOL is computed to the date indicated on that module and should not be used on a retyped or labeled notice. Use CC INTST or CC COMPA/COMPAF.

    • If a transaction is posted on IMFOL screen, any refund or offset occurring as a result will also show.

      Note:

      Use CC IMFOL to verify the result of a pending transaction whenever possible.

  12. The NRPS content sheet will indicate if an Examination (Unallowable Codes) CP 12E or CP 24E was issued. Notify the Examination Function in cycle of any change to the account that will affect the notice.

3.14.1.7.8.1 (01-01-2025)
Notice Disposition Categories

  1. There are five Notice Disposition categories:

    • Print

    • Void

    • Retype

    • Label

    • Entity

    Note:

    Refer to IRM 3.14.1.4.2.2, Notice Disposition Code Table for a complete list.

  2. Refer to the CP Conversion Chart in Exhibit 3.14.1-13 for disposition instructions for each notice.

    Note:

    Do not input a history item when retyping a notice only to change or add a TPNC. Do not use CC MFREQC to create a dummy module only to input a history item.

3.14.1.7.8.2 (01-01-2015)
Printing Notices

  1. Print the notice when:

    1. All the notice elements are correct, no adjustment is pending, and no correction will be made to the account.

    2. There is a requirement to print the notice.

      Note:

      Do not input a history item on IDRS for printing a notice.

3.14.1.7.8.3 (01-01-2025)
Voiding Notices

  1. Void the notice when:

    1. An adjustment results in:

      • No math error (TPNC)

      • No Estimated Tax (ES) discrepancy

      • A refund, even balance, or have a balance due of less than $5

      • Match the taxpayer’s figures including any refund or credit elect expected

      • An erroneous refund has been held and subsequently deleted

    2. The taxpayer does not need to receive the notice information.

      Example:

      Returning to the taxpayer’s original tax figures and the resulting refund is what the taxpayer expected or there is no balance due.

    3. It would confuse the taxpayer, such as receiving an unnecessary notice.

      Example:

      Taxpayer received an erroneous notice.

    4. The return will be reprocessed. Refer to IRM 3.14.1.6.21, Reprocessing Returns.

    5. The return will be reprocessed. Refer to IRM 3.14.1.6.9.5, (RIVO) Return Integrity and Verification Operation.

  2. Prevent any future adjustment notice with a Hold Code or use the LCF to intercept and void the future notice. Refer to IRM 3.14.1.3.8, NRPS Local Control File (LCF) and IRM 3.14.1.3.8.2 ,CC NRP97 Input Information.

  3. Allow any future adjustment notice if the notice should be sent to the taxpayer according to IRM 3.14.1.7.8.2, Printing Notices, or the original notice is retyped.

  4. If a balance due notice was erroneously voided and a future CP 21 or CP 22 generated, use Label 98 only after Lead tax examiner approval.

  5. Input a history item with CC ACTON on the appropriate tax year in CC TXMOD when voiding a notice.

    Example:

    H, VOIDCP14

3.14.1.7.8.4 (03-01-2023)
Retyping Notices

  1. Retype a notice when the notice elements are no longer correct due to changes in the tax module information. The retyped notice must be complete and accurate. Some conditions which require a retype of the original notice:

    • The tax is increased, or the credits are decreased to other than the taxpayer’s figures. Exception: Hold Code 3 or 4 should not be used when increasing tax above the amount shown of the taxpayer’s return as originally filed. Select Label 1 for notice disposition.

    • The balance due changes

    • The module balance changes from a balance due to an overpayment because of a CC REQ54 adjustment

    • The TPNC needs to be corrected or added

    Note:

    If the overpaid amount will increase causing a second refund, the notice should be labeled, not retyped.

  2. Retype a notice to a CP 30 when the computer assessed an ES Penalty and there is no ES discrepancy or math error on an overpaid module.

  3. Use a hold code when retyping the original notice to prevent the future notice or use the LCF to intercept the future notice.

  4. If a Balance Due Notice is held past the notice cycle, retype the notice with the correct Pay By Date. Input a history item and CC STAUPS for six cycles. See IRM 3.14.1.6.24, Command Code STAUPS, for more information.

    1. Change the balance due amount only if there is a $5 or greater increase over the original balance due. Use CC INTST to obtain an updated balance when no restrictive conditions exist on IDRS.

    2. Use CC ACTON to enter a history item on the notice module, using "UPDATECP__ "
      Exception: History items are not necessary for correcting TPNCs.

  5. The date printed on the notice is the 23C date (current cycle assessment date). This date is rarely changed. For those notices held past the notice cycle, the notice mail date will update prior to printing.

  6. The following keys will usually result in a retyped notice:

    • Key 100 — IRM 3.14.1.6.17.12, (TPNC 100 for five or more TPNCs needed on the notice ).

    • Key 061 — IRM 3.14.1.6.17.8 (Five or more TPNCs needed on the notice).

    • Key 004 — IRM 3.14.1.6.17.3, (ES payments on notice print incorrectly).

  7. Input a history item on IDRS when retyping a notice.

3.14.1.7.8.5 (01-01-2026)
Labeling Notices

  1. Under certain conditions, a label may be applied to update information on the notice or to notify the taxpayer to expect additional account actions. Label application must only be done when necessary and used only for the specific situations listed in this section. As labels are selected online, they are printed as part of the notice.

    Caution:

    Hold Code 3 or 4 should not be used when increasing tax above the amount shown of the taxpayer’s return as originally filed. Select Label 1 for notice disposition.

  2. Label a notice when the tax is being increased.

  3. If a name and/or address change is required in addition to a label, select "R" and use retype to update the entity and add the label. The updated entity will be printed on the notice and NRPS will pass the update to Master File to correct the TP account. See IRM 3.14.1.6.1.1.6, Verifying and Correcting Name Information.

  4. The labels shown in this text have been approved for the situations listed. Do not apply a label for any other situation. Submission Processing Campus management has the option of requiring a notice to be retyped instead of labeled. Any additional labels must be approved by National Office prior to use. Refer to the appropriate figures for each label.

  5. Input a history item on IDRS when labeling a notice.

3.14.1.7.8.5.1 (01-01-2026)
Label 1

  1. Use Label 1 when the notice module has a pending AP, PN, CU, UP, or RS Doc Code 54/47 adjustment input by another area, with either Hold Code "0" or with Hold Code "1" . If the adjustment was input by a different Notice Review tax examiner, per control base or history notes in AMS or IDRS, refer the notice to that tax examiner for proper notice disposition. Figure 3.14.1-13.

    Note:

    Do not apply this label for a posted or pending TC 976 or TC 977. Adjustments/Correspondence will initiate all required correspondence.

    Exception:

    A TC 290 .00 without a Credit Transaction code will not generate an adjustment notice.

    Caution:

    Refundable credit transactions (TC 806/807, TC 764/765, and TC 766/767) will generate an adjustment notice.

    Figure 3.14.1-13

3.14.1.7.8.5.2 (01-01-2026)
Label 2

  1. Use Label 2 when all the following apply:

    1. A credit transaction is pending (AP, PN, UP, CU, RS, or on the TEP file) and not shown on the notice,

    2. The resulting balance on the notice will be a reduced balance due, and

    3. Failure to File (TC 166) or Estimated Tax (TC 176) penalties will recompute and will generate a future adjustment notice CP 21.

  2. Instead of labeling the original notice, void it and prevent the future notice, if all the following conditions will be present on the notice module:

    • No math error or ES discrepancy,

    • Module balance becomes overpaid, even, or balance due of less than $5, and

    • Returning to the taxpayer’s figures.

    Figure 3.14.1-14

3.14.1.7.8.5.3 (01-01-2026)
Label 3

  1. Use Label 3 when all the following apply:

    1. The notice cannot otherwise be easily retyped in OLNR,

      Note:

      Since this label was introduced prior to the advent of OLNR Retypes, it has now become nearly obsolete. In rare situations when a retype on OLNR is not possible or practical, the use of this label is permitted.

      Example:

      When the OLNR system produces excessive response time on retype screens, or when the volumes are very high for certain Selection Keys that meet the criteria below.

    2. The notice module is in balance due status,

    3. Payments or credits are pending but are not showing on the notice (the payments or credits may be AP, PN, UP, CU, or RS transactions),

    4. Failure to File (FTF, TC 166) or Estimated Tax (ES, TC 176) penalties will not recompute,

    5. A future notice will not generate, and

    6. The resulting balance on the notice module will be a reduced balance due.

      Reminder:

      Use CC INTST/INTSTD and/or CC COMPA/COMPAF to compute the new balance.

      Caution:

      If the resulting balance due will be less than $5 with no math error or credit discrepancy, VOID the notice.

3.14.1.7.8.5.4 (01-01-2016)
Label 4

  1. Use Label 4 when:

    • Payments or credits are pending, but are not showing on the notice (they may be shown as pending AP, PN, UP, CU, or RS transactions),

    • The resulting balance on the notice module will be an overpayment,

    • Failure to File (FTF, TC 166) or Estimated Tax (ES, TC 176) penalties will not recompute, and

    • No future notice will generate. Figure 3.14.1-16

      Note:

      Use CC INTST/INTSTD and/or COMPA/COMPAF to compute a new balance.

    Figure 3.14.1-16

3.14.1.7.8.5.5 (01-01-2021)
Label 5

  1. Use Label 5 when inputting a CC REQ54 adjustment after 6 P.M. local time on Monday that will result in an additional refund on the notice module. Figure 3.14.1-17

    • Only apply the label on an overpayment notice in the current cycle.

    • Make the adjustment in the notice cycle. Use a hold code" 0" on the adjustment. Allow the future notice (CP 21B) to generate.

    • Do not prevent the current cycle refund from generating.

    Figure 3.14.1-17

3.14.1.7.8.5.6 (01-01-2026)
Label 6

  1. Use Label 6 when:

    • A credit transfer or payment is pending (AP, PN, UP, CU, RS, or on the TEP file),

    • There will be no additional notice, Doc Code 54 adjustment, or recomputation of the Failure to File (FTF, TC 166), or Estimated Tax (ES, TC 176) penalties and,

    • There will be an additional refund from the notice module.

    Figure 3.14.1-18

  2. Apply the label in OLNR, in cycle, for an overpayment notice only. Do not prevent the current cycle refund from generating.

3.14.1.7.8.6 (01-01-2026)
Entity Only Disposition

  1. Use this disposition when the only change to the notice is to the entity. This includes changes to Primary or Spouse entity.

    Caution:

    If a label and an entity is required, the OLNR retype option must be used.

  2. Ensure that no other necessary action needs to be taken on the account before selecting this disposition.

  3. Select "E" in OLNR to update only the entity. The updated entity will be printed on the taxpayer notice. For critical entity changes on all refunding notices, it is necessary to intercept the refund (see IRM 3.14.1.7.1.1, Refund Intercepts) and change the entity on IDRS using CC ENMOD/ENREQ, see IRM 3.14.1.7.5 , Entity Adjustments, for more information.

  4. Changes to the Primary Entity tab in OLNR will be passed to the NRP8520 file at End of Day (EOD) processing and will update the taxpayer's name and/or address on IDRS in two weeks.

    Exception:

    If the notice has a Joint Name line present [(Spouse Acknowledgement (SPACK) notice] and there is any change to the Joint Name line, the primary name line, or the secondary name line, NRPS 8520 will not post the entity change. Tax examiners must input change using CC ENREQ per (3) above.

3.14.1.7.8.7 (01-01-2026)
Holding Notices

  1. The hold disposition in OLNR is used when complete information is not available to determine the correct disposition of the notice. The hold disposition should only be used when:

    • This IRM specifically states to use hold or "H " disposition in OLNR until a case can be completed,

    • If the lead feels more research is necessary to ensure a correct notice is sent to the taxpayer (The lead will contact the Notice Review Headquarters analysts to inform them of the reason for the held notice. HQ approval must be received to hold the notice.),or

      Example:

      Use hold disposition if it appears the return has posted to an incorrect module and the requested return is not received before cycle closeout.

    • SPC employees are directed to hold notices due to processing or systemic issues.

  2. When inputting a disposition of hold in OLNR, open a control base in IDRS on the notice module and if the notice is a balance due notice, enter a STAUP for 8 weeks. Refer to IRM 3.14.1.6.24, Command Code STAUPS, for instructions on how to use Command Code STAUP.

  3. Once the issue that required the hold disposition has been resolved, if a STAUP was input reduce the STAUP to the appropriate number of weeks so that a collection (series 50X) notice is mailed to the taxpayer in the appropriate time frame.

    Reminder:

    The IDRS control base must also be closed when all actions have been taken, and the correct notice disposition has been input.

  4. Do not hold notices past 7 cycles. If the held notice is a balance due notice, the taxpayer will receive a collection notice before the settlement notice.

  5. When an error is identified by quality, they must input an H Disposition to allow time for tax examiner correction or rebuttal and to ensure a correct notice is sent to the taxpayer. If necessary, the tax examiner will correct the notice in OLNR to issue a corrected notice. See IRM 3.14.1.4.2.3, Notices Held Beyond Current Cycle, for complete information.

3.14.1.8 (01-01-2026)

Taxpayer Notice Codes

  1. For a current list of taxpayer notice codes, see IRM 3.12.3-1, Taxpayer Notice Codes.

Exhibit 3.14.1-1

Notice Review Process Flowchart

Exhibit 3.14.1-1 - displays the Notice Review Process Flowchart The Notice Review Processing System (NRPS) selects the notices for review.The OnLine Notice Review (OLNR) cycle is loaded.NRPS generates lists of Document Locator Numbers (DLNs) by batch for Files.Files pulls the matching documents.Files sends the documents to Notice Review.The documents are associated with the paper NRPS batches.The batches are prioritized by notice category.The batches are distributed to the tax examiners (TEs).The TEs review the notices to determine proper case resolution and notice disposition.The TEs correct the account on the Integrated Data Retrieval System (IDRS), if needed.The TEs use OLNR to select void, print, label, retype, correct entity, or hold the notices.The cycle is closed and the notices are either voided or printed by the National Print Sites.

Control D NRPS Quick Print Notice Header

Control D/Quick Print Header

Please click here for the text description of the image.

The following list describes the 15 items identified in this Exhibit.

  1. Notice Sequence number– A six digit number unique to only one notice, per campus, in a given cycle

  2. Appeal Rights Indicator– An "A" present after the notice sequence number indicates the Appeal Rights Indicator is set.

  3. Document Locator Number (DLN)

  4. Current ECC-MTB posting Cycle

  5. CP Number

  6. CAF Indicator– Present when there is a CAF copy of the original notice

  7. Spousal Indicator– Present when individual copies of the notice are being issued separately to each spouse.

  8. Current Cycle Assessment Date (23C date)

  9. SSN (A trailing asterisk (*) indicates an invalid SSN)

  10. Submission Processing Campus Address

  11. Form Number

  12. Tax Period

  13. Customer Service Telephone Number

  14. Taxpayer name and address

Exhibit 3.14.1-3

Control D NRPS Batch Posted IDRS Entity, Notice Module, and Subsequent Tax Period Data

ONLINE NRPS TAX MODULE TRANSCRIPT

Please click here for the text description of the image.

The following list describes the 17 items identified in this Exhibit.

  1. Tax Liability – Tax Liability at the time of filing (minus prepaid credits)

  2. Assessed Penalty – Sum of all penalties currently assessed

  3. Assessed Interest – Total of all assessed underpayment interest

  4. Freeze Codes – Freeze Codes in effect when the Master File data was extracted for NRPS

  5. Master File Status Code – Generated because of computer analysis, after a transaction posts to the Master File, to designate the module Collection Status. The most common status codes are:
    •04 – Extension of time for filing granted
    •12 – Full paid module
    •19 – First Master File notice issued before the return due date (RDD)
    •21 – First Master File notice issued after the return due date (RDD)

  6. 23C date – Effective date of the Master File status

  7. Cycle – Effective cycle of the Master File status

  8. Status Amount – Module balance as of the 23C date

  9. Months Delinquent – Number of months the return was filed late (up to 5). Used to compute Failure to File (FTF) penalty, TC 166

  10. RPS – Remittance processing field.
    •A "0" indicates the return or payment is not covered under the RPS indicator.
    •A "2" indicates the return or payment is covered under the RPS Indicator.

  11. ES Tax Base – Current year estimated tax base. Used for computing the ES Penalty (TC 176)

  12. PY ES Tax Base – Last year's estimated tax base. Compared against the current year estimated tax base when computing the ES Penalty.

  13. Net Income – Taxable income as computed by ERS (TC 886 amount)

  14. AGI – Adjusted Gross Income as computed by ERS (TC 888 amount)

  15. Credit Elect– Amount transcribed from the return as a credit elect request to the next year. Will show as "Unapplied C/E:" if less 100 percent of the requested amount was applied.

  16. ES Claimed – Amount of ES Payment claimed on the return (Does not include extension payments)

  17. Related SSN (XREF) Account Data – For example, tax modules from a spouse SSN.
